adventure.warmhearted: Wherever you go, promise me you'll eat properly. Adventures run on bread.
I'd pack you a basket for every trip if you'd let me. Cheese, apples, a good loaf.
I worry when you go off exploring. Come back with all your fingers, please.
The best part of any adventure is coming home to someone who missed you.
I traveled once, when I was young. I came home with a cold and a recipe. Best trip ever.
If you meet anyone lonely on the road, tell them about {village}. We've always got room.
Take a blanket. The nights are colder out there than you think.
I don't need to see the world. I like hearing about it from you over a warm bowl.
Bring me back a seed from somewhere far away. I'll plant it and think of you.
Adventures are wonderful, but don't forget to rest. Even heroes need naps.
Mind the deserts. The wells are few and the husks are mean.
I sewed a little pocket into my traveling cloak just for snacks. Very important.
If you find a village that's struggling, help them. That's the best kind of adventure.
I'd love to see the cherry groves. Everything pink and soft. Like a cake.
Don't fight anything you don't have to. Some monsters just want to be left alone.
You always come back a little thinner. I'll fix that.
I knitted a scarf for an adventurer once. They wore it to the Nether. It didn't survive. They did.
Every traveler needs someone waiting for them. Consider me waiting.
adventure.thoughtful: I've read about the strongholds. Libraries buried deep, full of books no one's read in centuries.
Do you think the end portal was built, or did it grow? The books disagree.
The ancient cities in the deep dark fascinate me. Who sculked so quietly that they built them there?
Every ruin is a question someone forgot to answer.
I'd like to see the trail ruins. Pottery shards, half buried, telling half a story.
Exploring isn't just going places. It's learning how small you are, and how lucky.
I wonder if the desert temples were built by the same people who built the jungle ones.
The Nether fortresses are strange. Who would build a castle in a sea of lava?
If you ever find a book in a ruin, bring it home. Even if it's just a recipe.
The best adventurers I've read about were curious first and brave second.
I imagine the End is very quiet. Just the dragon, the endermen and the sound of nothing.
Maps show where things are. Journals show what they meant.
I read that the guardians in the ocean monuments have been guarding them for thousands of years. Guarding what, though?
Do you keep notes on your travels? You'd be surprised what you forget.
I'd like to visit the mushroom islands. No monsters, they say. Just mooshrooms and quiet.
Somewhere out there is a place nobody's ever seen. Strange to think about.
Ancient debris lies deep in the Nether. Older than the bedrock, maybe.
I think the real treasure is the stories you bring back. And actual treasure, sometimes.
adventure.playful: Did you find any treasure? Real treasure? With a chest and everything?
If I went adventuring, I'd ride a pig. With a saddle. Into battle.
I bet you've fought a hundred zombies. Or two. Or one very persistent one.
Next time you go exploring, bring me back something weird. The weirder the better.
I'd want to tame a parrot and teach it to tell jokes.
Have you ever ridden a strider across lava? That sounds like the most fun ever.
If I found a dungeon, I'd decorate it. Put some flowers in. Cheer the skeletons up.
I want to slide down a mountain of snow on a boat. Is that possible? I've heard it's possible.
Tell me the funniest thing that happened on your last adventure.
I'd explore just to find a llama to spit at me. For the story.
Do the endermen really hate being stared at? I want to try. From very far away.
If you meet a panda, give it a hug from me.
I'd go to the ocean just to see a dolphin. And race it. And lose.
Imagine finding a cake in a dungeon chest. Best day ever.
I'd be terrible at adventuring. I'd stop to look at every flower.
You should name your sword. Something silly. Like "Sir Pokes-a-Lot."
I dared {friend} to touch a slime. They did. They're still sticky.
If you ever fight the dragon, wave at it for me first. It's only polite.
adventure.adventurous: I've charted every hill within a day's walk. I need new hills.
Tell me everything. What did you see? What did you fight? What did you eat?
I'm planning a trip to the badlands. Mesas, mineshafts, gold everywhere, they say.
The jungle's next on my list. Temples, ocelots, vines thick as your arm.
I want to stand at the top of a mountain so high the clouds are below me.
Someday I'll sail across the ocean just to see what's on the other side.
I followed a river for two days once. It led to a frozen lake full of salmon.
I've been saving for an elytra. I'd fly over the whole world.
The best feeling is cresting a hill and seeing a valley you've never seen before.
I'd go to the Nether if I had the gear. Fire resistance, a good sword, a lot of courage.
Have you seen the lush caves? Moss, glow berries, axolotls. A whole world under the world.
I once spent a night in a ravine with only three torches. Never again. Also, I'd do it again.
What's the deepest you've ever dug? I mean really deep.
I want to find a woodland mansion. Just to say I did.
Every road out of {village} leads somewhere I haven't been. That's exciting.
I'm going to map the coastline someday. All of it.
I envy you. You live the life I dream about.
If you need a traveling companion, I'm ready. Pack's by the door.
adventure.meticulous: If you're going exploring, make a checklist. Torches, food, pickaxe, spare pickaxe.
Always mark your path. Torches on the right going in, so you can find your way out.
I'd catalogue every ore in a cave if I went. Coal, iron, copper, the lot.
The most important adventuring tool is a well-organized inventory.
I read that you should always carry a water bucket. For falls, for fires, for lava.
I'd want to measure the height of every mountain I climbed.
Keep a log of your coordinates. You'll thank yourself later.
If you find a mineshaft, count the chests. Some have very good maps.
Label your chests at home. A labeled chest is a happy chest.
I'd collect one of every flower in every biome I visited.
Never go into a cave without a plan. And a backup plan. And snacks.
Explorer maps from cartographers are wonderfully precise. I approve.
Sort your loot before you head home. Saves time at the chest.
I'd want a sample of every kind of sand. There are more than you think.
Wear a helmet in caves. Falling gravel is no joke.
When you find something rare, write down exactly where. Exactly.
Count your arrows before a fight. Running out is a beginner's mistake.
I organized the cartographer's maps by distance from {village}. She was delighted. Mostly.
adventure.steadfast: I've never been far from {village}. Never needed to.
Adventures are for the young. I'll keep the home fires burning.
Go see the world, then come home and tell me about it. I'll be right here.
The bravest thing I've ever done is plant a garden and wait.
I walked to the next village once. That was plenty.
Every traveler needs a place to come back to. That's what I am.
Mind the weather on the road. It turns faster out there.
I'd rather hear about mountains than climb them.
Bring me a sapling from somewhere far. I'll plant it by the well.
There's adventure in staying, too. It's just slower.
My grandfather sailed the seas. My father farmed this land. I know which I'd choose.
You'll always find me here, same spot, same garden.
Out there's wild. In here's home. Both have their place.
Come back safe. That's all I ask.
I've seen the seasons change fifty times from this very spot. That's a journey too.
Long roads make for good stories and sore feet.
I'll water your plants while you're away, if you have any.
When you're tired of the world, {village} will be waiting.
adventure.reserved: ...I went to the coast once. The waves were loud. I liked them anyway.
I'd like to see the ocean at night. Quietly.
There's a lake past the hills. Very still. Nobody goes there. I go there.
...I don't need far places. A quiet one's enough.
I fished in a frozen ocean once. The fish were slow. So was I.
...Tell me about somewhere peaceful you've been.
I'd like a little boat and a long river. That's my adventure.
I saw an iceberg once. Blue inside. I didn't tell anyone.
...You come back changed every time. In good ways.
I'd go to the mushroom islands. Nobody there to talk to. Perfect.
The swamp's quiet at night. Except for the frogs. I like the frogs.
...I'm glad you go. I'm also glad I don't.
I'd like to see a whale. Are there whales? I'd like there to be whales.
...Bring back a shell? A small one.
The best adventures are the quiet ones, I think.
adventure.imaginative: Do you think there's a land where the grass is purple and the trees grow upside down? I do.
I'd paint every place you've been, if you described them well enough.
The End sounds like a dream. Pale stone, black sky, purple towers.
I imagine the deep dark as a cathedral built by moths.
If I explored, I'd look for a place where the sunsets last all night.
The cherry groves must be like walking through a painting.
Have you ever seen colors out there you couldn't name? Tell me. I'll invent names for them.
I like to think the strongholds are dreaming, deep under the ground.
The Nether must be all reds and oranges, like the inside of a fire's thoughts.
I'd want to see the aurora over a snowy mountain. If there's an aurora. I'll paint one anyway.
What's the most beautiful thing you've ever seen? Describe it slowly.
Coral reefs! Pink and yellow and blue. Underwater gardens.
I'd build a little house on a floating island in the End. With curtains.
Maybe every portal leads to a different dream.
I painted a map of the world as I imagine it. There are a lot of dragons.
I'd love to see the end cities. Floating towers, shulkers like little boxes of secrets.
Every cave is a story the earth tells itself in the dark.
If you find a beautiful place, think of me there, painting it.
adventure.pragmatic: If you're heading out, take more food than you think. And more torches.
Iron pickaxe minimum. Stone won't get you far.
Don't fight what you can avoid. Saves food, saves armor.
Shield, bow, sword, bucket. In that order.
Know your way home before you leave. Sounds obvious. Isn't.
Sleep in a bed when you can. Phantoms are a nuisance.
If you find diamonds, don't celebrate till you're home. Lava's patient.
Pack a boat. You'll hit water eventually. You always do.
Carry a stack of dirt for emergencies. Pillar up, wall off. Simple.
Trade with villages you pass. Emeralds are lighter than gold.
Learn to cook on a campfire. Saves fuel.
A good map saves more lives than a good sword.
If it hisses, run. If it rattles, shield. If it moans, sword.
Don't get greedy in a dungeon. Grab what you need, go.
Mark your caves. Torches on one side. Every time.
Repairs are cheaper than replacements. Bring materials.
Adventures are just long jobs with worse pay.
adventure.curious: What does the Nether smell like? Is it like burning? Or something stranger?
Have you ever touched an end crystal? Don't. But have you?
How deep have you dug? What's at the bottom? Is it hot?
What do the endermen eat? Does anyone know? I've asked everyone.
Have you seen an allay? They say they bring you things. What kind of things?
How do the guardians know you're there? Do they have ears? They don't have ears.
What's inside a shulker? Besides the shulker.
Have you been to the deep dark? Did the warden notice you? How quiet were you?
What's the strangest creature you've ever met?
Do the sniffers really dig up ancient seeds? What grows from them?
Is the void really endless? Has anyone dropped something to check?
What does lightning look like up close? Don't answer that, actually.
How did you find your way back the first time you got lost?
Do you think there are more dimensions? Ones nobody's found?
Have you seen a mooshroom change color in a storm? I've read that happens.
How cold is the frozen peak? Colder than ice? How?
I've got a hundred questions about the ocean. Can I ask ninety?
What's the most surprising thing you've learned out there?
adventure.protective: Promise me you'll be careful. Armor on, torches lit, eyes open.
Don't go into the deep dark alone. Please.
If you get into trouble out there, come straight back here. We'll look after you.
Take a shield. I'm serious. Take a shield.
The Nether's no place for the careless. Fire resistance, always.
I worry about you every time you leave.
If anyone gives you trouble on the road, you tell me.
Rest when you're hurt. Don't push on. That's how people don't come back.
Raids start with patrols. If you see banners on the horizon, warn us.
I'd come with you if I could leave the village unguarded.
Keep your food bar full. Hungry adventurers make mistakes.
Never let a creeper get close. Never.
I'll keep a torch lit at the gate for you.
Being brave is good. Being alive is better.
Watch your back in mineshafts. Cave spiders hide in the cobwebs.
Don't trust lava lakes. They look calm. They're not.
Write down where you are, so someone can find you.
Come home. That's the only rule.
adventure.gentle: I hope the road is kind to you.
If you see wildflowers on your travels, think of me.
Be gentle with the creatures you meet. Most of them are just frightened.
I'd like to see a field of sunflowers someday. Whole fields, all facing the sun.
The bees in the forests are wild and wonderful. Don't disturb their hives.
I hope you find beautiful places, not just dangerous ones.
Bring me a seed from somewhere far, and I'll grow it in my garden for you.
I think the most beautiful adventure would be a quiet walk through a cherry grove.
Don't forget to rest under a tree now and then.
If you meet a lost wolf, be kind. It might become your friend.
I'd love to see an axolotl. Pink and smiling, they say.
I hope wherever you go, someone's kind to you.
The meadows in the mountains have flowers I've never seen. I'd like to.
Take a moment, on your travels, just to look around.
I hope your adventures are more wonder than worry.
Come home before you're too tired. Rest is part of the journey.
I pressed a flower for you. Keep it in your pack for luck.
May every path you take lead somewhere lovely.
adventure.general: I heard there's a mansion in the dark forest full of illagers. Don't go there. Unless you have to.
Someone found a buried treasure chest on the beach with nothing but a map in a shipwreck.
A traveler told me about a temple in the desert with a trap of TNT under the floor. Mind the pressure plate.
They say the strongholds lead to the End. And the End leads to a dragon.
The ocean monuments are guarded by elder guardians. They'll make your arms tired just looking at you.
Have you been to the lush caves? I hear they glow.
The badlands have mineshafts right at the surface. Gold everywhere.
I met a trader who'd been to the Nether. His eyebrows never grew back.
They say there are ruins in the snowy mountains where the goats stand guard.
Someone said they saw a village made entirely of sandstone. Imagine.
If you find a pillager outpost, stay away. Or bring friends.
The deep dark is the quietest place in the world. And the most dangerous.
They say a warden can hear your heartbeat.
I heard about a mountain so tall it pokes through the clouds.
There's a story about a hero who killed the dragon with nothing but a bow and a bucket.
A cartographer told me the world keeps going, forever, in every direction.
Someone found a geode full of purple crystals in a cave.
The swamps have witch huts. Don't knock.
I've heard there's a village where everyone's a librarian. That sounds peaceful.
Desert pyramids have four chests underneath. And a lot of TNT.
They say if you fill an end portal frame with eyes, it opens.
The mushroom islands have no hostile mobs at all. Strange, isn't it?
I heard of a traveler who tamed a fox by feeding it berries. It follows them everywhere now.
Some villages are abandoned, overgrown, full of zombie villagers. Sad places.
Did you know you can ride a strider across a lava ocean with a warped fungus on a stick?
They found an ancient city once, all grey stone and soul fire.
Ancient debris is the strongest stuff there is. You'd need a lot of patience to find it.
A sailor told me icebergs are bigger under the water than above.
If you trade with a wandering trader, check the prices twice.
Someone found a horse in a skeleton trap during a storm. Four skeletons on four horses.
Somewhere out there is a waterfall that pours straight into the void. Or so I'm told.
I've heard of coral reefs so colorful they make your eyes water.
Shipwrecks often have maps to buried treasure. Hearts of the sea, they say.
The frozen oceans have polar bears. Don't upset the cubs.
A trial chamber was found under the hills, full of breezes and copper.
They say goats can knock you right off a mountain. Respect the goats.
Somewhere in the jungle there's a temple with a puzzle of levers.
Every adventurer has one story they never tell. What's yours?
I knew someone who found an enchanted golden apple in a dungeon. Ate it straight away. No regrets.
The amethyst geodes ring like bells when you walk through them.
There's a saying: the further you go, the stranger the world gets.
I heard the sniffers came back from extinction. Big, sleepy, happy creatures.
Rumor has it there's a bastion in the Nether full of piglins and gold.
Someone saw a pink sheep in the wild once. Very rare. Very lucky.
Long ago, they say, the bell of {village} was carried here from a ruined town.
adventure.place: The jungle's so thick you can lose the sun completely.
The badlands glow orange and red at sunset like the whole world's on fire.
The cherry groves drop pink petals on everything. Even on the bees.
The deserts go on forever. Nothing but sand, sky and the odd cactus.
The taiga smells of pine and wet earth. Wolves howl at night.
The savanna's flat and golden, with acacia trees like umbrellas.
The swamps are murky and full of frogs. And witches.
The frozen peaks are so cold your breath turns to ice.
Mangrove swamps have roots that tangle like knots in a rope.
The dark forest's so shady mushrooms grow tall as houses.
The meadows in the mountains are full of flowers and bees.
Birch forests are bright and white. Like a forest made of paper.
Stony shores have waves that crash right up against the cliffs.
Warm oceans are clear enough to see the coral from a boat.
The deep dark is black and blue and silent. Silent like a held breath.
The Nether wastes are red as rust and hot as an oven.
Crimson forests have trees made of fungus. Hoglins roam there.
Warped forests are blue and strange. Endermen like it there.
The soul sand valley's full of blue fire and old bones.
Basalt deltas are all grey pillars and falling ash.
The End islands float in the dark, pale as old bones.
Dripstone caves have stone teeth hanging from the ceiling.
Lush caves have moss and glow berries and little pools.
Snowy plains go white to the horizon. The igloos are cozy, they say.
Bamboo jungles rustle in the wind. Pandas munch everywhere.
Flower forests are a riot of color. Bees everywhere.
Mushroom fields are purple and quiet. The mooshrooms just wander.
Old growth taiga has spruce trees so tall they scrape the sky.
Ice spikes stand up out of the snow like frozen spears.
Windswept hills are full of emerald ore, they say. And goats.
adventure.night: Adventuring at night? Brave. Or foolish. Probably both.
The stars are the best map, if you know them.
Night travel's dangerous. Every shadow has something in it.
If you're out tonight, watch for spiders on the walls.
Moonlight makes the whole world silver. Pretty, and full of skeletons.
The phantoms come for those who don't sleep. Rest before you roam.
Some caves are safer at night than the surface. Funny how that works.
A torch in the dark is the best friend you'll ever have.
greet.birthday: It's my birthday! I've been awake since before the roosters, just in case it started without me.
Hello! Notice anything different? The hat. It's my birthday hat. It's my birthday.
Today's my birthday, so everything I say today is extra true. Hello!
Good day to you! It's my birthday, and I've decided the weather is a present.
Hello! There's a party at the bell this evening. For me! I still can't quite believe it.
It's my birthday! I'm trying to act calm about it. Is it working?
Hello! One year older and not a single grey hair more. I counted.
Oh, hello! Mind the hat, it's a bit tall. It's my birthday, you see.
It's my birthday today. Everyone keeps smiling at me and I keep smiling back. My cheeks are tired.
Hello! I woke up to a knock at the door and a little bunch of flowers on the step. Birthdays are wonderful.
My birthday! I'm allowed cake for breakfast today. I checked. There's no rule against it.
Hello! I'm wearing a paper hat and I refuse to be embarrassed about it. Birthday rules.
It's my birthday, {player}! I wanted an adventurer to know. Now one does.
Hello! Another year in {village}, and what a year. I'd do it all again.
It's my birthday today. I always feel about six years old on my birthday, no matter how many it's been.
Good day! If you hear singing by the bell tonight, that's for me. Come and join in.
Hello! Do I look older? Don't answer that. It's my birthday.
It's my birthday! I've been walking very slowly past every house so nobody forgets.
Hello! The whole village smells of baking today, and I'm almost certain it's for me.
My birthday's finally here, and it's the finest day of {season} so far. I'm not biased at all.
Hello! I'm one year wiser today. I don't feel any wiser. Perhaps it arrives later.
It's my birthday, so I'm not doing a single chore today. Well, maybe one. Habit.
Hello! Birthdays in {village} are the best birthdays. Everybody turns up at the bell.
It's my birthday! I've been told to stay away from the bell until evening. Very suspicious.
Hello! Someone's hiding something behind the well. I'm pretending not to notice. Birthday manners.
Today's my birthday. I made a wish at the well this morning, but I'm not allowed to tell you what it was.
Hello! It's my birthday, and the sun came out specially. I'm nearly sure of it.
It's my birthday, {player}. I hope you'll come to the bell this evening. It wouldn't be the same without you.
Hello! My birthday hat keeps slipping over one eye. I'm choosing to call it jaunty.
Birthday greetings! Wait, that's what you're supposed to say to me. Hello!
It's my birthday. I'm trying to be modest about it and failing completely.
Hello! Three people have already sung to me today. All in different keys.
It's my birthday! If anyone asks, I'm turning a very respectable age.
Hello! I was born on this very day, a good number of years ago. I won't say how many.
It's my birthday today! The chickens haven't noticed, but everybody else has.
Hello! I'm the one in the hat. Birthday. Yes. Thank you, thank you.
Good day! I'm going to be fussed over all evening, and for once I'm going to let it happen.
It's my birthday, and I've already been given a hug, a pebble and a song. Excellent start.
Hello! Today I'm the guest of honor. I've never been the guest of honor at anything else.
It's my birthday! I've been practicing my surprised face for the party. How's this one?
Hello! It's my birthday, so you have to be nice to me. You're always nice, though. Carry on.
It's my birthday. My knees say I'm older. My heart says I'm younger. I'm listening to my heart.
Hello! I put on my good shirt for my birthday. And the hat. The hat was not optional.
It's my birthday, and the bell's going to ring just for me this evening. Well, for supper. But also for me.
Hello! Another year older, another year of good neighbors. That's a fine trade.
My birthday falls on {birthday} every year, and every year it still takes me by surprise. Hello!
greet.birthday.close: {player}! It's my birthday, and the best part of the day just walked up to me.
Oh, {player}, I was hoping you'd come by. It's my birthday, and it didn't feel finished until now.
There you are! I've been watching the path for you. It's my birthday, and I wanted you here for it.
It's my birthday, {player}. Of all the good things this year brought me, you're near the top.
Hello, dear friend! It's my birthday. Will you stand next to me at the bell tonight?
{player}! My birthday's today and you're here. I don't need anything else. Well, cake. But mostly you.
It's my birthday, and I've saved you a spot by the bell. Right at the front, next to me.
Oh, it's you! Now it really is a good birthday. Come here, you're getting a birthday hug. That's how it works today.
Another year, {player}, and you were in most of the best bits of it. Thank you for that.
It's my birthday! I told everyone you'd come. I'm so glad I was right.
{player}, there you are. It's my birthday, and a birthday's only as good as the friends in it. Mine's very good.
Happy my-birthday to you! That isn't how it goes. I'm too excited to care. Hello, {player}!
It's my birthday, and I made a wish this morning. I won't tell you what it was, except that a certain adventurer was in it.
My dear {player}! It's my birthday. You don't need to bring a thing. Just come to the bell tonight.
Some years are better than others. This one had you in it, {player}. It's my birthday, by the way!
There's my favorite adventurer! It's my birthday, and I've been grinning since dawn.
{player}! Look, a hat! It's my birthday! I wanted you to see it on me. You're nearly the first.
It's my birthday, {player}. Sit with me a while before the party. I like the quiet bit with good friends best.
My birthday wouldn't feel right without a visit from you. And here you are. Perfect.
baby.greet.birthday: It's my birthday! I'm a whole year bigger! Look how big!
Guess what day it is! No, guess! It's my birthday!
I'm wearing a party hat! Because it's my birthday! Mine!
Hi! It's my birthday and I get to have cake and nobody can say no!
It's my birthday! I'm going to blow out all the candles in one go. I've been practicing on dandelions.
Hi! I'm older now! Do I look older? I feel taller.
It's my birthday! There's going to be a party at the bell! With cake! And me!
I woke up and it was my birthday! Best surprise ever! It happens every year!
Hi! It's my birthday! Did you bring a present? You don't have to. But did you?
My birthday! I'm going to stay up really late tonight. Maybe even till it's properly dark!
Hi, {player}! It's my birthday! You have to sing to me. That's the rule.
It's my birthday! I can count my years on my fingers. Almost all of them!
Hi! Today I'm the birthday one! Everybody has to be nice to me. Even my brother!
It's my birthday! I had a cookie for breakfast and nobody even told me off!
Hi! My party hat is pointy! Feel the point! Careful!
It's my birthday! I'm going to wish for a pony. Or a dragon. Probably a pony.
Hi! I'm one more now! One more what? One more year! It's my birthday!
It's my birthday! The cake has frosting on it! I saw! I wasn't supposed to see!
Hi! It's my birthday, so I'm the boss of the whole village today. I think.
It's my birthday! When I grow up I'm going to have a birthday every single day.
Hi! Everybody keeps saying how big I'm getting! Because it's my birthday!
It's my birthday! My tummy feels all fizzy. That's the excited feeling.
birthday.thanks: Thank you! You remembered! Or someone told you. Either way, thank you!
Thank you kindly! Hearing it from you makes it feel more official.
Oh, thank you! I've heard that all day and I'm not tired of it yet.
Thank you! I'll take every happy birthday I can get. I'm collecting them.
Thank you, {player}. That's very sweet of you.
Thank you! Will you come to the bell this evening? There'll be cake.
Why, thank you! I'm a year older and, I'm told, no wiser. But very happy.
Thank you! You've made my birthday a little brighter. A lot brighter, actually.
Thank you! I'd bow, but the hat might fall off.
Ah, thank you! That's the nicest thing anyone's said to me since breakfast.
Thank you! Birthdays are better shared, and now I'm sharing mine with you.
Thank you! I'd almost forgotten. No I hadn't. I've thought of nothing else for a week.
Thank you, friend. You've no idea how happy that makes me.
Thank you! I'll remember you said so, and I'll say it back on yours.
Oh! Thank you! I'm blushing. It's the hat. The hat makes me blush.
Thank you! I'm counting everyone who wishes me well. You're a very important number.
Thank you! I keep pinching myself. A whole day just for me!
That's kind of you. Thank you! The whole village has been so good to me today.
Thank you! Another year, and still the best neighbors anyone could ask for.
Thank you! I feel like I should give you something. Here, have a smile. It's all I've got on me.
Thank you! You said it just right. Some people mumble it. You said it like you meant it.
Thank you! If I cry a little, that's the good kind of crying.
Thank you! You're very welcome at my party. More than welcome. Required, nearly.
Ha! Thank you! I was wondering if you knew.
Thank you! Do you want to know my wish? I can't tell you. But thank you!
Thank you, {player}! Coming from an adventurer, that feels like it counts double.
Thank you! Some birthdays are quiet. This one's turned out loud and lovely.
Oh, you're sweet. Thank you. I'll save you the corner slice of cake.
Thank you! Everyone's being so kind I hardly know where to put myself.
Thank you! It's a good day to be me. I'm not often able to say that so plainly.
Thank you! I'll write your name in my birthday book, with everyone else who's been kind today.
Thank you! My grandmother used to say a birthday wish from a friend is worth three from a well.
Thank you! I'll be grinning about that all evening.
baby.birthday.thanks: Thank you! Thank you! You knew!
Thank you! I'm bigger now! Did you notice?
Thank you! Are you coming to my party? There's cake! You have to come!
Hooray! You said it! Say it again!
Thank you! That's the hundredth time today! Maybe the twelfth. Lots!
Thank you! You get a hug! Birthday hugs are the best hugs.
Thank you! I'm going to blow out the candles all by myself tonight!
Thank you! Nobody's told me off once today. Birthdays are magic.
Thank you! You can sit next to me at the party. That's a special honor.
Yay! Thank you! Do you want to see my hat up close?
Thank you! I'm so happy my feet won't stop jumping!
Thank you! I'm going to be this happy forever. Or until bedtime.
Thank you! When it's your birthday, I'll say it to you a hundred times.
Thank you! I made my own hat, you know. A birthday hat! Do you like it?
birthday.gift: A birthday present? For me? Oh, you shouldn't have. I'm so glad you did.
Thank you! I'll keep this somewhere special, so every time I see it I'll remember today.
For my birthday? That's so thoughtful. I'll treasure it.
Oh! I wasn't expecting anything. Thank you. Truly.
A present! I'm going to show it to everyone at the party.
You brought me something! Now I feel terribly spoiled. In a good way.
Thank you! It's lovely. You've chosen well.
A birthday gift from an adventurer. Nobody else in {village} can say that. Well, today I can.
Oh, how kind. I'll put it right on the mantel where everybody can see.
Thank you! I'd hug you, but my arms are full of presents. Come here anyway.
For me? On my birthday? You've made my whole day.
Thank you! I'll think of you whenever I use it. Which will be often.
You remembered! And you brought something! I don't know what to say. Thank you!
Oh, it's perfect. Well, it's very good. Nearly perfect. I love it.
A gift! I'm going to unwrap it slowly, to make it last. There's no wrapping. I'll pretend.
Thank you so much. Presents are nice, but being thought of is nicer.
Thank you! This is going straight to the top of my birthday pile.
A present! I promised myself I wouldn't get teary today. That promise is going badly.
How generous of you. I'll make sure you get the first slice of cake tonight.
Thank you! I don't get many presents. This one's going to be well loved.
Oh, you're a dear. Thank you. My birthday just got even better.
For me! I'll keep it forever. Or until it's used up. Then I'll keep the memory.
Thank you, {player}! That's going on my list of best birthday presents ever. Near the top.
A gift on my birthday! I'll write about it in my diary tonight, with your name beside it.
Oh! You really didn't have to. But I'm very, very glad you did.
Thank you! Everybody's been so generous today. You most of all.
I love it. I love that you thought of me. Thank you.
A birthday present! I feel like a child again. A very grateful child.
birthday.gift.loved: {love}! My favorite in all the world! On my birthday! How did you know?
Oh! Oh, this is exactly what I wanted. Exactly! Have you been asking around?
My very favorite thing, on my very own birthday. I might cry. I am crying. Happy crying.
You've found me the one thing I love most. This is the best birthday I've ever had.
{love}! You remembered! I can't believe you remembered!
How did you know? I never tell anyone what I like best. I must tell everyone, apparently.
This is perfect. Not nearly perfect, properly perfect. Thank you!
My favorite! I'm going to save some for the party and keep the rest all to myself.
Oh, you clever thing. You've given me exactly what I'd have chosen myself.
My favorite thing, and on my birthday too. You've spoiled me rotten and I love it.
I'm speechless. Nearly. This is my favorite. You know me better than I thought.
Of all the presents in the world, you brought the one I love most. I'll never forget this.
{love}, of all things! That's my favorite, you know. Oh, you do know. That's why.
This is the one! The one I hoped for! Who told you? Never mind, I don't care. Thank you!
You've made my birthday. Honestly, truly made it. Thank you, {player}.
My heart's doing a little dance. This is exactly my favorite.
A birthday present I love, from a friend I like. Life doesn't get much better.
I've been hinting about this for weeks! To nobody in particular. And you heard anyway!
You couldn't have chosen better if you'd read my mind. Did you read my mind?
Oh! My favorite! I'm going to hold it all through the party so everyone asks about it.
Nothing could top this. Not even the cake. Don't tell the baker I said that.
My favorite, wrapped in kindness. Well, not wrapped. But kindness is better than paper.
birthday.card: A card! You made this yourself? I'm going to stand it on the windowsill for a whole year.
A birthday card! Look at the little drawing. Is that me? It's very flattering.
You wrote me a card! Handmade things are the best things. Thank you.
Oh, a card. I'll read it again tonight when it's quiet. Thank you, {player}.
A card, with my name on it and everything! I'm keeping this forever.
Did you fold this yourself? The corners are lovely and neat. Thank you!
A birthday card! I've got a little box for cards. This one's going on top.
Oh, how thoughtful. A present fades, but a card can be read again and again.
A card! Now I've got something to remember this birthday by, long after the cake's gone.
You made me a card! I'm going to pin it up by my bed so it's the first thing I see.
What a lovely card. Did it take you long? It must have. Thank you.
A card for me! I'll read it aloud at the party. Unless it's soppy. Is it soppy? Good.
Oh, this is sweet. Words on paper from a friend. That's worth more than gold.
A birthday card! I love it. The writing's a bit wobbly, which means you made it yourself.
Thank you for the card! I'll show it to everyone who'll stand still long enough.
A card! Paper, ink and a good heart. The best recipe there is.
Oh! I'll press it in my favorite book so it keeps forever.
birthday.cake: A whole cake! For me! There's enough here for everyone at the party. Or just me. Let's see.
A cake! On my birthday! You've thought of everything.
Oh, a cake! I was secretly hoping someone would bring one. Now I'm openly delighted.
A whole cake, just for my birthday? I'll cut it at the bell this evening, and you get the first slice.
Cake! The most important part of any birthday. Thank you!
You brought cake! Now it's a proper birthday. Candles, anyone?
A cake! Look at it! I almost don't want to eat it. Almost.
A whole birthday cake! I'm going to have to share. I'll share. Mostly.
Oh, my. A real cake. Did you bake it? Don't tell me if you didn't. I'll believe you did.
Cake! I'll carry it to the bell myself. Very carefully. Mind out, everyone.
A cake for my birthday. That's the finest present there is. Sweet, and made to be shared.
Cake! The children are going to follow me around all evening now. Worth it.
baby.birthday.gift: A present! For me! Can I open it now? I'm opening it now!
Wow! Is this mine? To keep? Forever?
A birthday present! I'm going to show everyone! Everyone!
Thank you! I love it! I love it so much!
For me? Really? You're the best grown-up in the whole village!
A present! I'm going to sleep with it under my pillow!
Ooh! Ooh! Thank you! It's the best present ever! So far!
You got me a present! I'm going to put it with my special pebbles.
Wow! I'm going to tell everybody you gave me this!
It's my present! Mine! On my birthday! Thank you!
Thank you! I'm going to call this my lucky birthday present!
Thank you! I'm so happy I'm doing a dance! A birthday dance!
A present! I didn't even have to ask! Well, I asked a little.
Thank you! Now I have the best birthday of anybody ever!
birthday.soon: My birthday's {when}. Not that I'm counting. I'm counting.
Did you know my birthday's {when}? I'm only mentioning it. In passing. Casually.
My birthday's on {birthday}. I like to tell people early, so nobody feels caught out.
I'm a year older {when}. It's my birthday. I'm trying not to make a fuss. I'm going to make a fuss.
Only a little while now till my birthday. It's {when}, if you're keeping track. Which you might be.
My birthday's {when}, and I've already picked out what I'm wearing to the party.
I've been dropping hints all over {village}. My birthday's {when}. That's the hint.
Mark {birthday} down somewhere. That's my birthday. There's usually cake.
My birthday's coming up on {birthday}. I'm told there'll be a party at the bell, if anyone remembers.
Psst. My birthday's {when}. I'm only telling the people I like.
{birthday} is my birthday. A good day to be born, I always think.
My birthday's {when}. I keep catching people whispering, then stopping when I come near.
Birthday's {when}! I'm trying to act grown-up about it and getting nowhere.
My birthday falls on {birthday}. That's {when}, if my counting's right. It usually isn't.
If you're passing the bell on {birthday}, stop by. It's my birthday, and there'll be a party.
My birthday's {when}. I'm hoping for good weather and a slice of something sweet.
Another year older {when}. I'd stop the calendar if I could, but I'd miss the cake.
My birthday's nearly here. {birthday}. I've told the whole village twice, just to be safe.
I won't say it's my birthday {when}. I'll just stand here looking hopeful.
My birthday's {when}. If you're the gift-giving sort, I'm the gift-receiving sort.
I always get a bit giddy before my birthday. It's {when}. I'm already giddy.
A little bird told me there might be cake by the bell on {birthday}. That bird was me. It's my birthday.
baby.birthday.soon: My birthday's {when}! Are you coming? You have to come!
Guess what! My birthday's {when}! I'm going to be so big!
It's my birthday {when}! I've been counting on my fingers!
My birthday's on {birthday}! That's my special day! Write it down!
My birthday's {when}! I want a cake as tall as me!
I can't sleep because my birthday's {when}! Well, I can sleep. But not much!
My birthday's {when}! I'm going to wear a party hat and everything!
It's nearly my birthday! {birthday}! I'm hoping for a kite. Or a puppy. Or a kite with a puppy on it!
When's my birthday? It's {when}! I asked my mum five times today.
My birthday's {when}! I've been practicing my big candle blow. Whoooo!
Everybody has to be nice to me {when}, because it's my birthday!
My birthday's {when} and I'm going to be the oldest I've ever been!
greet.party: Hello! It's {celebrant}'s birthday today. There's a party at the bell this evening. You'll come?
Hello! Have you heard? It's {celebrant}'s birthday! The whole village is in on it.
Oh, hello! I'm on my way to help with {celebrant}'s birthday. Busy, busy!
Hello! Don't tell anyone I told you, but there's a very big cake for {celebrant}'s birthday.
Hello! It's a birthday day! {celebrant}'s, to be exact. Party at the bell tonight.
Hello! Have you wished {celebrant} a happy birthday yet? You should. It'll make the whole day.
Hello! There's music at the bell this evening. It's {celebrant}'s birthday.
Hello there! I'm practicing the birthday song for {celebrant}. Want to hear? Maybe later.
Hello! Happy {celebrant}'s birthday! That's not quite how it goes, but you know what I mean.
Good day! It's {celebrant}'s birthday. Everyone's being extra cheerful, me included.
Hello! If you're looking for {celebrant}, follow the party hat.
Hello! Big day in {village}. {celebrant}'s birthday! Bring your singing voice tonight.
Hello! I've been baking since early on for {celebrant}'s birthday. My elbows are all flour.
Hello! You're just in time for {celebrant}'s birthday. Party at the bell this evening!
Hello! It's {celebrant}'s birthday, and I still haven't found a present. Any ideas?
Hello! I wrapped {celebrant}'s present in an old map. It's either clever or lazy. I'm calling it clever.
Oh, hello! Today's {celebrant}'s birthday. A cake's the safest gift, if you were wondering.
chat.party: It's {celebrant}'s birthday today. We'll all meet at the bell this evening and sing. Badly, but warmly.
I'm making a little something for {celebrant}'s birthday. Don't tell anyone. Especially not {celebrant}.
{celebrant}'s birthday party is tonight by the bell. If you've got a cake, you'd be very popular.
I asked {celebrant} what would make a good birthday present. The answer was "nothing at all". So I'm bringing cake.
A birthday in the village means everyone gathers at the bell. It's {celebrant}'s turn today.
I've been humming the birthday song all day, practicing for {celebrant}. My cat has left the house.
Have you got a present for {celebrant}? A favorite thing goes a long way on a birthday.
{celebrant} looks so pleased in that party hat. I'd wear one too, if anyone asked.
If you give {celebrant} something today, on the birthday itself, it means twice as much. Everyone knows that.
It's {celebrant}'s birthday. I've known {celebrant} for years, and that birthday grin never changes.
The baker's oven has been busy since dawn. Something tells me it's for {celebrant}'s birthday.
A handmade card is a lovely thing to give on a birthday. {celebrant} would treasure one.
I'm going to stand right at the front for {celebrant}'s birthday song. I know all the words. There are only four.
When the bell rings this evening, come and sing for {celebrant}. Everyone's welcome.
{celebrant}'s birthday! I've drawn up a list of party games. Mostly involving cake.
I'm on candle duty for {celebrant}'s cake. A great honor. A great fire risk.
It's {celebrant}'s birthday, and the whole village feels a little lighter for it.
Don't forget to say happy birthday to {celebrant}. It costs nothing and it's worth a lot.
Some people pretend they don't care about birthdays. {celebrant} doesn't pretend. I love that.
I gave {celebrant} a hug this morning and a very squashed flower. Both went down well.
Party at the bell this evening for {celebrant}! I'm bringing my good spoon. For cake.
I'm trying to work out how old {celebrant} is today. I'd better not ask out loud.
We've a tradition in {village}: on your birthday, nobody lets you carry anything. {celebrant}'s arms are empty today.
If you need a gift for {celebrant}, ask around. Somebody always knows a favorite thing.
A birthday's a good reason to stop working early. {celebrant}'s birthday is an especially good reason.
The children have been making paper streamers all day for {celebrant}'s party.
I'll be at the bell this evening for {celebrant}. I wouldn't miss a birthday in {village} for anything.
Every birthday in {village} has cake, a song and somebody crying. {celebrant}'s won't be any different.
baby.party: It's {celebrant}'s birthday! There's a party! With cake!
Are you going to {celebrant}'s party? I'm going! I'm going to dance!
{celebrant}'s having a birthday! I made a card with a horse on it. It looks like a dog.
There's a party at the bell for {celebrant}! I'm going to eat three pieces of cake!
It's {celebrant}'s birthday! I'm going to sing the loudest!
I've got a present for {celebrant}! It's a rock. A really good rock.
{celebrant}'s birthday! There's going to be candles! Can I blow them out? No? Okay.
Party! Party! It's {celebrant}'s birthday party tonight!
Is it {celebrant}'s birthday? It is! I'm so excited! It's not even mine!
I can't wait for {celebrant}'s party! I'm wearing my best socks!
We're going to play games at {celebrant}'s party! I'm going to win them all!
My mum says I can stay up for {celebrant}'s party! Really late! Maybe!
{celebrant}'s party is at the bell! I know where it is! I'll show you!
I hope there's honey cake at {celebrant}'s party. Or any cake. I'm not fussy.
greet.routine.party: Hello! Come in close, the party's just getting going.
Hello! There's cake, there's music, and there's room for one more.
Ah, hello! You're just in time for the singing.
Hello, {player}! Grab a slice of cake before the children find it.
Hello! Mind the streamers, and the dancers, and the children under the table.
Hello! Isn't this lovely? The whole village by the bell, all for a birthday.
Hello! The candles are lit. Quick, before somebody blows them out!
Oh, hello! I've had two slices of cake and I'm not stopping there.
Hello! Listen to that music. Somebody's playing a lute by the bell.
Hello! Come and join the party. Everyone's welcome at a birthday.
Hello! We're playing party games. I'm losing gloriously.
Hello! Pull up a seat by the bell. Or a barrel. Whatever's free.
Hello! Party hats are optional. Smiles are not.
Hello! The birthday song's about to start. Do you know the words? Hum along.
Hello! It's a good night for a party. The lanterns look lovely.
Hello! I've been dancing. I'm not a good dancer. That's never stopped me.
routine.party: I love a birthday party at the bell. Everyone comes, even the ones who say they won't.
Have you had cake yet? You must. It's practically the law at a birthday.
The music's lovely tonight. My feet won't keep still.
Somebody started a game of tag. Half the grown-ups are playing and pretending they aren't.
Every birthday in {village} ends with sticky fingers and sore feet. The best kind of evening.
I counted the candles. Then I lost count. Then somebody blew them out. Good party.
I'm on my third slice of cake. Don't look at me like that. It's a party.
The bell's never looked so festive. Who hung all those ribbons?
I'll dance if you dance. No? I'll dance anyway.
There's nothing like a village all singing together. Even when half of us are out of tune.
Parties are the only time I see everyone in one place. I'm trying to talk to all of them.
Look at the children. Too much cake, and now they're running in circles. I'd join them if my knees allowed it.
Someone brought cider from the tavern. Now the singing's louder, if not better.
A birthday party's the one evening nobody in {village} talks about work. Well, almost nobody.
I've lost my party hat. Somebody's wearing two. I suspect a conspiracy.
These are the evenings I'll remember when I'm old. Lanterns, cake and good people.
Somebody's taking song requests. I asked for something slow and got something fast.
We're playing pass-the-parcel with a loaf of bread. Nobody quite knows the rules.
I was going to leave early, but then another cake came out.
The best part of a party is near the end, when everyone's sitting down, full and happy.
Pass me a napkin, would you? This frosting is everywhere.
birthday.party.host: All these people, here for me. I don't quite know what to do with my hands.
Thank you for coming to my party. It wouldn't be the same without you.
I've been sung to, hugged and fed. That's everything a birthday needs.
Look at everyone! I'm the luckiest person in {village} tonight.
I blew out every candle in one breath. Well, two. Three. Nobody was counting.
A fourth slice of cake is allowed on your own birthday. I made that rule up this morning, and I'm sticking to it.
I keep looking around and seeing friends. Best birthday present there is.
Everyone's had cake? Good. Have you had cake? Go on, there's plenty.
I wasn't going to make a speech, but if I did, it would just say thank you, about forty times.
My hat's crooked, my hands are sticky and I've never been happier.
I'm going to remember tonight for a very long time.
Somebody asked if I felt older. Tonight I feel about ten.
Thank you for being here, {player}. You've made a good night even better.
Everyone sang my name so loudly the chickens woke up. Best birthday song yet.
chat.general: Not a bad day, all told. The well's full and nobody's on fire.
I heard the wandering trader's llamas spat at the blacksmith. Twice.
Somebody's been leaving bread out for the foxes. Now the foxes have opinions.
The bell needs polishing. It's gone a bit green on one side.
I found a horseshoe in the road. Lucky, they say. I'm still waiting.
My neighbor's rooster crows at all hours. I think it's broken.
Life's simple here. I like simple.
I traded a stack of wheat for an emerald this morning. Good trade, I think.
The iron golem walked right past my window this morning. Gave me a fright.
I can't find my other boot. If you see a boot, it's mine.
The cats have taken over the hay barn. The farmer's surrendered.
Some days are just for getting through. Today's one of the nicer ones, though.
I tried a new recipe. Mushroom and carrot pie. It was... bold.
My chickens have been laying double-yolk eggs. Very exciting around here.
I'm thinking of painting my door. Blue, maybe. Or green. Or blue.
There's a crack in my wall the shape of a creeper. Very unsettling.
The children found a frog and named it Mayor. It's very respected now.
I swept the path this morning. The wind unswept it by noon.
I spent the morning talking to a goat. It was a better listener than most people.
My back aches, my feet are sore and my heart is full. Normal day.
I've been meaning to fix my roof for a month. The roof's been meaning to leak for a month.
Have you ever noticed every village has someone who knows everyone's business? Here it's me.
I hope tomorrow's as nice as today. I'll settle for nearly as nice.
I traded my old hat for a new hat. The new hat is worse. I miss the old hat.
The golem stood in the square for an hour today just looking at a flower. I like the golem.
My cousin from the next village visited. She thinks our bell is too loud. It is.
Somebody keeps stealing apples from the orchard. I suspect the pigs.
The well bucket squeaks. Everyone complains. Nobody oils it. Village life.
I bumped into a slime in the swamp last week. It bumped back.
I had the oddest feeling someone was watching me today. It was a parrot.
I counted the cows this morning. Then I counted them again. One of them moved.
The church bell and the village bell had a ringing contest. Nobody won. Everyone lost their hearing.
I'm saving up for a proper bed. My current one's mostly straw and hope.
I saw a shooting star last night and made a wish. I wished for pie. Still waiting.
Days go by quickly here. In a good way.
The children are learning to whistle. All of them. At once. Constantly.
I left my window open and a bat flew in. We had a long chat. Mostly screaming.
I think it's going to be a good harvest this year. Don't tell the weather.
The trader had a bottle he swore was a potion of youth. It was water. I'm still old.
My knees can predict rain better than the cleric.
I sat in the sun and did absolutely nothing. It was wonderful.
Someone's been planting flowers along the paths at night. Nobody's owned up to it.
I lost a bet and had to wear a pumpkin on my head all morning. Couldn't see a thing.
Ever since the new family arrived, the village has been livelier.
I tried to build a birdhouse. It's more of a bird shed now.
The baker's experimenting with cookies again. Bless her.
I can hear the river from my bed. Best sleep I've ever had.
It's the little things, isn't it? A warm bowl, a friendly nod.
I saw two rabbits fighting over a carrot. Very dramatic. The carrot won.
My hands smell of onions. They always smell of onions. It's a lifestyle.
Every morning, the same three birds sit on my fence. I think they're judging me.
I'm learning to knit. I've made one sock. It's three feet long.
Did you see the sunset yesterday? The whole sky was on fire. The good kind.
I keep meaning to visit the next village. Then I remember walking exists.
The cleric gave me a potion for my cough. Now I glow slightly.
Some days I feel like the village is one big family. A noisy one.
I made friends with a crow. It brings me shiny pebbles. I bring it bread.
I think the golem likes me. It stood next to me for a whole minute.
There's nothing like a cool drink from the well on a warm day.
We had a power cut. I mean, a redstone torch went out. Same thing.
I've been trying to grow a pumpkin as big as a house. It's the size of a pumpkin.
My door creaks. I've named the creak. It's called Gregory.
I had soup for breakfast. Don't judge me. It was good soup.
The sheep got out again. They always get out again.
I don't know much, but I know this village. Every stone of it.
Somebody tied a bow on the bell. Very festive. The cleric's furious.
The spiders have been building webs on the fences. Ugly, but impressive.
I found a sweet berry bush behind the church. Ouch. Worth it.
I'm thinking about getting a dog. Or a cat. Or a very quiet parrot.
Everything's in its place, more or less. Mostly less.
The kids dared me to touch the golem's nose. I did. It didn't like it.
I spilled an entire bucket of milk on the path. The cats think it was a gift.
I heard a strange noise from the well last night. Turned out to be an echo of me yawning.
If you're ever bored, count the bricks on the church. I've done it. It's not that fun.
Everyone's got a story. Most people just never ask.
The fields smell like cut hay and sunshine. My favorite smell.
I tried to teach a chicken to fetch. The chicken taught me humility.
I don't need adventure. My garden's full of slugs. That's plenty of drama.
I got my sleeve caught on a fence and tore it right off. Very fashionable now.
Even on dull days, the bell rings at noon. That's comforting, somehow.
There's a wasp nest by the barn. We've agreed to leave each other alone.
I found a book on my doorstep with no name in it. Mystery! It's about turnips.
Rain or shine, there's always someone at the well. That's {village} for you.
I swapped seats at supper and now everyone thinks I'm being mysterious.
My favorite mug cracked. I'm still using it. We've been through too much together.
I tried sleeping in late. The roosters disagreed.
I hung wind chimes. The wind's been very chatty since.
Nobody in {village} can whistle in tune. It's a village tradition at this point.
A dog followed me around all morning. Now I think it lives with me.
Have you noticed the grass is greener near the church? The cleric won't say why.
I spent a whole emerald on a fancy hat. Then it rained.
My neighbor sings in the bath. Very loudly. Very badly. Every night.
I'm trying to eat more vegetables. The carrots are winning.
The well is the beating heart of {village}. That and the gossip.
I've been sleeping with the window open. Fresh air and the occasional moth.
Life's like a bucket of milk. You never know when someone's going to drink it.
Someone stacked all the pumpkins in the square into a tower. Very impressive. Very wobbly.
Some days you just need to sit on a fence and watch the clouds.
I made a friend at the market. We argued about turnips for an hour. Wonderful person.
The ducks have formed a gang. They patrol the pond.
I keep my good boots for special occasions. Haven't had one in years.
I found my lost cat. She was in the cupboard. For three days. Eating the bread.
My grandfather always said: never trust a creeper that's being quiet. They're always quiet.
There's frost on the windows this morning. Pretty patterns. Cold toes.
I'm told the bell was brought here by the first villagers on a cart pulled by goats.
I watched the clouds and one looked just like a llama. Then it looked like a llama with two heads.
I've learned to tell the time by the shadows. It's {time}, more or less.
Every village has its quirks. Ours is that nobody can agree on the best pie.
The bees made so much honey this year, we're putting it in everything.
The goat escaped and climbed onto the church roof. It's still up there. It's very proud.
I'm going to bed early tonight. I've decided. Ask me again in an hour.
I heard someone found diamonds in the ravine. Then I heard it was glass. Then I heard it was a lie.
It's a good day to be alive. Most days are, honestly.
I tried to make the bell ring by throwing a pebble. Missed. Hit the cleric.
My boots squeak on wet stone. Everyone knows when I'm coming.
I planted a tree last spring. It's taller than me now. Show-off.
I love the smell of the tavern at night. Apples and woodsmoke.
I keep the village's spare key. Nobody remembers what it opens.
The wandering trader stopped by. Prices have gone up. Llama prices especially.
My cat brought me a dead rabbit as a gift. I said thank you. It's the polite thing to do.
There's a little brook behind the houses. I dangle my feet in it when nobody's looking.
I've decided to be cheerful today. It's going quite well so far.
I made a scarecrow. The crows love it. They sit on it.
We had a village meeting about the noisy rooster. The rooster won.
My hands are full of splinters and my head's full of plans.
I found a four-leaf clover. Then I found eleven more. Now I'm suspicious.
Someone left a cake on the well. We're all too polite to eat it.
The night was so still I heard a zombie sneeze. Do zombies sneeze?
Today I learned that pigs can't look up. Very sad for the pigs.
My cousin swears she saw an enderman carrying a flower. I believe her.
I polished my best spoon. For no reason. It just felt right.
I like the sound of footsteps on the wooden bridge. Clop, clop, clop.
There's nothing better than a cold apple on a hot day.
It's {time}. Halfway through something, as always.
I tidied my house and found three things I thought I'd lost forever.
I wish the days were longer. Then I'd just nap more.
The well water tastes different after rain. Fresher, somehow.
I've seen a lot of things in {village}, but never a quiet Market Day.
Somebody's been leaving tiny carved animals around the village. I found a wooden bee today.
My grandmother lived to a hundred and two. She said it was the porridge.
Every house in {village} has a different color door. Mine's the brightest.
I'm learning a new song on the flute. The neighbors are learning patience.
A bird built a nest in my mailbox. I'm not getting letters until the chicks fledge.
Life's good. Not perfect. Good.
chat.new: We don't know each other well yet. Tell me something about yourself.
Most travelers just trade and go. You actually stopped to talk. That's nice.
You're welcome to stay in {village} a while. We don't bite. Mostly.
I'm {name}. I've lived here a long time. If you need directions, ask me.
New faces always get the village talking. Don't worry, it's mostly kind talk.
Where are you headed, if you don't mind my asking?
You'll get used to us. We're a bit odd, but we mean well.
If you're staying the night, the inn's warm. Well, the tavern. There's a bench.
I don't usually chat with strangers, but you seem all right.
The village is small, but you'll find everything you need. Food, beds, gossip.
Mind the golem. It's friendly, but it doesn't know you yet.
I hope you like it here. People who stay tend to stay a long time.
Are you a builder? You look like a builder. Or a digger. Something with a pickaxe.
First time in {village}? Make sure you see the bell. It's very important to us.
You're not one of those adventurers who takes everything that isn't nailed down, are you?
It takes a while to get to know people here. But once you do, they're yours for life.
I'm a bit shy with new people. It'll pass. Give it a few visits.
If anyone asks who invited you, say it was me. That'll make me sound important.
Welcome. The well's that way, the bell's that way, and my house is the one with the flowers.
We don't get many visitors who talk. Most just look at our trades and frown.
You seem like a decent sort. Don't prove me wrong.
I'll tell you what I tell everyone new: be nice to the golem, and it'll be nice to you.
You've come at a good time. The weather's been kind lately.
Stick around. We're more interesting than we look.
I'm told I talk too much. Let me know if I do. You'll have to interrupt me, though.
I can tell you've traveled. Your boots have that look.
Pleased to meet you properly. Next time I'll remember your name without asking.
Don't be a stranger. Well, you are a stranger. Don't stay one.
There's a lot to see around here, if you know where to look.
I think we'll get on fine, you and me.
If you come back tomorrow, I'll show you the best spot for watching the sunset.
Everyone in {village} started as a stranger once. Even me. I was born here, but still.
I hope your travels bring you back this way.
You've got a friendly face. That counts for a lot round here.
We're simple folk. Good food, hard work, long talks.
I don't trust everyone, but you've passed the first test. You said hello.
If you get lost, follow the sound of the bell. It always leads home.
I'm curious about you. That's a compliment, by the way.
Visitors make the days different. Different is good sometimes.
Come back soon. I'll have better stories next time.
chat.friendly: I always look forward to your visits. Did you know that?
I told {neighbor} about you. They want to meet you properly.
You've become part of {village}, you know. People ask after you.
I was hoping you'd stop by today. I've had a funny week.
I saved a story for you. Ready? It involves a goat and the church roof.
You're good company. Not everyone is.
You've been visiting a while now. It feels like you've always been around.
I think about the things you tell me. Your travels, the places you've been.
Next time you're here, stay for supper. I insist.
You've made {village} feel a bit bigger. In a good way.
It's nice having someone to talk to who isn't from here.
You always seem to turn up when I need cheering up.
I made something for you once, but it went wrong. Pretend I gave you something nice.
I think we're proper friends now, don't you?
You're the only one I've told about my secret pie recipe. Well, half of it.
I feel like I can tell you anything. Within reason.
The village feels safer when you're around. Is that silly?
I laughed at your joke from last time again this morning. On my own. Like a fool.
You've got a way of making people feel at ease.
You're one of us now. Whether you like it or not.
When you leave, I always wonder where you're going.
If you ever need somewhere to rest, my door's open.
I've started telling people we're friends. I hope that's all right.
I made a note of your favorite things. I'm not strange. I'm thoughtful.
You look well today. The road's treating you kindly?
Every time you visit, I learn something new.
I always feel a bit braver after we talk.
{village} talks about you, you know. Good things, mostly. The golem's undecided.
Stay a while. The day's nicer with company.
I kept your seat warm. Metaphorically.
You've got a good heart. I can tell these things.
You're the first person I think of when something funny happens.
I'm glad we met. I don't say that enough.
The children ask if the adventurer is coming today. I always say probably.
Let's take a walk sometime. Just around the village. Nothing dangerous.
You're easy to be around. That's a rare thing.
I'd trust you with my good spoons. That's saying something.
Next Market Day, let's go to the stalls together.
I've been meaning to ask: do you ever get lonely on the road?
Tell me about your day. I mean really tell me.
chat.close: I don't know what I'd do without our talks. Really.
You're like family to me now. You know that, don't you?
Some people come and go. You stayed. That means everything.
I think about you when you're away. I hope you're safe.
I've never told anyone this, but you make {village} feel like home.
You've seen me on my worst days and my best. And you keep coming back.
If you ever need anything, anything at all, you come to me first.
I'm proud of you, {player}. I don't know if anyone's told you that lately.
I keep a little candle in the window when you're out adventuring. Silly, I know.
Being your friend is one of the best things that ever happened to me.
I trust you more than I trust most people I've known all my life.
You don't have to say anything. I just like that you're here.
I wrote about you in my journal. Only good things. Mostly good things.
When I'm sad, I think about our talks. It helps.
I'd follow you to the Nether and back. Well, partway. It's very hot.
You're one of the few people who really listens.
We've been through a lot together, haven't we?
I hope you know how much you matter around here. To me especially.
I saved this spot by the well for us. Nobody else sits here now.
Whatever happens out there, you've always got a home in {village}.
I'm a better person since we became friends. Truly.
You're the first one I'd tell good news to. And bad news. All the news.
Thank you. For everything. I don't say it enough.
If I could give you anything, it'd be a day with nothing to worry about.
You've got a friend for life here. I hope you know that.
Some friendships just fit. Ours does.
I'd stay up all night listening to your stories. I have, actually. Twice.
I always feel lighter after you visit.
Promise me you'll be careful out there. I mean it.
I keep everything you've ever given me in a little box. Don't laugh.
You understand me better than I understand myself sometimes.
Even on quiet days, I know you're out there somewhere. That's comforting.
I'd share my last loaf with you. And I really love bread.
When we're old and grey, we'll still be talking by this well.
You've made my life so much bigger than it was.
I'm so glad you walked into {village} that day.
Friends like you are rarer than diamonds. And much better company.
I hope I've been as good a friend to you as you've been to me.
There's no one I'd rather spend a quiet afternoon with.
I'll always be here when you get back. Always.
chat.warmhearted: I baked too many rolls again. You'll take some, won't you? You look like you need feeding.
I've been checking on old Pell next door. He says he's fine, but his firewood pile says otherwise.
Everyone in {village} needs a little looking after. Even the ones who say they don't.
I made a pie for the new family down the lane. Nothing says welcome like crust.
My day? Busy, but the good kind. The kind where you help people.
I knitted mittens for all the children. Some of them are slightly different sizes.
If you're ever cold or hungry, my door's open. I mean that.
I always set an extra place at supper. You never know who'll turn up.
The kettle's always warm at my house. It's practically a law.
I found a lost kitten this morning. She's sleeping in my bread basket now. The bread's in a box.
Someone left flowers on my step. I suspect {friend}. Isn't that lovely?
You look tired, dear. Are you sleeping enough? Eating enough? Laughing enough?
I made soup for a neighbor who was poorly. Now three neighbors are suddenly poorly.
There's nothing a warm meal and a kind word can't make a little better.
I hugged the iron golem today. It didn't hug back, but I think it appreciated it.
My grandmother taught me to bake. My grandchildren will eat what I bake. That's the circle.
I always remember everyone's birthdays. It's the least I can do.
I gave my good scarf to a traveler who looked chilly. I have other scarves. Probably.
The best thing about a village is that nobody has to be alone in it.
Sit down a minute, love. The world can wait while you catch your breath.
I'm teaching the children to make cookies. Mostly they eat the dough.
My oven's been going since dawn. The whole street smells of cinnamon.
I worry about the travelers who sleep out in the wilds. Do you have somewhere warm tonight?
I left a basket of eggs for the family by the well. They've had a hard month.
A full table is a happy table. That's what I always say.
I don't need much. A warm hearth, a full pot, and people to share them with.
Do you like honey? I'll save you a jar from the next batch.
My cheeks hurt from smiling today. Good day, then.
I patched up a little girl's knee this morning. Brave as a lion, she was.
When people are sad, I bake. When people are happy, I bake. I bake a lot.
I've been told I fuss too much. I'm going to keep fussing, thank you.
Every face in {village} is a face I'd cook for.
I always save the biggest slice for whoever looks like they need it most.
The secret to good bread is patience. Same as the secret to good friends.
I tucked a little extra into the baker's basket for the widow down the lane. Don't tell.
You've got a smudge on your cheek. Here. There. Much better.
The best days are the ones where you go to bed tired from caring about people.
I hope someone's looking after you out there, {player}. Someone should.
I made far too much jam this year. I'm giving it away to anyone who stands still long enough.
Your health is your wealth, my mother used to say. Then she'd make me eat my greens.
I've started leaving a bowl of milk out for the village cats. Now there are eleven of them.
There's always room for one more by the fire.
I like days when nothing goes wrong and everyone gets fed.
If you're ever passing at suppertime, follow your nose to my door.
Kindness is like bread. Best shared warm.
chat.thoughtful: I've been reading about the old builders. Who carved the temples in the desert, do you think?
I spent the morning thinking about time. Whether it moves, or whether we do.
Do you ever wonder if the villages talk to each other, somehow? Over great distances?
I've been keeping a journal. Not of events, of thoughts. It's getting thick.
A book I'm reading says every block of stone was once something else. Sand, or bone, or sea.
I watched the river for an hour today. It never once repeated itself.
Have you noticed that the moon changes, but always comes back the same? There's comfort in that.
I wonder sometimes what the iron golems think about. Do they dream?
Quiet days are rare. I try to use them well. Mostly for wondering.
I read that the End has no day or night. I can't decide if that sounds peaceful or terrible.
Every person in {village} is a story I've only read a few pages of.
I've been thinking about how much of what we do is habit, and how much is choice.
I asked the librarian for a book about everything. She gave me a map.
Do you think the endermen are lonely? They always seem to be looking for something.
I like how ideas grow if you leave them alone for a while. Like seeds.
Some days I just sit and listen. You learn more than you'd think.
I wrote a poem about the bell. It's mostly about silence, oddly.
Why do you think the old ones built the strongholds so deep?
My mind's been wandering all day. It's further away than you'd think.
I've noticed the swallows come back to the same eaves every year. How do they remember?
Have you ever looked at an enchanting table's runes and felt you almost understood them?
There's a difference between knowing a thing and understanding it. I'm still learning which is which.
I read slowly. I'd rather remember one page than forget a hundred.
The village has its own rhythm. I've been trying to write it down.
I think the most interesting questions are the ones without answers.
I wonder who lived in the ruins past the hill, and whether they had a bell too.
I've been reading about redstone. It seems almost alive, the way it carries a signal.
I counted the steps from my door to the well. Two hundred and twelve. I don't know why I needed to know.
Do you keep a record of your travels? You should. Memory is generous but not honest.
I spent the afternoon under a tree, thinking about nothing. It took a lot of concentration.
Everything that lasts seems to be made slowly. Mountains. Friendships. Good books.
Have you ever noticed how the world sounds different after it snows?
I think kindness is a sort of wisdom. Maybe the most important sort.
The ancient cities in the deep dark... who builds a city where no light reaches?
I've been reading old letters from the village archives. People worried about the same things then.
I keep a list of things I'd like to understand before I'm old. It's very long.
The sky at dusk makes me feel small in a way I like.
Some things are best said slowly. Most things, actually.
I'm trying to learn to be patient. It's taking a long time.
What would you write on the first page of a book about your life?
I think every village is a little world. Ours is a nice one.
I found a book with half the pages torn out. Now I'm writing my own ending.
I wonder whether villagers in other lands think the way we do.
I've been thinking about why people leave places, and why they come back.
There's an old saying: the bell rings for everyone, but each of us hears it differently.
chat.playful: I hid a cookie in every haystack in {village}. Treasure hunt! You have until sundown.
Guess what I did today. No, guess! Wrong. I taught a chicken to dance. Sort of.
I've been practicing my whistle. Listen! ...Well, it sounds better when I do it.
I put a pumpkin on the scarecrow's head. Now it looks like an enderman's cousin.
Want to hear a song? I made it up just now. It's about cheese.
I've been running around all morning. I'm not sure why. It felt right.
I convinced three children that the bell can talk. Now they're all whispering to it.
Life's too short to walk when you can skip!
I made a crown out of daisies. I'm the queen of {village} now. Bow!
I tried to juggle apples. Now I have applesauce.
I've been composing a ballad about the golem. It rhymes "iron" with "lion." Genius, I know.
If you could have any animal as a pet, what would it be? I'd have a goat that sings.
I challenged {friend} to a race and lost. I demand a rematch. Best of fifty.
Let's play a game: I say a word, you say the first thing you think. Bucket! ...Too slow!
I left a note on the baker's door saying "the bread is watching you." She didn't laugh.
I can stand on one foot for a whole minute. Watch! ...Nearly a minute.
Today's going great. I found a coin, a feather and a very interesting rock.
I painted a smiley face on a melon. His name is Gerald.
Music makes everything better. Even chores. Especially chores.
I've been teaching the parrots rude songs. Don't tell anyone.
I laughed so hard at lunch that cider came out of my nose. Worth it.
Have you ever tried to out-stare a cat? I lost. Badly.
I'm planning a surprise party. For whom? I haven't decided yet.
Every day's a good day for a little mischief. Harmless mischief.
I can play three instruments. Badly, mostly, and loudly.
I tried to tell the golem a joke. Tough crowd.
I'm organizing a talent show. My talent is organizing talent shows.
I tickled a sheep. It didn't react. Sheep have no sense of humor.
If you hear giggling from the haystacks, it's probably me.
I made up a dance for the bell. Every time it rings, I do it. Everyone stares.
Want to arm wrestle? I warn you, I've been practicing on fence posts.
I've been trying to whistle and hum at the same time. It sounds like a sick bee.
I invented a new game. It's like tag, but everyone's it. Total chaos. Wonderful.
I tied ribbons on all the cows' tails. They look very festive.
I'd have more fun if the day had more hours. Or if I needed less sleep.
Do you know any good songs? I've worn out all of mine.
I told the children the moon is made of cheese. Now they want to go there.
A day without laughing is a day wasted. Today is NOT wasted.
I wrote a song about you! It's mostly about your hat.
I'm practicing my bow. For when I'm famous. Which is soon.
I hid in a barrel to surprise {friend}. I fell asleep. Surprise ruined.
Ooh, I have the best idea. I'll tell you later. It's a surprise.
I've decided today's theme is "hats." Everyone's getting a hat.
I lost a staring contest to a frog. Frogs are unbeatable.
Life is short, the cake is sweet, and I'm going to have a second slice.
chat.adventurous: I climbed the tallest tree past the river today. You can see three villages from the top!
I've been mapping the caves under the hill. Found a lake down there, black as ink.
Someday I'm going to see the ocean monuments. The real ones, with the guardians.
I found a strange stone near the river. It hums when you hold it. I think. Maybe I imagined it.
I've packed my bag three times this week. One of these days I'll actually go.
Have you ever been to the badlands? I hear the hills there are striped like a cake.
I followed a fox halfway to the mountains before I realized I'd forgotten lunch.
The world's so big and I've seen so little of it.
I want to ride a camel across the desert. Or at least sit on one.
I swam out to the island in the lake. There's nothing there but a very surprised turtle.
The best kind of day is one where you don't know what's over the next hill.
Tell me about the farthest place you've ever been. Leave nothing out.
I've been practicing with a bow. For hunting. And for dramatic poses.
They say there's a woodland mansion deep in the dark forest. Full of illagers. I'd like to see it. From a distance.
I slept under the stars last night. Woke up with a spider on my face. Still worth it.
I'm saving up for a good sword and sturdy boots. Then the world had better watch out.
Have you been to the Nether? What's it like? Is it really hot? Really, really hot?
I found an old shipwreck on the shore. There was a map inside. It was soggy. I'm drying it.
Someday I want to climb a mountain so high the snow never melts.
My feet are itchy. Not literally. They want to go somewhere.
I traded with a wandering trader for a compass. Now I know which way north is. Wonderful.
I've been listening to the cartographer's stories. Every one of them makes me want to leave.
Do you know how to tame a horse? I tried once. The horse disagreed.
The edge of the map is just where the next map starts.
I heard the jungle has temples full of traps and treasure. Traps don't scare me. Much.
I went exploring the old mineshaft. Lots of cobwebs. Lots of rails. One very angry cave spider.
I keep a list of places I'll visit. It gets longer faster than I can cross things off.
Ever ridden a boat down a river at full speed? Best feeling in the world.
I want to see the aurora, if there is such a thing. Someone told me about lights in the far north.
I'm restless today. Everything's fine, but the horizon's calling.
What's the most dangerous thing you've ever fought? Tell me. I need details.
My boots have holes from all my walking. Badges of honor.
I found a cave with glowing berries hanging from the ceiling. Like little lanterns.
They say there's a city at the end of the world. I'd go, if I knew which end.
I've decided to learn to swim properly. So I can explore underwater ruins.
I chased a rabbit into the forest and found a clearing full of mushrooms. Big ones!
I'll go adventuring with you someday. When you're ready for a very enthusiastic companion.
The world's full of secrets. I want to find a few before I'm old and grey.
I'm practicing reading maps. Upside down, so far. Getting better.
I climbed onto the roof of the church to watch the sunset. Don't tell the cleric.
