There's a ravine to the east that goes down forever. I dropped a pebble. Still waiting.
Some people want a quiet life. I want a loud one, full of stories.
I envy the birds. They don't need maps.
I met a traveler who'd seen a bamboo jungle full of pandas. Pandas!
One day I'll come back from somewhere far away with a story nobody believes.
chat.meticulous: I reorganized my collection of buttons by size, then by color, then by age. It took all morning.
Did you know there are forty-two different kinds of flowers in this region? I've pressed thirty-nine.
Everything has a place, and everything in its place. That's my motto.
I counted the bricks in the church wall today. Four hundred and twelve. One's slightly crooked.
I keep a ledger of every trade I make. Every single one. It's very satisfying.
Someone left the gate open at the sheep pen again. I've written a strongly worded note.
I've catalogued every shell I've ever found. Would you like to see the catalog? It's in alphabetical order.
I like my mornings planned to the minute. Today I was three minutes behind. It's been a struggle.
Tidy home, tidy mind. That's what I always say.
I found a rare blue feather today. It's now item four hundred and six in my collection.
I polished my doorknob. You can see your face in it. Go on, look.
Did you notice the path stones are uneven near the well? I've reported it twice.
I collect interesting stones. Each one's labeled with where and when I found it.
My spice rack is alphabetical. My bookshelf is by height. My socks are by mood.
If everyone just put things back where they found them, life would be so much simpler.
I measured the bell. Exactly as tall as it is wide. Isn't that pleasing?
I spent the afternoon sorting seeds. Wheat, beetroot, melon, pumpkin. Separately. Obviously.
I have a list of lists. It keeps me sane.
Somebody moved my chair two inches to the left. I noticed immediately.
I've been studying the patterns of the village banners. There's a system, if you look closely.
Every coin I've ever earned is accounted for. Except one. I think about it often.
I make my bed with perfect corners every morning. It's the little things.
I dusted every jar in my pantry today. Even the ones I never open.
Did you know a stack holds sixty-four items? Perfect number. Divides evenly every way.
I've labeled all my drawers. Including the one that says "miscellaneous labels."
I'd like to visit the library's archive someday and organize it properly.
I noticed the bell rings a quarter beat late on cold mornings. Fascinating.
My collection of pressed leaves is up to every tree in the region. Except jungle. Too humid.
I wrote down everything I ate this week. Very informative. Too much bread.
Precision is a kind of kindness. To yourself, mostly.
I always know where everything is. People come to me when they lose things.
I've started a collection of interesting knots. I have nineteen.
I wipe my boots three times before going inside. Some say that's excessive. Those people have dirty floors.
I have a theory about which chickens lay the most eggs. I'm keeping notes.
I wound all the clocks in the village this morning. They're all in agreement now.
Order is calming. Chaos is exhausting. I choose calm.
I traded for a lovely little music disc. I don't own a jukebox. It's for the collection.
If you need anything found, measured or sorted, I'm your resident.
I spent an hour arranging my bookshelf by the color of the spines. It looks like a rainbow.
I've noted every time it's rained this season. There's a pattern. I'm close to cracking it.
Everything I own fits neatly into three chests. I'm very proud of that.
A crooked picture frame can ruin my whole afternoon.
I collect stamps. Well, wax seals from letters. Same thing, really.
I organized the village shed. Now nobody can find anything except me.
Small, careful steps. That's how you build anything worth building.
chat.steadfast: Same as always. Up early, garden, work, supper. I like a day that knows what it is.
The tomatoes are coming along. Slowly. Good things take their time.
I've lived in {village} all my life. Never felt the need to leave. Everything I love is here.
Rain or shine, the garden needs tending. So I tend it.
My father planted that oak by the well. I water it every week. It'll outlive us all.
Not much changes around here. That's what I like about it.
I fixed the fence by the sheep pen. Took all morning. It'll hold for years now.
You can count on me. That's not a boast. It's just how I'm made.
I don't say much, but I'm always around if you need a hand.
Steady work and a good night's sleep. Can't ask for more.
My roses are blooming. Three years I've waited for that bush. Worth every day.
I pulled weeds till noon. They'll be back. So will I.
Some folks need excitement. I need my porch and a quiet evening.
The soil here's good. Dark and rich. You can grow anything with a little patience.
I made the same breakfast every day for twenty years. Never once got tired of it.
Promises are only as good as the person keeping them. I keep mine.
The wind's from the west today. Means rain by evening. You'll see.
I've watched the children of {village} grow up. Now their children are growing up.
I like knowing what tomorrow will look like. Mostly it looks like today, and that's fine.
My hands are dirty, my back's sore and my beans are thriving. Good day.
I've been fixing the same squeaky wheel on my cart for years. It's an old friend now.
There's nothing wrong with a quiet life. Quiet doesn't mean empty.
I've planted a row of saplings along the path. In ten years it'll be a fine avenue.
Hard times come and go. The village stays. So do I.
I'm not one for big speeches. But I'm glad you're here.
I check on the beehives every morning. They know my face.
You'll find me in the garden most days. Easy to find. Hard to move.
I like a job done properly, even if nobody notices.
I don't hurry. Hurrying's how you trip.
My grandmother's spade still works better than any new one.
The seasons come round regular as the bell. I find that comforting.
I've weathered three bad winters and a raid. I'll weather whatever's next.
A good fence makes a good neighbor. A good neighbor makes a better one.
Just tending the carrots. They're shy this year. They'll come round.
I don't need much. Good bread, honest work, a warm bed.
I plant a tree every spring. Someone else will sit in its shade someday.
People think steady means boring. I think it means dependable.
My garden doesn't care what kind of day I've had. That helps.
Some things you can't rush. Bread. Trees. Trust.
I've sat on the same bench by the well every evening for years. It knows the shape of me.
Good soil, good rain, good people. That's {village}.
I keep my tools sharp and my word kept.
I'll be here tomorrow, same as today. Come by anytime.
Every season has its work. Right now it's mulching.
The best things grow slowly and stay a long time.
chat.reserved: ...It's been a quiet day. I like quiet days.
I went fishing this morning. Didn't catch anything. Didn't mind.
I don't talk much. But I listen. ...Mostly.
...The river was very still today. Like glass.
I sat by the water. Watched the dragonflies. That's all. It was nice.
...Sorry. I'm not good at small talk. It's nice of you to ask, though.
I caught a salmon this big. ...Well. About this big. Fine. This big.
...I don't really like crowds. The well at noon is too much for me.
...Thank you for talking to me. People usually don't.
I like the early mornings. Before anyone else is up.
...I made a little wooden boat. It floats. Mostly sideways.
Mm. Today was fine. The fish were shy. So was I.
...There's a heron that comes to the river every morning. We have an understanding.
I don't say much at the tavern. I just like hearing everyone laugh.
...I'm happy, I think. In my own quiet way.
The rain sounds nice on the water. Like a hundred little whispers.
...You're easy to talk to. That doesn't happen often.
I spent the afternoon mending my nets. It's peaceful work.
...I know people think I'm odd. I don't mind.
There's a spot upstream where the water's deep and clear. ...I could show you. If you like.
...I read a little last night. A story about a lighthouse keeper. I liked him.
I prefer animals, mostly. They don't expect you to talk.
...Today was good. Nothing happened. That's good.
I'm not lonely. I'm alone, sometimes. It's different.
...The golem nodded at me today. At least, I think it did.
Mm. Nice weather for fishing.
...I wrote a letter to my sister. I didn't send it. I might.
Some people fill silences. I like letting them be.
...I don't need much. A rod, a river, a quiet evening.
...Thank you for remembering my name.
I saw a kingfisher today. Blue as the sky. Gone in a blink.
...I'm better at doing than saying.
Mm. The fish are biting in the evening this week.
...I can tell you're kind. You don't push.
I like the sound of the oars when I row out at dawn.
...I watched the sunset alone. It was lovely. I wished someone was there. Then I didn't.
...Sorry, I was thinking. What did you say? Oh. My day. It was fine.
...I carved a little fish for the baker's son. He hasn't let go of it since.
The tavern's too loud, but the walk home after is nice.
...I'm glad you stopped by. Really.
...I don't know what to say. But I'm happy you're here.
I sat on the dock and let my feet dangle in the water. Cold. Nice.
...Some days are just for breathing.
I'll answer any question you have. Slowly.
...The stars were bright last night. I counted some. Lost count.
chat.imaginative: I dreamt the whole village floated up into the clouds and the sheep grew wings. Isn't that lovely?
I painted the sky purple today. It wasn't purple. It should have been.
Do you think the stars are holes in the night, and something bright is behind them?
I named all the clouds this morning. That one's Bartholomew. He's grumpy.
I'm writing a story about a mushroom who wants to be a tree. It's very moving.
If colors had sounds, I think yellow would be a trumpet. What do you think green would be?
I see faces in everything. The well has a face. It's surprised.
I painted a mural on my wall. It's a forest at night with glowing foxes.
What if the endermen are just very tall, very shy painters?
I made a hat out of leaves. I'm a tree today. Please water me.
I imagine the bell talks to the moon at night. Long, slow conversations.
The light this afternoon was the color of apricots. I tried to paint it. I made a peach.
I collect sunset colors in my sketchbook. I have forty-three oranges.
What if every footprint you left behind grew into a flower? You'd be very easy to find.
I'm designing a castle made entirely of glass and moss. It's mostly in my head.
I think the river's singing. Listen closely. It's a very old song.
I painted {friend} as a dragon. They didn't love it. I loved it.
Do you ever feel like you're in a story, and someone's reading you?
I've decided the moon is a great big pearl that a giant forgot to collect.
Every block in the world has a color nobody's discovered yet.
I'm painting a picture of what {village} will look like in a hundred years. There are more trees.
I mixed every color of dye together. It made brown. Disappointing brown.
If I could live anywhere, I'd live inside a rainbow. Probably in the blue bit.
I think the chickens are secretly plotting. Look at their eyes.
I painted my door with stars. Now it feels like I'm walking into the night every time I go home.
Have you ever looked at a lava pool and seen pictures in it? Like a fire that tells stories.
I'm writing a song for the wind. It doesn't have words. It doesn't need them.
Clouds are just the sky's daydreams.
I imagine every house in {village} has its own little personality. Mine's cheerful but forgetful.
I made a little painting of you. You were very heroic. Slightly taller.
What color is today, do you think? I think it's a soft teal with a dot of gold.
I tried to paint the smell of rain. It came out grey and hopeful.
When I close my eyes, I see whole worlds. Some of them have better weather.
I'm going to paint the bell tower blue. Don't tell anyone.
I think the fireflies are tiny stars that fell down and decided to stay.
I drew a map of a place that doesn't exist. I've been exploring it all week.
Every sunset's a painting the sky only shows once.
I've imagined a whole family living in the hollow tree by the path. They're very small. Very polite.
If you could paint anything, what would it be? I'd paint music.
I spilled paint on my shoes and now they're my favorite shoes.
The fog this morning made everything look like a dream. I walked around in it for ages.
I'm painting a portrait of every resident in {village}. I'm on number three. It's slow.
I think beauty hides in ordinary places so only the patient people find it.
Do you think the sea dreams? I think it dreams of being the sky.
My head's full of colors today. I hope some of them spill out.
chat.pragmatic: Day's fine. Fixed a door, mended a cart, sharpened my tools. Productive.
If it isn't broken, don't fix it. If it is broken, bring it to me.
I carved a new handle for my axe. Better grip. Fewer blisters.
Waste not, want not. I've used every scrap of that oak.
The roof on the barn needs patching before winter. That's tomorrow's job.
People talk too much and do too little. Not you, though. You seem all right.
I don't bother with fancy. Sturdy's better. Sturdy lasts.
Spent the morning splitting firewood. Enough for a month now.
You want my advice? Plan for the worst, hope for the best, carry a spare torch.
I don't see the point in worrying about things you can't change.
Good tools are worth the emeralds. Cheap ones cost you twice.
I measure twice and cut once. Saves time. Saves wood.
Everyone wants things to be easy. Easy doesn't build houses.
That old well needs a new bucket. Third time I've said it. I'll just make one.
There's always work to be done. Might as well do it well.
I carved a spoon today. It's a good spoon. Nothing fancy. Just good.
Rain's coming. Better get the hay covered.
If you're going out at night, bring a shield. Simple as that.
I don't trust anything I can't fix myself.
Fixed the bell rope. It was fraying. Could've snapped mid-ring. Disaster averted.
Sentiment's fine, but it doesn't patch a roof.
I keep spare nails in every pocket. You'd be amazed how often that matters.
Most problems have simple answers. People just don't like simple answers.
Good day's work. Tired arms, clear head.
I whittled a peg for the gate. Gate's closing properly now. Small win.
Don't waste daylight. It's the cheapest light you'll ever get.
I don't need thanks. I just need people to stop leaning on the fence.
A sharp blade's safer than a dull one. Most people don't believe that.
I like a straight answer. Ask me anything. You'll get one.
Bought a new saw from the trader. Overpriced, but it works.
Supper's beans. Simple, filling, cheap. Perfect.
I build things that last. Everything else is decoration.
Busy hands, quiet mind.
If you need a hand with anything practical, come find me.
People fuss about the weather. Can't change it. Dress for it.
I counted my firewood. Enough for winter if nobody wastes it.
I don't like waiting around. I'd rather be making something.
The church door was sticking. Shaved a little off the bottom. Fixed.
Long day. Got a lot done. That's the best kind.
There's no shortcut to doing a job properly.
I made a stool from the offcuts. Nothing gets wasted in my workshop.
Common sense isn't common. That's my experience.
The bridge planks are rotting. I'll replace them before someone goes through.
I don't believe in luck. I believe in preparation.
Make it simple, make it strong, make it last. That's the whole trick.
chat.curious: Did you know the bees all fly home in a straight line? How do they know where home is?
I've been watching the stars every night. One of them moved. I'm sure of it.
What's the farthest place you've ever been? What was the sky like there?
I took apart a clock to see how it works. I can't put it back together. I learned a lot though.
Why do you think cats can see phantoms? I have so many questions about cats.
I found a beetle with a shiny green back. I've been following it around all day.
Have you ever wondered what's under the bedrock? I wonder about it every night.
I asked the cleric where the stars come from. She said "up." Not very helpful.
How do you think the endermen move so fast? Do they fold space? Do they fold themselves?
I spent the night on the roof counting shooting stars. I got to eleven.
Is it true that some fish glow in the deep ocean? I need to see that.
I've been studying how the redstone torches flicker. There's a rhythm. Like breathing.
Why do sheep's wool grow back different colors if you dye them? That's not how hair works.
I mixed two potions together. Don't worry, nothing exploded. This time.
What do you think the moon is made of? I have three theories.
I've been listening to the wind through the bell tower. It makes different notes at different speeds.
Have you ever seen an axolotl? Are they really pink? I've only read about them.
I wonder why villages always grow around a bell.
I tried to dig straight down to see what's there. My mother stopped me. Wisely.
How does a compass always know where the spawn point is? What's it pointing to, really?
I found a fossil in the riverbank! A big curved bone. What do you think it was?
What do you think the first villager was like? Did they have a bell?
I tried to measure how fast the river flows. A leaf took forty seconds to pass the bridge.
I have a question for every star in the sky.
How do the bees know which flowers they've already visited? I've been watching for hours.
I made a list of things I don't know. It's the longest thing I've ever written.
What do you think's at the bottom of the ocean? Besides fish. And sand. And drowned.
I stayed up to watch the moon rise. It came up orange! Why orange?
Have you ever looked at a snowflake through a glass? Each one's different.
Do you think there are other villages that look just like ours? Somewhere very far away?
I want to know everything. Is that too much? It feels like the right amount.
I watched an ant carry a crumb bigger than itself all the way home. How?
Why does lava glow but water doesn't? I've been thinking about it all day.
What's your favorite thing you've ever discovered?
The stars make shapes if you squint. I've found a pickaxe, a bucket and a very small cow.
I found a cave with blue lights in the walls. I don't know what made them. I need to go back.
I'm keeping a journal of every bird I see. Twelve kinds so far!
Did you know if you put a sugar cane next to water, it grows? But not next to sand alone. Why?
How deep does the river go? Has anyone ever measured it?
I'm trying to figure out why the golem only gives flowers to children. Theories welcome.
I wish I could see inside a mountain. All those layers, all that history.
What do the wandering traders do in winter? Where do they go?
Every rock is a puzzle if you look closely enough.
Do you think the stars can see us too?
Tell me something you've learned recently. Anything! I collect facts.
chat.protective: Everyone's safe today. That's all I need to know.
I walked the edge of the village twice this morning. No tracks. Good.
I built a new fence round the sheep pen. Wolves came sniffing last week.
I keep an eye on the children when they play by the river. The current's stronger than it looks.
If anything's bothering you, tell me. I'll handle it.
I made sure every house has a torch by the door. Can't be too careful after dark.
I've been teaching the young ones how to spot a creeper. Green, quiet, hissing. Run.
Nothing gets past me in this village. Not even the cats.
I patched the wall by the fields. One less gap for the zombies to find.
I worry about you out there in the wilds. Do you have enough food? Enough torches?
A village is only as safe as the people watching over it.
I sharpened every blade in my workshop today. Just in case.
I don't sleep much. Someone has to keep listening.
I walked {friend} home last night. It was only two doors, but still.
The golem and I keep the peace. It does the heavy lifting.
I put a lantern on the path to the well. Somebody nearly fell in last week.
You look like you've had a rough trip. Rest here. You're safe in {village}.
I checked the bell rope. If there's trouble, everyone needs to hear it.
I made a woodworking project for the children: wooden shields. They love them.
Someone has to be the one who worries. I volunteer.
I keep spare bandages at home. Come by if you ever need them.
The pillagers haven't come this way in years. Doesn't mean they won't.
I taught my nephew to stay inside after dark. Took a while. He's stubborn. Like me.
I built shutters for every window on the north side. Storm season's coming.
I don't trust the woods after sunset. Too many glowing eyes.
If you hear the bell at night, get indoors. Don't ask questions.
I'd stand between this village and anything. I mean that.
Spent the day reinforcing the doors. Oak with iron hinges. Solid.
I know everyone's routine here. If someone's late, I notice.
The children call me the watchman. I don't mind. It suits me.
Safe roads, safe homes, safe people. That's my whole job, as I see it.
I spotted a spider on the church roof at dawn. Dealt with it.
I made a little wooden dog for the baker's girl. She was scared of the real ones.
Don't wander off the path, {player}. The bogs out east swallow boots.
I don't like strangers lurking. You're not a stranger. You're fine.
I keep a lantern lit by the gate all night. Guides people home.
I built a sturdy bench by the well. Nobody's going to fall off this one.
The golem's getting old. I check its cracks every week. I bring it flowers.
I count the sheep every evening. All accounted for. Good.
I'll walk you to the edge of the village when you leave. Just to be sure.
Someone has to think about the worst so everyone else doesn't have to.
I carved new handles for all the village gates. Sturdier.
Peace isn't free. Somebody's always paying attention.
You're welcome here as long as you like. You're under my watch now.
I'd rather build a hundred fences than lose one sheep.
chat.gentle: The poppies by the well opened today. I sat with them a while.
I found a little bird with a hurt wing. I'm keeping it warm in a basket until it's better.
It's been a soft sort of day. I hope yours has been too.
I planted forget-me-nots along the path. So nobody forgets the way home.
I like the quiet hour after rain, when everything drips and sparkles.
I made a wreath of cornflowers for the church door. Blue suits it.
Be gentle with yourself today, {player}. You do so much.
I watched a butterfly land on my hand. It stayed for ages. I didn't dare breathe.
I gave flowers to everyone I passed today. It made the whole morning brighter.
The bees and I have an agreement. I grow the flowers, they hum me songs.
I sing to my plants. They seem to like it. They're polite, anyway.
Sometimes the kindest thing you can do is just sit with someone.
I pressed a violet in my book today. Now every time I read, I'll find it.
I don't like loud things. Thunder, shouting, creepers. I like soft things.
The lilies of the valley smell so sweet. Would you like to smell them? Careful, they're shy.
I spoke softly to the horse that kicked the fence. He calmed right down.
I think flowers are the world's way of saying sorry for the rain.
I made tea from chamomile. Very calming. Would you like some?
I left a flower on the golem's shoulder. It's still there. It hasn't moved.
I tend the little garden by the graves. Everyone deserves flowers.
The morning glories climbed all the way up my window this week.
I hope nobody's sad in {village} today. I'd like to help, if they are.
I collect seeds from every flower I meet. Someday my whole garden will be memories.
I sat by the river and listened. Rivers are very good listeners too.
A kind word costs nothing, but it's worth so much.
I saw a fox cub playing in the meadow. I didn't tell anyone. It's our secret now.
I like the way dandelion seeds float. Like little wishes.
My garden's small, but there's something blooming in every season.
I put flowers in the windows of the empty house. It looked lonely.
I always say good morning to the oak tree by my door. It's very old. It deserves respect.
I made a daisy chain long enough to go around the well. It took all afternoon.
Gentle hands make good gardeners. My grandmother told me that.
I hope your journey has been kind to you. If not, rest here a while.
I fed the ducks today. One of them followed me home. He's very persistent.
I like to think every flower I plant makes the world a little softer.
The roses bloomed pink this year. Last year they were red. I think they're moody.
I don't like to see anyone hurting. Even the zombies look sad, if you look closely.
I tucked lavender in everyone's pillows. For good dreams.
A quiet word, a warm cup, a kind face. That's all most people need.
I'm growing sunflowers. They follow the sun around all day. So loyal.
I wrote a little poem about the meadow. It's only four lines. It's enough.
I'm glad you visit. You're gentle too, I think. I can tell.
I left honey on the doorstep of a neighbor who's been grieving.
Some days I just walk slowly and notice things. The world's full of small wonders.
May your day be as soft as a dandelion clock.
baby.greet: Hi! Hi! Hi! Are you the adventurer everyone talks about?
Hello! I'm not supposed to talk to strangers, but you look nice.
Hi! Do you have any cookies? You look like you have cookies.
Hello, grown-up! Want to see my rock collection?
Hi! I'm {name}! I'm this many years old! Well, almost!
Ooh, a visitor! Are you a knight? You look like a knight.
Hello! Did you bring presents? I'm only asking.
Hi! I can count to sixty-four! Want to hear?
Hello! My mum says I talk too much. Is that true?
Hi! Is that a real sword? Can I hold it? No? Okay.
Hello! I just saw a beetle as big as my thumb!
Hi! You're tall! Are all adventurers tall?
Hello! Do you want to play tag? You're it!
Hi! I lost a tooth! Look! There's a hole!
Hello! I'm going to be the bravest villager ever when I grow up.
Hi! The golem picked me up today! I was so high!
Hello! My friend says you've been to the Nether. Is it really on fire?
Hi! Shh, I'm hiding from my sister.
Hello! I drew a picture of you. You have very square hair.
Hi! Want to see me do a cartwheel? ...That was a cartwheel.
Hello! Can I ride on your shoulders? Please? Please?
Hi! I found a feather! It's blue! Well, grey. Bluish-grey.
Hello! Are you staying for supper? We're having stew. We're always having stew.
Hi! I'm not tired. I'm never tired. *yawn*
Hello! I've been waiting for you forever! Since lunch!
Hi, {player}! I remembered your name!
Hello! Guess what? No, guess! I learned to whistle! Listen! ...Fffft. Almost!
Hi! Did you see any dragons today?
Hello! Do you know any good games?
Hi! I'm practicing being a grown-up. Good day to you, sir or madam. How was that?
baby.chat: I found a frog and named it Captain Hops. It's my best friend now.
I built a fort out of hay bales! Nobody's allowed in except my friends. And you, maybe.
The golem gave me a poppy today! I'm going to keep it forever.
I'm not allowed near the river by myself. But I can see it from here!
When I grow up I'm going to have a hundred cats.
I ate a whole carrot today. A whole one! Raw!
My grandma tells the best stories. Mostly about when she was little. Like me!
I can hop on one foot all the way to the well. Almost.
The baker gave me a bread crust. I fed it to a duck. The duck was happy.
I'm scared of the dark. A little. Only at night.
I have a secret. I can't tell you. Okay, I'll tell you. I like pickles.
My friend said creepers are made of leaves. Is that true? I don't think that's true.
I saw a rainbow and tried to run to the end. It kept moving!
I'm learning my letters. B is for bell! And bread! And bees!
My big brother says I'm annoying. I'm not annoying. I'm enthusiastic.
I've been collecting shiny pebbles. I have eleven! And one that's sort of shiny.
The chickens chase me sometimes. I chase them back.
I helped my mum bake today. I mostly ate the dough.
I can't wait to grow up. Then I can stay up late every night!
I named the clouds today. That one's called Fluffy and that one's called Also Fluffy.
I fell in a puddle. It was the best thing that happened all week.
The cat sleeps on my bed every night. She snores!
I made a crown out of daisies! I'm a princess now. Or a king. Or a queen-king.
My favorite color is every color.
I tried to catch a butterfly. It caught me. It landed on my nose!
I'm going to be a knight when I grow up. Or a baker. Or a knight who bakes.
My dad can lift a whole hay bale. By himself! He's the strongest.
I found a hole in the ground. I think a rabbit lives there. Or a dragon. A small dragon.
I'm not allowed to touch the bell. I touched it once. It was cold.
The other kids and I are digging to the other side of the world. We're nearly there.
I can do a really good pig noise. Oink! See?
Grown-ups talk about boring things. Like weather. And taxes. What are taxes?
I saw a spider in the barn. I wasn't scared. Much.
I want to go on an adventure like you! Can I come next time? When I'm bigger?
I lost my shoe. Then I found it. It was on my foot.
My friend {friend} can wiggle their ears! I'm practicing.
I put a worm in my pocket. Mum found it. Mum screamed.
I like the sound of rain on the roof. It sounds like clapping.
I'm making a map of the village. The bell is in the middle and it's very big.
I can count all the cows. There are lots. Lots and lots.
Do you have a pet? I want a pet. A wolf! A tame one.
I had a dream that I could fly. I flew over the whole village!
I'm not crying, my eyes are just leaking because I bumped my knee.
The tavern smells like apples. I'm not allowed in yet. When I'm big!
I found a really good stick. It's a sword. And a wand. And a fishing rod.
I'm going to build the biggest sandcastle ever. Out of real sand blocks!
When the bard plays, I dance! Like this! Wheee!
My teacher says I'm clever. My teacher says I'm also loud.
I tried to ride a sheep. It didn't work.
Why is the sky blue? Nobody knows. I asked everyone.
I gave the golem a hug. It's very cold and very hard. Still nice.
I'm going to stay up until midnight tonight. Maybe. Probably not.
The best day is Market Day. There's honey cake!
I found a robin's egg! Well, a blue rock. But it looked like an egg!
I want to be just like you when I grow up, {player}.
My sister and I had a race. I won! She says she let me. She didn't.
I hid a cookie under my pillow for later. Then I forgot. Then the cat found it.
There's a monster under my bed. It's actually my slipper. But it might be a monster.
I can jump over the fence! Okay, the little fence. The very little one.
I'm learning to whistle. Pheeeew! Close enough.
My favorite food is everything with honey on it.
I've decided to be a scholar. I'm going to know every single thing.
I like when you visit. You're fun for a grown-up.
The goats are funny. They yell for no reason!
I sang a song for the chickens. They liked it. I think.
I've got a loose tooth! Wanna see? Wiggle, wiggle!
I'm going to marry a frog. A nice frog. When I'm older.
Grown-ups worry too much. I don't worry. I play.
I made mud pies! Don't eat them. I learned that the hard way.
The moon follows me when I walk at night! Everywhere I go!
I collected all the feathers in the chicken coop. Now I'm part chicken.
Today was the best day ever! Yesterday was also the best day ever.
I'm going to grow up to be the tallest villager in the whole world.
Shh, I'm a ninja. You can't see me.
I fed the fish in the pond. Some of them waved. Fish can't wave. These ones did.
I wrote my name in the dirt. It's a bit wobbly. The rain washed it away.
I'm going to train a parrot to say my name. And "cookie."
The well echoes! Hello! Hello! Hello! See?
I pretended to be a zombie and scared my brother. Then he cried. Then I said sorry.
Why do grown-ups drink coffee? It smells nice but tastes like burnt dirt.
My favorite animal is a llama. Because they spit! Ew! But funny!
I want to see the ocean one day. Is it really really big?
I'm brave. I walked past the dark barn all by myself. Fast. But by myself.
I found a mushroom! Don't worry, I didn't eat it. This time.
The baby next door can't talk yet. I'm teaching her words. She says "ba."
I've got a secret clubhouse. The password is "potato."
I'm a very good helper. I helped carry ONE apple today.
Stars are tiny holes in the sky's blanket. My grandpa said so.
I'm going to be a painter! I already painted the dog. He didn't like it.
baby.work: When I grow up I'm going to be a farmer and grow the biggest pumpkin ever!
I want to be a librarian so I can read all the books. ALL of them.
I'm going to be a knight and fight a dragon! A small one first.
I'll be a baker and make cookies every day. Cookies for breakfast!
I'm practicing being a fisherman. I caught a stick! It counts.
I want to be a cartographer and draw maps of everywhere!
When I'm grown I'm going to be a bard and sing all day.
I'm going to work at the sawmill! Saw saw saw!
My mum says I can be anything I want. Even a llama. Especially a llama.
I'd like to be an apothecary. I already know which flowers smell nice.
I'm going to be the golem's helper. Do golems need helpers?
I want to be a painter! I'll paint the whole village purple.
I'm going to be a cook! I can already make toast. Mostly burnt.
When I grow up I'll have a trade and an apron and everything!
I'm practicing my serious trading face. Hrrmm. Hrrmm!
I'm going to be the tavern keeper so I can have all the cider.
I'd be a shepherd! I love sheep. They're like clouds with legs.
I want to be an archer! I can already hit the barn. It's a big barn.
I'm going to be a tailor and make clothes for the cats.
When I'm big I'll be a scholar and know everything about everything.
I help my dad at work. I hold things. Very important job.
I want to be a mason and build a castle. A real one.
I'll be a cleric and make potions that turn things blue.
I'm going to work so hard and then take a nap. Like the nitwit.
Being a grown-up looks hard. You have to work AND be tired.
I made a workstation out of a box. It's a cookie workstation.
I'm going to be a carpenter! I already made a stick. It's a wooden stick.
I'd be a toolsmith and make a pickaxe made of cake.
I want to be everything! Can I be everything?
Grown-ups go to work and come home smelly. I can't wait!
I'll be a fletcher and make arrows out of chicken feathers! The chickens won't like that.
I'm going to be an adventurer like you. That's a job, right?
I'd be a leatherworker and make boots for every animal in the village.
I'm going to be a butcher. No, wait, I like the animals. A vegetable butcher!
I watched the smith hammer all morning. Clang clang! I want to clang!
When I'm big, I'll have a workstation right next to the bell.
I already know how to sweep. That's basically a job.
I'll be a painter and paint your portrait. You'll be very handsome. Or pretty. Very square.
My dream job is cookie taster.
I want to work at the market selling honey cakes. And eating the leftovers.
I'm going to be the bell ringer! Ding dong! Is that a job?
I'll be a guard and protect everyone. Even the cranky ones.
Every day I'm going to work and then play. Work then play. Perfect.
When I'm a farmer, I'll grow carrots for every rabbit in the world.
I'm learning about stars so I can be an astronomer. What's an astronomer?
baby.adventure: Did you fight a dragon? Was it big? Was it this big? Bigger?
Tell me about the scariest monster you ever saw!
Have you been to the bottom of the ocean? Are there mermaids?
When I'm bigger, I'm going on an adventure. Just like you!
Did you find treasure? Real treasure? Gold and diamonds?
Is it true that endermen steal blocks? Why do they want blocks?
I went on an adventure to the end of the garden. I found a snail.
Have you ever ridden a horse? A really fast one?
What's the farthest you've ever walked? Farther than the well?
Do zombies have friends? Do they play together?
I want to see a polar bear! Are they soft? Can you hug them?
Have you been in a cave? Is it dark? Are there bats? I love bats!
Did you sleep outside? Under the stars? With the monsters?
I went exploring in the barn. I found three eggs and a very angry chicken.
Is the Nether hot like soup? Or hot like the sun?
Have you seen a panda? I want to see a panda more than anything!
I'm going to sail a boat across the whole ocean someday.
Did you ever get lost? What did you do?
I want to find a dungeon. A friendly one. With friendly skeletons.
Have you been to the End? Is it really the end? What's after the end?
I made a treasure map of the village. X marks the cookie jar.
Can you take me on an adventure? Just a little one? To the river?
Are there villages like ours far away? With kids like me?
I want to climb the biggest mountain and wave at everyone.
I found a cave behind the waterfall! Okay, it's a dent in the rock. But it's MY cave.
Have you ever met a wandering trader's llama? Did it spit at you?
I'm going to tame a wolf and call him Sir Woofington.
Tell me a story about your adventures. A long one!
When I grow up I'll explore the whole world and come back and tell you about it.
Is it scary being an adventurer? I'd be brave. Mostly.
Have you seen the ocean? Is it blue all the way down?
I want to ride a pig! With a saddle! Into battle!
Did you ever fight a creeper? Did it go boom? Did you go boom?
I'm saving my pebbles for a big adventure. Pebbles are very useful.
Do you have a sword? Can I see? Ooh! Shiny!
Have you been to the jungle? Are there monkeys? There should be monkeys.
I went on an adventure in my dreams. I flew to the moon on a chicken.
What's the coolest thing you ever found?
I want to see snow! Lots of snow! A whole mountain of snow!
Promise you'll take me exploring when I'm grown up!
Is the world flat? My brother says it's square. Like everything.
I heard there's a mansion full of baddies in the forest. Did you go in?
I want to find a geode. They're like rocks with sparkly insides!
Do fish sleep? Have you seen a fish sleep?
When I go adventuring I'm bringing my whole rock collection.
baby.joke: Why did the chicken cross the road? To get to the other side! Hee hee!
Knock knock! Who's there? Banana. Banana who? Knock knock! Who's there? Orange. Orange you glad I didn't say banana!
What do you call a cow with no legs? Ground beef! My uncle told me that one.
Why did the cookie cry? Because its mother was a wafer so long! Hee!
What's brown and sticky? A stick! Ha ha ha!
Why can't a nose be twelve inches long? Because then it'd be a foot!
What do you call a sleeping dinosaur? A dino-snore! Zzzzz!
Why did the teddy bear say no to dessert? It was stuffed! Hee hee!
What's a pig's favorite color? Mud! Okay, mud's not a color. It should be.
Knock knock! Who's there? Boo. Boo who? Don't cry! It's just me!
Why do cows wear bells? Because their horns don't work! Moo!
What do you call a funny chicken? A comedi-hen!
Why did the zombie go to school? To get smarter! Grrr! Brains!
What do you call a fish with no eye? A fsh! Fsh! Get it?
Why did the golem cross the road? To pick up the flower! It's true, I saw it!
Knock knock! Who's there? Cow says. Cow says who? No silly, cow says MOO!
What do you call a bear with no ears? B! Hee hee!
Why are frogs so happy? They eat whatever bugs them!
What did the sheep say to the other sheep? Baaa! That's it. That's the joke. Baaa!
Why don't skeletons go to parties? They have no BODY to go with! Hahaha!
What has four legs and goes boo? A cow with a cold!
What's the fastest vegetable? A runner bean! Zoom!
Why did the banana go to the doctor? It wasn't peeling well!
What do you call a rabbit that tells jokes? A funny bunny! Hop hop!
Knock knock! Who's there? Lettuce. Lettuce who? Lettuce in, it's cold!
Why did the egg hide? It was a little chicken!
What do you call a duck that gets all A's? A wise quacker!
What do you call a cat that's a beach? A sandy claws! Hee hee!
Why did the creeper cross the road? Hssssss! BOOM! ...I don't know the end.
What's a ghost's favorite fruit? Boo-berries!
What's a pirate's favorite animal? An aaaaardvark! Arrr!
Why couldn't the pony sing? It was a little horse!
Why did the bee go to school? To get a little buzz! Bzzz!
What's a snake's favorite subject? Hiss-tory!
What do you get when you cross a snowman and a vampire? Frostbite! Grrr!
Knock knock! Who's there? Interrupting cow. Interrupting c- MOO!
Why did the tomato go red? It saw the salad dressing! Hee!
What's a cat's favorite dessert? Mice cream!
I told the golem a joke. It didn't laugh. Golems don't have funny bones.
What do you call a dog that does magic? A Labracadabrador! My favorite!
baby.weather.rain: Rain! Puddles! I'm going to jump in every single one!
Mum says I have to stay inside. The puddles are calling me!
I caught a raindrop on my tongue! It tasted like sky!
The worms are coming out! Hello, worms!
Rain sounds like a hundred tiny drums.
I'm a frog! Ribbit! Frogs love rain!
I made a boat out of a leaf and it sailed down the path!
I'm all wet and I don't even care!
The rain made a river in the road! It's MY river.
When it rains, the flowers drink. Glug glug glug.
baby.weather.thunder: The thunder's so loud! Is the sky angry?
I'm not scared of thunder. I'm just hiding under the table for fun.
Every time it flashes, I count! One, two, BOOM!
My dog is hiding under my bed. I'm hiding with him.
Is lightning hot? It looks hot.
Mum says thunder is just the clouds bumping heads.
I hope the golem's okay out there.
I'm being brave. Look how brave I'm being. Eek!
When it booms, I squeeze my cat. She doesn't like it.
I want the storm to stop so I can go play.
baby.weather.snow: SNOW! It's snowing! Snow snow snow!
I'm going to build a snow golem! A really big one!
I made a snow angel! Look! It's me but flat!
My nose is cold but I don't care! Snow!
Can I eat the snow? Mum says no. I already did.
I threw a snowball at my brother and he threw one back. War!
The snow's so deep it's up to my tummy!
Everything's white and sparkly! It's like the world's covered in sugar!
I want to slide down the hill on a boat! Is that allowed?
I wish it snowed every day forever!
baby.weather.clearing: Did you see the rainbow? I'm going to find the end of it!
Everything smells like wet grass! I love it!
The snails are out! I'm racing them.
I'm going to splash in every puddle before they dry up!
baby.weather.hot: It's so hot! I want to swim in the river!
My ice melted. Well, my snowball. It was a snowball from yesterday.
I'm hiding in the shade with the cats.
Can we have cold milk? It's so hot!
The sand's too hot for my feet! Ouch! Ouch!
I'm going to dig a hole and sit in it. It's cooler in holes.
baby.routine.wake: I had the best dream. There were cookies. Big ones.
I'm still sleepy. But I don't want to miss anything!
Morning! Is breakfast ready? Is it porridge?
I woke up before everyone! Even the rooster!
baby.routine.breakfast: I'm eating breakfast! It's porridge. With honey!
I have a milk mustache. Look!
Breakfast is my favorite meal. Then lunch. Then supper. Then snacks.
I ate all my bread and the crusts. The crusts make you brave!
Mum says I have to finish breakfast before I can play. I'm eating SO fast.
Can I have cookies for breakfast? No? Okay. Porridge.
baby.routine.play: We're playing tag! You're it! No tag-backs!
I'm hiding! Count to ten! No, twenty!
We're building a fort out of hay! Want to come in? Password's potato.
I'm a dragon! Rawr! I'm going to eat the village! Not really. Rawr!
Race you to the bell! Go!
We're playing village and I'm the golem. Clank! Clank!
I'm on a quest to find the shiniest pebble in the whole world!
Look at me jump! I'm jumping!
baby.routine.lessons: We're doing lessons! I'm learning about bees!
Shh, the teacher's talking. She's telling us about the stars.
I know my letters! A, B, C... um... bell!
We learned that sheep can be different colors! I want a purple one!
I'm learning numbers. Sixty-four is a whole stack!
Lessons are fun today. We're drawing maps!
baby.routine.lunch_home: I'm having lunch at home! Bread and cheese!
Mum made soup. I'm blowing on it. Whoosh!
Lunch! I'm so hungry I could eat a whole cow. A small one.
I'm eating my carrots first so I can have dessert.
Lunch is short! I have to eat fast and go play!
I shared my lunch with the cat. She ate the cheese.
baby.routine.market: It's Market Day! I got a copper! I'm buying a honey cake!
There are so many stalls! I want everything!
Market Day is the best day! There's music and cake!
I saw a llama at the market! It looked at me funny!
I traded my best pebble for a ribbon. Good trade!
Mum says I can have ONE treat. I'm choosing very carefully.
baby.routine.supper: It's supper time! We're having stew. We're always having stew.
I have to eat my vegetables. I'm hiding them under my bread.
Supper with everyone is the best!
I'm so full! My tummy is round like a pumpkin!
Dad told a funny story at supper. Milk came out my nose!
After supper I get a story. Then bed. Booo, bed.
baby.routine.evening: I'm getting ready for bed. Do I have to?
Mum's reading me a story. It's about a brave chicken.
I'm in my pajamas. They have bells on them!
The stars are coming out! I'm counting them! One, two, lots!
I'm not tired. I'm just resting my eyes. Very hard.
Can I stay up five more minutes? Please? Five?
baby.routine.sleep: I'm supposed to be asleep. Shh, don't tell!
I'm so sleepy... but I want to talk to you...
Goodnight! Will you be here tomorrow?
I sleep with my wooden sword. In case of monsters.
Night night! Don't let the spiders bite!
baby.routine.shelter: I have to stay inside because of the rain. Boooring!
I'm watching the rain from the window. Drip drip drip.
Can I go out? Just for one puddle? Please?
I'm building a fort out of blankets until the rain stops.
The rain's making music on the roof!
I'm drawing pictures of rainbows to make the rain stop.
baby.routine.storm: I'm hiding! The thunder's too loud!
Mum's holding my hand. I'm not scared. She is. A little.
The lightning made the whole room white!
I'm under the table with my dog. We're very brave.
When will the storm stop? Soon? Now? Now?
I'm counting the booms. Seven so far!
baby.routine.snowed_in: We're stuck inside because of the snow! Can we go play in it?
I'm warming my toes by the fire. They're toasty now!
Mum made hot cocoa! It's the best thing ever!
I'm drawing snowflakes on the frosty window!
The snow's so high it's covering the door!
I want to go out and make a snow golem!
baby.routine.rain_walk: I'm splashing in puddles! Splash! Splash!
I'm a duck! Quack! Ducks love rain!
I'm soaking wet! Mum's going to be so mad. Worth it!
Look how big this puddle is! It's an ocean!
I'm dancing in the rain! Come dance!
baby.routine.snow_play: I'm building a snow golem! He needs a pumpkin head!
I made a snow angel! It's the best one ever!
I'm sliding on the ice! Wheee! Ow. Wheee!
My mittens are soaked but I don't care!
I'm making a snow fort! It's going to be HUGE!
baby.time.dawn: It's so early! The roosters are still yawning.
The sky's pink! Like a strawberry!
Shh, everyone's still asleep. Except me!
I got up to see the sunrise! It was worth it!
baby.time.morning: I've already found two beetles and a snail this morning!
The morning sun is warm on my face!
It's morning! The whole day is ahead! So much playing to do!
baby.time.noon: The sun's right on top of us! I can't find my shadow!
Noon means lunch, and lunch means food!
I'm hungry. Are you hungry? I'm always hungry.
baby.time.afternoon: The afternoon's the best for playing tag!
I'm not tired! Okay, a little tired.
The shadows are getting long! Mine's taller than me!
Afternoon is when the cats nap. I don't nap. I'm too busy.
baby.time.evening: The sun's going down! It's all orange!
Mum says I have to come in soon. Five more minutes!
The fireflies are coming out! I'm going to catch one!
It's getting dark! Time for stories!
baby.time.night: I'm supposed to be in bed! Shh!
The stars are out! I'm making wishes on them!
Night is spooky. I like spooky. A little.
Are there monsters out there? The golem will protect us!
baby.time.late: I can't sleep! There's too much thinking in my head.
It's so late! I've never been up this late! I'm so grown up!
I heard a noise. Was it a ghost? It was probably the cat.
I'm only up because I needed water. And to see the moon.
baby.market: It's Market Day! Everything smells like honey cake!
Mum gave me a copper to spend. I'm going to spend it so carefully.
There's a juggler at the market! Well, the bard juggling apples. Badly.
I saw so many stalls! Toys and ribbons and cakes!
On Market Day nobody makes me do chores!
I want to buy a wooden sword. And a cake. And a llama.
deed.raid_defended.seen: I watched you from behind the well when the raiders came. You didn't back down once.
I saw you holding the line by the houses. I've never seen anyone move like that.
You were out there in the thick of it while the rest of us hid. I saw every swing.
I saw the raiders fall back from you. I'll remember that sight for a long time.
I peeked through the shutters during the raid. You were the only thing standing between them and us.
deed.raid_defended.heard: Word is you stood up to the raiders when they came. Thank you, {player}.
{teller} says you fought off the raiders practically by yourself. Is that true?
Everyone's saying you were right in the middle of it when the raiders came through.
I was hiding in the cellar during the raid, but I heard all about you afterwards.
They tell me you kept the raiders away from the houses. That's a debt the whole village owes you.
deed.raid_won.seen: I saw the last raider fall, and I saw who was standing at the end of it. You!
I watched the whole thing. When the raid broke, I cried and cheered at the same time.
I saw you win it. The bell rang, the raiders were gone, and there you were.
I was there when it ended. I've never heard {village} so loud, or so happy.
I saw you send the whole raid packing. I still can't quite believe it.
deed.raid_won.heard: You're the one who beat the raid! {teller} hasn't stopped talking about it.
The whole village is saying you won the day when the raiders came. Thank you.
I heard the raid's over and it's thanks to you. {village} is still standing because of you.
News travels fast here. Raid beaten, village safe, and your name on everyone's lips.
They say you saw off the whole raid. I'd shake your hand, but I'd like to hug you instead.
deed.revived.seen: I saw you kneel down beside {victim} and bring them back. I was shaking the whole time.
You're the one who brought {victim} round! I saw it with my own eyes.
I watched you work on {victim} when everyone else had frozen. Thank you.
I saw the whole thing. One moment I thought we'd lost them, and then you were there.
I was right there when you brought them back. I didn't know what to do. You did.
deed.revived.heard: You're the one who carried {victim} back from the brink! {teller} told me everything.
Is it true you brought {victim} round when nobody else could?
I heard what you did for {victim}. The whole village has heard, I think.
{teller} says you kept someone breathing when it mattered most. Thank you, {player}.
Word is you saved a life here. I just wanted you to know people noticed.
deed.revived.self: You're the one who brought me back. I don't remember much, only your face. Thank you.
They tell me I was very nearly gone, and that you wouldn't let me go. I owe you everything.
I woke up and the first thing I saw was you. I'll never forget that.
Thank you for not giving up on me. I mean it, {player}. Every day from now on is partly yours.
deed.revived.family: You saved my {kin} {victim}. I don't have the words. I just don't.
You're the one who brought {victim} back to us. Our door is always open to you.
My {kin} is alive because of you. Please, come and eat with us some time.
Our family nearly lost someone, and you wouldn't let it happen. Thank you, {player}.
deed.bandaged.seen: I saw you patch up {victim}. Gentle hands, for an adventurer.
I watched you wrap that bandage. You've done that before, haven't you?
I saw you stop to tend someone who was hurt. Not everyone stops.
You knelt right down in the dirt to see to {victim}. I saw. That was kind.
I saw you bandage someone up as calm as anything. Thank you for that.
deed.bandaged.heard: {teller} says you bandaged {victim} up when they were hurt. Thank you.
I heard you stopped to tend somebody who'd been hurt. That's the right sort of person.
Word is you've been patching people up around here. Our apothecary will be jealous.
Somebody told me you bandaged {victim}. Good. They'd have tried to walk it off.
I heard you looked after someone who was hurt. Thank you, {player}.
deed.bandaged.self: You patched me up when I was hurt. It still stings, but it's healing well. Thank you.
Look, the bandage held! You've got a steady hand, {player}.
Thank you for looking after me when I was down. I felt very small just then.
I'm on my feet again, and that's partly your doing. Thank you.
deed.bandaged.family: You tended to my {kin} when they were hurt. Thank you for that.
{victim} told us you bandaged them up. We're grateful, all of us.
Thank you for helping my {kin}. That sort of thing means a great deal in a family.
You looked after one of ours. We won't forget it.
deed.saved_from_monster.seen: I saw that monster go for {victim}, and I saw you get there first.
I watched you cut it down before it could reach {victim}. My heart's still pounding.
I saw what you did out there. One more second and it would have been too late.
I saw you jump in between that thing and one of ours. Thank you, {player}.
I was too far away to help, but I saw you get there in time. I've never been so glad to see anyone.
deed.saved_from_monster.heard: {teller} says a monster went after {victim} and you dealt with it. Thank you.
I heard you saved someone from a monster at the edge of the village.
Word is you got between {victim} and something nasty. That took nerve.
Everyone's saying you saved one of ours from a monster. Is that true? It is, isn't it?
I heard a monster nearly had someone, and then you happened to it. Good.
deed.saved_from_monster.self: That monster would have had me if you hadn't come. Thank you, {player}. Truly.
I still see it when I close my eyes. And then I see you, and it's all right.
You saved me out there. I didn't even get the chance to scream.
I owe you my life. I'm not exaggerating, for once.
deed.saved_from_monster.family: You saved my {kin} from that monster. I'll be grateful to you for the rest of my days.
{victim} came home shaking and told us all about you. Thank you, thank you.
You stood between my {kin} and that monster. There's nothing I wouldn't do for you now.
Our family owes you, {player}. If you ever need anything, you come to us first.
deed.rescued_companion.seen: I saw you go back for {victim} out there. You didn't leave them behind.
I watched you help {victim} up when they were down. That's a real companion.
I saw you turn round for your friend instead of running. Good on you.
I saw you carry {victim} out of trouble. They're lucky to travel with you.
I saw you get your companion back on their feet. I like that about you.
deed.rescued_companion.heard: {teller} says {victim} went down on the road and you went back for them.
I heard you never leave a friend behind on your travels. That's how it should be.
Word is you saved {victim} out in the wilds. They're telling everyone.
I heard you picked your companion up when they fell. I'd travel with you, then.
They say you went back for your friend when it would have been easier not to.
deed.rescued_companion.self: You came back for me out there. I thought I was done for, and then there you were.
Thank you for getting me back on my feet. I'll watch your back next time, I promise.
I went down and you didn't leave me. I won't forget that, {player}.
You're a proper friend. Not many would have turned round for me.
deed.rescued_companion.family: You brought my {kin} home safe from your travels. Thank you for looking after them.
{victim} says you came back for them when they fell. We're so grateful.
Thank you for not leaving my {kin} out there. I'd never have forgiven the road.
You looked after one of ours out in the wilds. That means everything to us.
deed.notice_answered.seen: I saw you take that notice down off the board. Thank you for helping.
I saw you sorting out one of the notices. You're getting to be a regular helper.
I watched you bring the reward home. Well earned, I'd say.
I saw you hand it over to {victim}. They looked so relieved.
I saw you turn in a notice. The board has a friend in you.
deed.notice_answered.heard: {teller} says you answered {victim}'s notice. That was good of you.
I heard you took care of a notice off the board. People notice that sort of thing.
Word is you've been helping folk through the notice board. Thank you.
I heard you sorted out {victim}'s trouble. You're becoming quite the neighbor.
Somebody's notice came down and everyone says it was you. Thank you, {player}.
deed.notice_answered.self: I'm still glad you answered my notice. Things have been so much easier since.
I keep thinking about the help you gave me. Thank you again, {player}.
You answered when I asked for help. I won't forget who did.
My notice is long gone from the board, but I still remember who took it down.
deed.notice_answered.family: You answered my {kin}'s notice. Thank you for helping our family.
{victim} told us you sorted things out for them. We're grateful.
Thank you for helping my {kin}. You've made our house a happier one.
You took on {victim}'s notice. That makes you a friend of the family.
deed.birthday_gift.seen: I saw {victim}'s face when you gave them that birthday present. You picked well!
I saw you bring a birthday gift for {victim}. They lit up like a lantern.
I watched {victim} open your present. I don't think I've seen them that happy all year.
I saw you remember a birthday. Most travelers don't even know what day it is.
I saw that gift you gave. Perfect choice. How did you know?
deed.birthday_gift.heard: {teller} says you gave {victim} the perfect birthday present. How thoughtful!
I heard you remembered {victim}'s birthday. That's the sort of thing that matters here.
Word is you found just the right birthday gift. You must listen when people talk.
I heard about the birthday present. {victim} is still showing everybody.
Someone told me you brought a lovely birthday gift. You're a thoughtful one, {player}.
deed.birthday_gift.self: I'm still thinking about the present you gave me for my birthday. It was perfect.
You remembered my birthday! And you knew exactly what I'd love. Thank you.
I keep your birthday gift right where I can see it. It makes me smile every morning.
Nobody's ever picked a present for me that well. Thank you, {player}.
deed.birthday_gift.family: You gave my {kin} the loveliest birthday present. They haven't stopped talking about it.
{victim} showed us your birthday gift. You've made our whole family smile.
Thank you for remembering my {kin}'s birthday. That was a kindness we noticed.
The gift you gave {victim} is on our mantelpiece now. Pride of place.
deed.pet_kindness.seen: I saw you give {victim}'s pet a fuss. It's been strutting about ever since.
I saw you stop and pat that little animal. Kind hands are worth noticing.
I watched you share a treat with one of the village pets. It's your friend for life now.
I saw you kneel down to say hello to {victim}'s pet. That made my day.
I saw you being sweet to one of our animals. You're a good sort.
deed.pet_kindness.heard: {teller} says you've been spoiling {victim}'s pet with treats. Good.
I heard the village pets have taken a liking to you. Animals know a good heart.
Word is you never walk past a pet without a pat. I like that in a person.
I heard you made friends with {victim}'s pet. That's no small thing. It's very picky.
Somebody told me the animals here all come running when you walk by.
deed.pet_kindness.self: My pet adores you, you know. It waits by the door when it hears you coming.
Thank you for being so kind to my pet. It's had a spring in its step all day.
You've been feeding my pet treats, haven't you? It's getting round. I don't mind.
My little one was so happy after you gave it a fuss. Thank you, {player}.
deed.pet_kindness.family: You've been kind to our family's pet. It talks about you. Well. It wags about you.
{victim} says you made a fuss of our pet. Thank you, it loves attention.
Our pet has a new favorite person, and it's you. My {kin} is a little jealous.
Thank you for being gentle with our animal. A family's pet is part of the family.
deed.hit_resident.seen: I saw you hit {victim}. I don't know what happened between you, but I saw it.
I saw what you did to {victim}. We don't do that here, {player}.
I was standing right there when you struck {victim}. I haven't forgotten.
I saw you raise your hand to one of ours. I'm keeping my distance for a bit.
I saw that. Hitting folk in their own village? I expected better of you.
deed.hit_resident.heard: {teller} says you hit {victim}. Tell me that isn't true.
I heard you struck one of our neighbors. That's not how you make friends in {village}.
Word is you've been knocking people about. I'd rather it stopped, thank you.
I heard what happened with {victim}. People are talking, and not kindly.
Someone told me you hit one of us. I'm going to need a while before I trust you again.
deed.hit_resident.self: You hit me. I haven't forgotten it, even if you have.
I've still got the bruise, you know. I'd like an apology, not a hello.
Why did you hit me? I've gone over it a hundred times and I still don't understand.
Please keep your hands to yourself around me from now on.
deed.hit_resident.family: You hit my {kin}. I'm being polite to you because I was raised to be.
{victim} came home bruised and told us who did it. Don't expect a warm welcome at our house.
You struck one of my family. I'd think very hard before doing that again.
I know what you did to my {kin}. I just wanted you to know that I know.
deed.knocked_out_resident.seen: I saw you put {victim} on the ground. I thought they'd never get up again.
I saw {victim} go down, and I saw who did it. It was you.
I watched you beat {victim} until they fell. I still feel sick about it.
I saw what you did. If the apothecary hadn't come, I don't know what would have happened.
I was there when you knocked one of us down cold. I won't pretend I wasn't.
deed.knocked_out_resident.heard: {teller} says you beat {victim} so badly they had to be carried to the cot.
I heard someone was knocked senseless, and everyone says it was you.

Not today. Maybe not tomorrow. But I'm listening.
deed.apology.accept.child: Okay! I forgive you! Pinky promise you won't do it again?
You said sorry! Mum says that makes it all right. So it's all right!
Okay. I'm not cross any more. Want to play?
I forgive you! But you have to give me a piggyback. That's the rule.
You said sorry properly! I'll tell everyone you're nice again.
Okay! Friends again! Friends forever, actually.
I accept your sorry! I've never accepted a sorry before. It feels nice.
Okay. Sorry is a magic word. Now everything is fixed.
deed.apology.cool.child: Hmm. I'm still a bit cross. Say it again tomorrow.
Mum says I don't have to forgive you yet. So I'm not. Yet.
I'm thinking about it. Thinking takes a long time.
You have to say sorry a lot more times. Like, a hundred.
Not yet. I'm still sulking. Sulking is important.
deed.apology.remembered: You said sorry, and you meant it. That counts for a lot round here.
I haven't forgotten your apology. Water under the bridge, {player}.
We had our trouble, you and I. You put it right. I respect that.
You owned up when you didn't have to. I think better of you for it.
Remember when you said sorry? I do. It took courage.
There was a rough patch between us, but you mended it. Good.
I've told the others you apologized. Folk here believe in second chances.
Every time I see you, I remember the apology more than the trouble. That's a good sign.
deed.kept.revived.self: The day I nearly died, {player} knelt in the dirt and stayed with me until I breathed again.
{player} brought me back when I was nearly gone.
I woke on the ground with {player} kneeling beside me. I'm alive because of them.
{player} wouldn't let me go. I owe them every day since.
deed.kept.revived.family: Our family still has {victim}, and that is because of {player}.
When {victim} was nearly lost, {player} saved them. Our family will never forget it.
{player} kept my {kin} breathing when it mattered most.
deed.kept.saved_from_monster.self: I was nearly lost to a monster in {village}. {player} saved me.
{player} saved me from a monster at the edge of {village}.
A monster nearly had me, and {player} got there first.
{player} stood between me and the dark. I'll remember it always.
deed.kept.saved_from_monster.family: When a monster came for {victim}, {player} was there. We are all grateful.
A monster went for {victim}, and {player} stopped it. Our family owes them.
{player} saved my {kin}. I'll be grateful for the rest of my days.
deed.kept.rescued_companion.self: Out on the road, when I could go no further, {player} carried me home.
{player} came back for me when I fell on the road.
I went down far from home, and {player} didn't leave me there.
{player} picked me up when I couldn't stand. A true companion.
deed.kept.rescued_companion.family: {player} looked after {victim} out in the wilds and brought them home to us.
{player} brought my {kin} {victim} home safe from the wilds.
When {victim} fell on the road, {player} went back for them.
{player} didn't leave my {kin} behind. We remember that.
greet.unwelcome: Oh. It's you. What do you want?
You've got a nerve, showing your face in {village}.
I'll talk to you. I won't enjoy it.
Make it quick, {player}. People are watching.
I've nothing to say to you that you'd like to hear.
You're not welcome here, you know. Not after everything.
Folk here remember what you did. So do I.
I'm only answering because my mother raised me polite.
Keep your hands where I can see them, please.
If you've come to make amends, I'm listening. Otherwise, I'm busy.
The whole village knows your name now, {player}. Not in a good way.
greet.unwelcome.warmhearted: I'd usually offer you tea. Not today, {player}.
I want to be kind to you. You're making it very hard.
My door's open to everyone. Almost everyone. Just now, not you.
greet.unwelcome.thoughtful: I've thought a lot about you lately. None of it was pleasant.
What do you want, {player}? I'm asking honestly.
I keep hoping you'll give me a reason to think better of you.
greet.unwelcome.playful: Oh look, it's the village villain. No jokes for you today.
Hello, trouble. And I don't mean the fun sort.
I'd make a joke, but nobody here is laughing about you.
greet.unwelcome.adventurous: I've met bandits on the road with better manners than you've shown here.
Out in the wilds, folk like you get left behind. Just so you know.
What brings you back? Not more trouble, I hope.
greet.unwelcome.meticulous: I've kept count of everything you've done here. The list isn't short.
I've noted that you're here. I note everything.
greet.unwelcome.steadfast: I'll stand here and hear you out. That's more than you've earned.
I don't hold grudges for ever. But I hold them for a while.
Say what you came to say.
greet.unwelcome.imaginative: In every story the village tells now, you're the one in the dark cloak.
I used to imagine you as a hero. My imagination has changed its mind.
You've the look of a cautionary tale about you today.
greet.unwelcome.pragmatic: Let's not waste each other's time. What do you need?
I'll trade with you, because emeralds are emeralds. Don't expect more than that.
You know nobody wants you here, right? Just checking.
greet.unwelcome.curious: I'm curious about lots of things. Why you're still here is one of them.
What makes a person do what you've done? I still can't work it out.
You're back? Why? I really want to know.
greet.unwelcome.protective: Stay away from my family, {player}. I mean it.
Don't make me ask you to leave.
greet.unwelcome.gentle: Oh. Please don't come too close.
I'm sorry, I'm a little frightened of you.
baby.greet.unwelcome: Mum says I'm not allowed to talk to you.
You're the mean one. Everybody says so.
I'm not scared of you! ...I'm a bit scared of you.
Go away! I'm guarding this bit of the village.
Are you going to say sorry? You should say sorry.
I'm not supposed to be near you. Bye!
Everyone's cross with you. Even the chickens.
You have to be nice for a REALLY long time now.
chat.unwelcome: How's my day? Better before you turned up, if I'm honest.
I don't really want to chat with you, {player}.
People will talk if they see me being friendly with you. I'd rather they didn't.
I've nothing to share with you. Not today.
If you want things to go back to how they were, you'll have to earn it.
My day is my business. Yours seems to be trouble.
I'm not one to hold a grudge for ever. But it hasn't been for ever yet.
Maybe try saying sorry to the people you hurt. Then we'll talk.
You'll find {village} a lot friendlier when you start being friendlier to it.
Good deeds wash out bad ones, slowly. You'd better get started.
notice.unwelcome: There's nothing on that board for you, {player}. Nobody wants your help just now.
I wouldn't ask you to carry a letter, let alone my troubles.
We'll find somebody else for our notices, thank you.
The board's for friends of the village. You're not one at the moment.
Help? From you? Not until folk can trust you again.
Put things right with the village first. Then maybe there'll be a notice for you.
tale.legend: My grandad swore {legend} lives in {legend_where} and only bites {legend_when}. He also swore he once arm-wrestled a bear, so make of that what you will.
They say {legend} is out there in {legend_where}, waiting. It bites {legend_when}, if it bites at all. Most folk who go looking come home with wet boots and a story.

My cousin swears she had {legend} on her line out in {legend_where}. Snapped the line, the rod and very nearly her arm. She tells it differently every time, but the arm's always in it. The trick, she says, is to go {legend_when}.

A fellow at the tavern last night, three ciders in, told everyone {legend} lives in {legend_where} and bites {legend_when}. Then he fell off his stool. I've been thinking about it all day. The fish, not the stool.
If you ever want to catch {legend}, they say you look in {legend_where}, {legend_when}. And you bring a bigger net than you think. Then a bigger one than that.
My uncle lost a boot to {legend}. Pulled clean off his foot, he says, out in {legend_where}. He still goes back {legend_when} to look for it. The boot, he says. Nobody believes that either.
You know the story of {legend}? Lives in {legend_where}. Bites {legend_when}. Has eaten, depending on who's telling it, a goose, a goat or a tax collector.
My gran would never go near {legend_where} {legend_when}. "That's when {legend} is hungry," she'd say. She went every other time, mind. She was a practical woman.
A wandering trader swore he'd seen {legend} with his own two eyes, out in {legend_where}. It bites {legend_when}, he said. Then he tried to sell me a lucky spoon, so I'm still weighing it up.
Some say {legend} is just a story to keep children from wandering off. But my neighbor goes to {legend_where} {legend_when} and comes home pale, and she's not a woman who frightens easily.
They say {legend} only shows itself {legend_when}, and only to someone with a patient heart and a strong line. That's why nobody in {village} has seen it. We're impatient, and we buy cheap line.
Every angler in {village} has a theory about {legend}. Mine is that it lives in {legend_where} and bites {legend_when}. Mine is also the right one.
I heard {legend} is so old it remembers when the mountains were hills. It lives in {legend_where}, rises {legend_when}, and has never once been caught. Not properly.
The miller's wife says her father fished for {legend} his whole life. He'd go out to {legend_where} {legend_when}, year after year. Hooked it once. Says it looked right at him. Then it left.
They say if you want {legend}, you wait by {legend_where} {legend_when} and don't say a word. My brother tried it. He lasted about a minute. He's a talker.

My grandmother used to frighten us with {legend}. "It lives in {legend_where}," she'd say, "and it comes up {legend_when}, looking for children who won't eat their greens." I ate every green I was ever given.
I don't believe in {legend}. I don't. But I'll tell you this: I don't go near {legend_where} {legend_when}. No reason. I just don't.
Somebody's grandfather's friend caught {legend} once, or so the story goes. It lives in {legend_where} and bites {legend_when}, he said, and it took four oxen to land it. Then it got away anyway.
A fish as long as a cart, with eyes like dinner plates. That's {legend}, if you believe the stories. It's meant to lurk in {legend_where} and bite {legend_when}. I believe about half.
The tavern keeper says {legend} is real. Their grandmother's cousin used to see it in {legend_where} {legend_when}. Of course, the tavern keeper also says the cider's watered down for our own good.
I'll tell you a secret if you promise not to spread it: {legend} bites {legend_when}. In {legend_where}. Now you know as much as I do, which isn't much.
My aunt says the trick with {legend} is the bait. Go to {legend_where} {legend_when} with a fresh loaf, a lump of cheese and something you love. It only takes the last one. That's the cruel part.
Two fishermen had a shouting match over {legend} last Market Day. One said it bites {legend_when}. The other said nonsense, it bites {legend_when}. It took them an hour to notice.
Folk say {legend} has been swimming in {legend_where} since before {village} had a name. It comes up {legend_when} to see if we're still here. We are. It always looks a bit disappointed.
You'll hear a lot of nonsense about {legend}. Some say it can talk. Some say it grants wishes. The only bit everyone agrees on is that it bites {legend_when}, somewhere in {legend_where}.
{neighbor} has been after {legend} since they were small. Off to {legend_where} {legend_when}, regular as the bell. Never caught it. Says the looking is the good part.

There's a song about {legend}. Fifteen verses, fourteen of them about how big it is. The last one says it lives in {legend_where} and bites {legend_when}, but nobody's ever stayed awake long enough to hear it.
Half of {village} says {legend} is a bedtime story. The other half go to {legend_where} {legend_when} and sit very still. I know which half has the better stories.
An old sailor swore to me that {legend} swallowed his whole boat, then spat it back out because it didn't care for his cooking. Lives in {legend_where}, he said. Bites {legend_when}. Avoid his stew.

My great-grandad's rod still hangs over our hearth, snapped clean in half. He said {legend} did it, out in {legend_where}. He'd only fish for it {legend_when}, and he made the whole family come along for luck.
The children dare each other to go to {legend_where} {legend_when} and shout for {legend}. None of them ever do. Neither would I, and I'm a grown-up.
{friend} swears {legend} winked at them from the water in {legend_where}. That's the trouble with fishing {legend_when}: you start seeing things. Or the fish starts winking. One of the two.
Nobody believes my sister caught a glimpse of {legend}. Mostly because she's my sister. But she does go to {legend_where} {legend_when}, and she does come home with a very funny look on her face.
The old ones say {legend} isn't a fish at all. It's a wish with fins. It swims in {legend_where} and rises {legend_when}, and only for someone who's stopped hoping it will.
Ask ten fishermen about {legend} and you'll get ten different stories. Ask them where and when, though, and nine say the same thing: {legend_where}, {legend_when}. The tenth changes the subject.

The old mason kept a tally on his door, one mark for every time he went after {legend}. Hundreds of marks. He'd go to {legend_where} {legend_when}, just like the stories said. Under the last mark he carved "Nearly."

They reckon {legend} has outlived every angler who ever tried for it. It sits in {legend_where} and comes up {legend_when}, just to see who's new. Then it goes back down, laughing. Fish can laugh. Ask anyone who's lost one.
The cleric says there's no such thing as {legend}. But I've noticed the cleric takes a rod to {legend_where} {legend_when}, and nowhere else, ever.
My mother's people had a saying: "Where {legend} swims, keep your toes in your boots." It swims in {legend_where}, mind, and gets bold {legend_when}. I keep my toes well in.
The fisherman's dog won't go near {legend_where} {legend_when}. Sits down and whines. Folk say it can smell {legend}. I'd take that dog's word over most people's.
tale.legend.warmhearted: I worry about anyone who goes after {legend}. They say it bites {legend_when}, out in {legend_where}. If you go, take a warm scarf and a pie. I'll make the pie.
My old dad chased {legend} for years. He'd go to {legend_where} {legend_when} and come home soaked and happy, and there'd always be soup on for him. I still make too much soup.
If you're set on finding {legend}, love, they say you try {legend_where}, {legend_when}. Come and tell me how it went. Even if it went badly. Especially then.
tale.legend.thoughtful: I sometimes wonder whether {legend} tells stories about us. "There's an odd little creature who comes to {legend_where} {legend_when} and dangles worms at me." We must seem very strange.
Every village needs a fish that can't be caught, I think. Ours is {legend}. It's said to live in {legend_where} and rise {legend_when}. The not-catching is the point.
The tales about {legend} change with every teller, except for two things: {legend_where}, and {legend_when}. When a story holds that still, the truth is usually hiding in it.
tale.legend.playful: I'm going to catch {legend}! I've got a plan. Step one: go to {legend_where} {legend_when}. Step two: catch it. Step three: I haven't got that far.
Race you to {legend_where}! First one to catch {legend} gets bragging rights forever. It only bites {legend_when}, so we've loads of time to argue about the rules.
I tried to catch {legend} with a cookie on a string. Didn't work. Next time I'm going to {legend_where} {legend_when}, like the old stories say. With two cookies.
tale.legend.adventurous: Forget dragons. The beast I want is {legend}. Lives in {legend_where}, bites {legend_when}, and has broken every rod that ever touched it. I've packed three.
I've chased rumors across half the world, and I still can't shake the one about {legend}. It's out there in {legend_where}, rising {legend_when}. One of these days I'll be waiting for it.
Every great adventure starts with a tall tale. Mine's {legend}. They say it lives in {legend_where} and bites {legend_when}. That's all I need: a place, a time and a strong line.
tale.legend.meticulous: I've written down every story about {legend} I've ever heard. Forty-one so far. Thirty-eight put it in {legend_where}. Thirty-six say it bites {legend_when}. The odd ones out were all told by the same man, at the tavern.
If you're going after {legend}, do it properly. Go to {legend_where} {legend_when}, with a spare line, a spare hook and a spare pair of socks. The socks are not optional.
The stories about {legend} are terribly imprecise. "Huge." How huge? In feet, please. All I've managed to pin down is {legend_where} and {legend_when}. It's a start.
