tale.legend.steadfast: My father went after {legend}, and so did his father. Same place, {legend_where}. Same time, {legend_when}. None of them caught it. I'll be going this year too. Somebody has to keep it honest.
People come and go with their clever new ideas about {legend}. I'll stick with what my family's always said: {legend_where}, {legend_when}, and a great deal of patience.
I've sat by {legend_where} {legend_when} more times than I can count, waiting for {legend}. It hasn't come yet. I'm not going anywhere.
tale.legend.reserved: ...They say {legend} lives in {legend_where}. ...Bites {legend_when}. ...I've been. Twice. I didn't tell anyone. ...Don't tell anyone.
...I go to {legend_where} sometimes, {legend_when}. ...I saw something big there once. People say it was {legend}. ...I didn't say anything.
...Everyone talks and talks about {legend}. ...I'd rather just go and look. Quietly. It bites {legend_when}, they say. ...That's all I'll say.
tale.legend.imaginative: I think {legend} wears a crown under the water and holds court with all the little fish. It lives in {legend_where}, and {legend_when} it comes up to look at its kingdom from above.
What if {legend} is dreaming us? Down in {legend_where}, fast asleep, dreaming up a whole village. And {legend_when} it stirs a little, and bites. I'd be careful what you dangle.
I painted {legend} once, from the stories. Eyes like lanterns, a tail like a sail. They say it lives in {legend_where} and bites {legend_when}, so I wrote that in the corner, very small.
tale.legend.pragmatic: I don't hold with tall tales, but if {legend} is real it'd feed half the village for a week. It's meant to bite {legend_when} in {legend_where}. Worth a try on a slow day.
Plenty of folk say {legend} bites {legend_when}. Plenty say it lives in {legend_where}. That's either a fish or a very popular lie. Either way, take a strong line.
If you're going after {legend}, don't waste good bait. They say it bites {legend_when} in {legend_where} whatever you put on the hook. I wouldn't know. I've got work.
tale.legend.curious: Why does {legend} only bite {legend_when}? Is it shy? Is it hungry? Is it waiting for someone? I've asked everyone in {village} and nobody knows. I'll have to ask the fish.
How big do you think {legend} really is? Everyone says something different. The only thing they agree on is {legend_where}, {legend_when}. Will you measure it if you catch it? Please?
I've been collecting stories about {legend}. It lives in {legend_where}, and it bites {legend_when}. But what does it do the rest of the time? Nobody ever thinks to ask that.
tale.legend.protective: If you're going to {legend_where} {legend_when} after {legend}, you tell someone first. Me. Tell me. I'll come looking if you're not back by supper.
I don't like all this talk of {legend}. The young ones hear it bites {legend_when}, and off they go to {legend_where} without a word to anyone. Not on my watch.
They say {legend} has pulled grown men off their feet. If you go to {legend_where} {legend_when}, plant your boots and never wrap the line round your hand. I mean it.
tale.legend.gentle: I hope nobody ever catches {legend}. Isn't it nice, knowing something wild is still out there in {legend_where}, coming up {legend_when} to look around?
If you do go after {legend}, be kind to it. Something that old deserves kindness. They say it rises {legend_when} in {legend_where}. Say hello for me.
My grandmother told me about {legend} when I couldn't sleep. How it swims slow circles in {legend_where} and comes up {legend_when} to see the world. I always fell asleep before it saw very much.
tale.legend.fisherman: I'll tell you what my old master told me: {legend} lives in {legend_where} and feeds {legend_when}. Everything else you hear is decoration.
Tall tales are mostly wind, but the ones about {legend} have a bit of water in them. Try {legend_where}, {legend_when}. Use your heaviest line and say goodbye to it in advance.
Every fisherman worth his salt has lost something to {legend}. I lost a good rod and three days of pride, out in {legend_where}. It bites {legend_when}, if you're asking. You're asking.
Folk ask me if {legend} is real. I tell them: go to {legend_where} {legend_when}, keep your line tight and your mouth shut, and then you tell me.
Don't listen to the tavern about {legend}. Listen to the water. It's {legend_where} you want, and {legend_when}. When it's about to bite, you'll know. Everything goes quiet first.
I've seen the wake of {legend}. Not the fish, just the wake. Like a cart going past underwater. That was in {legend_where}. It bites {legend_when}. Bring patience. Then bring more.
The trick with {legend} isn't the bait or the rod. It's the hour. Go to {legend_where} {legend_when} and not a minute otherwise. Most folk get bored and leave just before it comes.

My father had {legend} on the line once. Said it was like trying to pull a church out of {legend_where}. He taught me two things after that: it bites {legend_when}, and never tie a knot you haven't tested.
Everybody in {village} thinks they know where {legend} is. I actually do: {legend_where}, {legend_when}. I tell everyone. Nobody believes the fisherman. They'd rather believe the drunk.

A big fish doesn't get old by being stupid, and {legend} has been getting old in {legend_where} longer than anyone remembers. It bites {legend_when}, and it bites like it knows exactly what you're up to.
baby.tale.legend: My brother says {legend} lives in {legend_where} and bites {legend_when} and it ate a whole cow! I don't think it ate a whole cow. Maybe half a cow.
Grandpa says {legend} is as big as a house! It lives in {legend_where}! I'm going to catch it when I'm big. I'll need a really big worm.
Did you know about {legend}? It only comes out {legend_when}! In {legend_where}! My friend told me. Her uncle saw it. Her uncle sees lots of things.
I'm not scared of {legend}. Even though it bites {legend_when}. Even though it lives in {legend_where}. I'm not scared. I'm just standing over here.
When I catch {legend} I'm going to keep it in a bucket. A really big bucket. My sister says it lives in {legend_where}, so I'll have to carry the bucket a long way.
Mum says {legend} is just a story. But my brother says it bites {legend_when}, and my brother knows everything. He says so.
I saw {legend}! In my dream. It was swimming in {legend_where} and it waved at me with its fin. Then I woke up and it was breakfast.
Shh! I'm practicing fishing for {legend}. My cousin says you have to go to {legend_where} {legend_when} and you can't even sneeze.
tale.caught: Is it true? {player} caught {legend}? I've been hearing that story my whole life, and now someone's gone and finished it.
You caught {legend}! My grandad spent forty years trying. He's going to be so proud of you and so cross with himself.
No. No! You didn't. You caught {legend}? Show me. Show me right now, or I'll never believe it.
They'll be talking about this in {village} for a hundred years. "That was the year {player} caught {legend}." You're in the stories now.
I heard you landed {legend}! Half the village thinks you're making it up. The other half are already telling it bigger than it was.
You've caught {legend}? I don't know whether to cheer or sit down. I think I'll sit down. And then cheer.
My whole life, {legend} was just a story. Now {player} has gone and caught it. What are we going to frighten the children with now?
Is it as big as they say? Bigger? You caught {legend}, {player}! I want to hear every bit of it. Start from the first nibble.
I didn't believe {legend} was real. Then I heard you'd caught it. So now I owe the fisherman an apology and a cider.
Well, that's that, then. {player} caught {legend}. Every angler in the land will want to buy you a drink and pick your brains.
You caught {legend}, and the old folk at the tavern are crying into their cider. Happy tears. Mostly. One of them's been after it for fifty years.
I shook your hand once, {player}. Before you caught {legend}. I'm going to tell everybody that. I knew you before.
contest.soon: The fishing contest is {contest_when}! I've been practicing my casting on the washing line. The washing has suffered.
Have you heard? The season's fishing contest is {contest_when}. Weigh-in at the tavern, and the biggest fish wins.
The contest's {contest_when}, and I've got a secret bait recipe. I'm not telling you what's in it. It's cheese. Don't tell anyone.
I can't sleep for thinking about the fishing contest. It's {contest_when}. I keep dreaming about scales. The weighing kind and the fish kind.
Fishing contest {contest_when}, here in {village}! Suddenly everyone's an expert. Even folk who can't tell a hook from a hairpin.
The fishing contest is {contest_when}. Last time I came second to a man who caught his fish with a bucket. I'm still not over it.
I've walked every bit of bank around {village} this week, looking for the best spot for the contest. It's {contest_when}. I've found it. I'm not telling you where.
There's a fishing contest in {village} {contest_when}. The whole place is buzzing. Even the cats are excited, but that might just be the fish.
The tavern keeper's already polishing the big scale for the weigh-in. The fishing contest's {contest_when}, and they take it very seriously.
I traded my old hat for a new hook for the contest {contest_when}. I won't need a hat if I win. I'll need a crown.
Are you entering the fishing contest? It's {contest_when}. Fish all day, bring your biggest one to the tavern by five, and hope.
My nerves are terrible. The fishing contest is {contest_when}, and I've told everyone I'm going to win. I should not have told everyone.
Every season it's the same. The contest comes round, {contest_when} this time, and every angler in {village} goes very quiet and very secretive. Like a lot of herons.
The fishing contest is {contest_when}. I've been soaking my worms in honey. Don't laugh. My great-aunt swore by it, and she won three times.
I've been bragging all week about the fishing contest {contest_when}. Now I actually have to catch something. That's the part I forgot about.
contest.today: It's the fishing contest today! Fish all day, weigh-in at the tavern at five. I've been at the water since first light.
Contest day! Don't talk to me, I'm concentrating. ...Fine, talk to me. I haven't had a bite since breakfast.
Today's the day. Fishing all day, then everyone carries their biggest catch to the tavern at five for the weigh-in. Good luck. Not too much luck, mind.
The whole village is down at the water today for the fishing contest. You can hear the bobbers plopping from the square.
Are you entering the contest? Then you should be fishing, not talking to me! Go on! Weigh-in's at five, at the tavern.
The tavern keeper's dusted off the big scale. At five o'clock it decides who's the best angler in {village} for a whole season.
It's contest day in {village}! Everyone's pretending they aren't nervous. Everyone's nervous.
I've been fishing since dawn for the contest. My back hurts, my feet are wet and I've never been happier.
Don't stand there! You're casting a shadow on my water. It's the fishing contest. Every little thing matters today.
Contest day, and I've a fish in my basket as long as my forearm. Is that good? It feels good. Don't tell anyone. Weigh-in's at five.
Fishing contest today! Remember, the biggest single fish wins, not the most fish. I learned that the hard way with forty minnows.
I've changed my bait four times today. Bread, worms, cheese, back to worms. The fish are judging me. The weigh-in's at five, at the tavern, if you're curious.
All of {village} smells of fish today, and nobody minds. It's the contest. Bring your biggest one to the tavern at five.
I'm not fishing in the contest this year, I'm watching. It's nearly as nerve-wracking, and I don't have to touch a single worm.
The tavern will be packed at five for the weigh-in. Everyone wants to see who's caught the biggest. Everyone wants it to be them.
contest.won.player: Congratulations, {player}! Winner of the fishing contest! The whole tavern cheered. Even the ones who lost. Well, most of them.
You beat every angler in {village}, {player}. With a fish like that, I'd have bowed to you too.
Champion angler! Somebody get {player} a cider. I'd do it myself, but I spent all my emeralds on bait.
You won the contest! I came in somewhere near the back, but I clapped the loudest. Ask anyone.
The biggest fish of the season, and it was yours, {player}. The old-timers are already arguing about whether they'd have beaten it in their day.
Well done, {player}! You won the fishing contest fair and square. Mostly fair. Very square. I'm joking. Well done.
I can't believe you won the contest! I mean, I can. I saw the fish. That fish was the size of my little brother.
You won! You actually won the fishing contest! You're going to be unbearable now, aren't you? Go on, you've earned it.
Every child in {village} wants to be an angler now, {player}. That's what winning the contest does. You'll have a little crowd following you to the water.
I lost the fishing contest to you, {player}, and I'm glad it was you. Next season, though, that prize is mine. I've already started on my bait.
contest.won.resident: Did you hear? {winner} won the fishing contest with the {catch}. Biggest one anyone's seen all season. {winner} hasn't stopped smiling since.
{winner} won the contest. With the {catch}! I had one nearly as big. Nearly. It got away. They always get away.
{winner} carried that {catch} into the tavern like a newborn baby. Won the whole contest with it. Good for them. I suppose.
The fishing contest went to {winner} this season. That {catch} was a beauty, I'll give them that. I'll give them that and nothing else.
I'm not saying {winner} cheated. I'm saying that's a very big {catch} for someone who goes fishing twice a year.
{winner} won the contest! The whole tavern cheered when the {catch} went on the scale. The scale creaked. I think it was cheering too.
{winner} has been telling everyone about winning the fishing contest. Everyone. The {catch} gets an inch longer every time.
Good for {winner}, winning the contest with the {catch}. I came in last with a boot. A big boot, though. Nobody gave me any credit for the size.
You missed it! {winner} won the fishing contest. Pulled out the {catch} just before the weigh-in and ran it all the way to the tavern.
{winner}'s {catch} won the contest, fair and square. I measured it twice myself. Hated every inch.
fishing.chat: Worms for the river, bread paste for the lake, and for the sea, whatever the sea's in the mood for.
Patience isn't waiting. It's waiting and not minding. Took me twenty years of fishing to learn the difference.
The one that got away was this long. No, longer. It gets longer every year, funnily enough.
River fish fight. Lake fish sulk. Sea fish do whatever they like. That's my whole philosophy.
The fishmonger wants three emeralds for a pike. Three! I could catch one myself for nothing. Well, for nothing and a whole day.
Cloudy days are good for fishing. The fish can't see you looming over the water with that hungry look on your face.
I lost a good hook to a weed bed this morning. The weeds have more of my hooks than I do.
Fishing is mostly sitting. The trick is to sit somewhere lovely.
My best fishing spot is a secret, but I'll give you a hint. It's wet.
Sea fishing's all very well, but I like a river. A river talks back.
If they're not biting, change your bait. If they're still not biting, change your spot. If they're still not biting, go home and have supper.
Rain on the water brings the fish up. Rain down my neck brings me nothing but a cold.
I keep a little book of every fish I've caught. Size, weather, bait and mood. My mood, not the fish's.
Dawn and dusk, that's when the fish feed. The middle of the day is for napping on the bank and pretending you're still fishing.
The fishmonger and I have an arrangement. I don't tell anyone what I'm paid, and the fishmonger doesn't tell anyone how little I bring in.
Never fish downstream of the leatherworker's yard. Just trust me on that one.
I had a fish on the line once that towed my little boat right round the lake. I let it. It seemed to have somewhere to be.
Some folk talk to their bait. I don't. I sing to it. There's a difference.
Cheap line, lost fish. Good line, lost fish anyway, but at least you feel better about it.
Nothing all morning, then a beauty in the last minute before I packed up. It's always the last minute. The fish know when you're leaving.
A herring for breakfast, a trout for supper and a story for the tavern. That's a good day on the water.
You can tell a real angler by their hands. Little hook scars on every finger, and a smell no soap can shift.
The sea's for the brave and the river's for the patient. The pond's for children and for old fellows who've stopped needing to prove anything.
Carp love bread. Trout love flies. Catfish love the worst thing you can find. The smellier the better.
Ice fishing's a special kind of madness. You cut a hole, you sit on the cold, you wait. Then a fish the size of your hand makes your whole week.
fishing.dock: Shh. Something's nosing at my bait. ...No. Gone. Carry on.
Keep your voice down, would you? They hear everything through the boards.
Lovely spot, this dock. Water slapping the posts, the village behind me, nothing to do but watch the bobber.
Mind your feet on the end plank. It wobbles. I've only fallen in twice.
Nibble! ...Nibble. ...And there goes my worm. Clever little thief.
Pull up a bit of dock if you like. Just don't drop your shadow on my water.
I come down to the dock for the fish, mostly. And to get away from everyone, a bit. Not you. You can stay.
Watch the bobber with me. There. See it twitch? That's somebody down there thinking about it.
The fish come in under the dock where it's shady. I just drop my line straight down and wait for them to get curious.
Quiet out here. Just the water, the wind in the reeds and me, not arguing with anybody for once.
Don't stamp on the boards! You'll frighten off everything for half a mile. Tiptoe. That's it.
Best view in {village}, this dock. Water on one side, home on the other, and the odd fish, if I'm lucky.
I've got a bite. I've definitely got a bite. ...I've got a weed. Never mind.
If you're going to stand there, at least hold the bucket. It's empty so far, but it's full of hope.
Fish don't care who you are down here. Doesn't matter what sort of day you've had. It's just you and the line.
fishing.catch: Look at this {catch}! Fresh out of the water and still flapping. Mind your face.
See this {catch}? Pulled it in just now. Fought me like it owed me money.
I've just landed this {catch}, and I want everyone to know. Everyone. Can you tell the whole village? Thanks.
Feel the weight of this {catch}! No, go on, hold it. ...Not like that. Like a baby. A slippery baby.
My {catch}! I've been after one all week. Look at it. Just look at it.
There! This {catch} took me ages. I nearly gave up twice. Good thing I'm stubborn.
Look what I caught! A fine fat {catch}, and the fishmonger's going to be jealous.
This {catch} leapt clean out of the water before I got it in. Nearly took my hat with it. I'm keeping it. The fish, not the hat. Well, both.
I'll be having this {catch} for supper. Or I'll keep it in the barrel and just admire it for a bit. I haven't decided.
Ha! Got you! ...Sorry, I was talking to the {catch}. Isn't it a beauty?
That's the best {catch} I've caught all season. I'll have to tell it at the tavern. I'll add a bit. Everyone adds a bit.
Oh, I'm pleased with this {catch}. Not the biggest in the water, but it's mine, and it put up a proper fight.
fishmonger.work: Fresh fish! Caught today, sold today, on your table by supper. You can't get fresher without getting wet.
Cod, salmon, a nice bit of perch! Step up, step up! Don't mind the smell. That's the smell of quality.
That one? For you, one emerald. For anyone else, two. Don't tell anyone else.
Haggle all you like. I've haggled with herons. I always win.
Every fish here was swimming this morning. Well, most of them. That one was swimming yesterday. It's half price.
Smell that? That's the sea. Or the river. Depends which basket you're standing next to.
You want it cleaned? I'll clean it. You want it filleted? I'll fillet it. You want it to sing? That costs extra.
Fresh fish, honest prices! Well, fresh fish, fairly honest prices. A body's got to make a living.
Look at the eyes on this one. Bright and clear. That's how you know it's fresh. Never buy a fish that looks sad.
The cats have been sitting by my baskets since I opened. They don't buy anything. They just stare. It's very unsettling.
Three emeralds for the big one, and I'll throw in a herring for your trouble. You won't find a better deal in {village}.
You're right, that's a lot for a pike. But it's a lot of pike. Feel the weight of it.
I don't sell the little ones. I throw them back so they can grow up and become expensive.
Fish for supper! Fish for breakfast! Fish for your grandmother! Everyone's grandmother wants fish.
Somebody tried to pay me in cabbages yesterday. I took them. You can't eat emeralds, can you? You can eat cabbages.
greet.dawn: You're up early! The roosters haven't even finished complaining.
Morning already? The sky's still deciding what color to be.
Ah, a fellow early riser. The dew's still on everything.
Good dawn to you. I always think the first hour belongs to whoever's awake for it.
Shh, the village is still yawning. Hello, though!
Up with the sun, are we? Or did you never go to bed?
The bread isn't even in the oven yet, and here you are.
Look at that sky. Pink and gold, like someone spilled a pie.
Hello! I'm only half awake, so be gentle with me.
Early bird, are you? The worms are terrified.
The well water's coldest at dawn. Very good for waking up. Very bad for my toes.
Good morning! Or very late night, depending on how you look at it.
You caught me before my first cup of anything. Hello!
The mist's still sitting on the fields. I love this hour.
Well, good dawn, {player}. You look like someone with plans.
Mornings like this make the whole village smell of woodsmoke and wet grass.
Hello! I just watched the sun come up over the rooftops. Free show, every day.
The golem's on its first round of the day. So am I.
greet.morning: Good morning! The day's still full of possibilities.
Hello there! The village is properly awake now.
Good morning. Everything smells like fresh bread at this hour.
Ah, morning visitors. My favorite kind.
Hello! The bell's already rung twice and I've already lost my gloves once.
Morning! I've got the whole day ahead and absolutely no idea what to do with it.
Good morning! You've got that "going somewhere" look.
Hello, hello! The chickens are out and so are we.
A fine morning to you. The air's crisp and the gossip is fresh.
Good morning! If you're looking for trouble, try somewhere else. If you're looking for company, here I am.
Morning! The shadows are long and the queue at the well is longer.
Hello! I always feel braver in the mornings.
Morning, friend of the village! What brings you by?
Good morning. Mind the puddle by the path, it's deeper than it looks.
Hello! It's {time} and I've already had three conversations about turnips.
Morning! I love how the light comes through the window at this hour.
Good morning, {player}. The day's young and so am I, in spirit.
greet.noon: Midday already? My stomach noticed before I did.
Hello! Perfect timing, I was just thinking about lunch.
Noon, and the sun's right on top of us. Nowhere to hide from it now.
Hello there! The shadows have all gone for their break.
Good day! It's the hour when everyone in {village} smells of somebody's soup.
Ah, hello! The bell's about to ring for lunch, I can feel it.
Midday greetings! Half the day's gone and I've done about a quarter of it.
Hello! It's warm enough for the cats to stop moving entirely.
Hello! Join me in pretending I've been productive all morning.
Noon! The perfect time to stand still and talk to someone.
Hello! Have you eaten? You look like you haven't eaten.
Good day, {player}. The sun's at its highest and so are my spirits.
Hello! I was halfway through a sandwich in my head.
Midday already. Where does the morning go? Somewhere nicer than here, probably.
Hello! The market stalls are busy and the gossip is busier.
greet.afternoon: Good afternoon! The day's settled into itself now.
Hello! Afternoons are for slow walks and long talks, I always say.
Afternoon, {player}! The light's gone all golden.
Ah, hello! The busy part of the day is over and the nice part's begun.
Good afternoon. I've done my share for today, so I'm all yours.
Hello there! The bees are out in force this afternoon.
Afternoon! The bread's long gone but the company's still good.
Hello! It's the sleepy part of the day. Talk to me so I don't nod off.
Good afternoon! You've caught me in a thinking mood.
Hello! The shadows are starting to stretch. I like that.
Afternoon greetings! The village feels lazy and warm today.
Hello! It's {time} already. The day's sneaking away from me again.
Good afternoon. If you hear snoring from the hayloft, no you didn't.
Hello! I always feel chatty in the afternoon.
Afternoon! The children are out of lessons and the noise level is climbing.
Good afternoon, friend. The sun's on its way down but it's in no hurry.
greet.evening: Good evening! The lanterns are going up one by one.
Evening, {player}! Supper smells drift all over {village} at this hour.
Hello! The sky's going orange. Sit a while?
Good evening. Everyone's heading home, but I'm glad you stopped.
Evening already? The day went past like a startled rabbit.
Hello! The light's soft and the day's work is done.
Good evening! The bell's quiet and the crickets have taken over.
Evening, friend. This is my favorite hour for a chat.
Hello! I can hear the tavern from here. Can you?
Good evening. It's getting dark soon, so let's not dawdle too long.
Evening! The cows are complaining about dinner, same as every evening.
Hello there! The first stars are coming out.
Good evening, {player}. You'll want to be indoors before long.
Evening! The smoke from the chimneys goes straight up when it's this still.
Hello! I just lit my lamp and saw you through the window.
Good evening! It's been a long day. Make it a good ending.
greet.night: You're out late! Aren't you worried about the zombies?
Good evening, or should I say good night? It's very dark out.
Oh! You startled me. Not many visitors after dark.
Hello! Quietly, now. Half the village is asleep.
It's late, {player}. Stay close to the lamps.
Night visitor! I hope you've got a sword and a sensible reason.
Hello. The stars are out, and so are the skeletons, so mind yourself.
Good night to you! I was just about to turn in.
You're brave, walking around at this hour.
Hello! I heard something groaning near the fields. Probably the wind. Probably.
Oh, it's you. I thought you were a creeper for a moment. You're much less green.
Late, isn't it? The golem's doing its rounds, at least.
Hello! I can't sleep either. Want to listen to the frogs?
Evening, or night, or whatever this is. Hello!
It's dark as a cave out there. Did you bring a torch?
Shh. The baby next door just fell asleep. Hello!
greet.late: Goodness, it's the middle of the night! Is everything all right?
Hello? It's {time}! Even the owls are tired.
You know it's past midnight, don't you? I'm only up because of the dog.
Oh! You gave me a fright. What are you doing up at this hour?
The middle of the night is no time for visiting, but... hello.
Can't sleep? Me neither. The moon's too bright.
Shh, shh. If my neighbor wakes up, we're both in trouble.
Hello, night owl. Mind the phantoms if you haven't slept in a while.
It's so late the stars are starting to look bored.
Ah, a midnight wanderer. You'd better have a good story.
Hello. I was dreaming about pie, so this had better be important.
Up at {time}? You and the zombies keep the same hours, it seems.
Oh, hello. I came out to check on the noise. It was a sheep.
Hush now, it's the quiet part of the night. What brings you?
greet.band.stranger: Hello, traveler! I'm {name}. I don't think we've met.
Oh, a new face! Welcome to {village}. I'm {name}.
Hello! You're not from around here, are you? I'm {name}.
Greetings, stranger. Are you lost, or just exploring?
Welcome! It's not every day someone new walks through {village}.
Hello there. I'm {name}, the {job} round here. And you are... {player}? Nice to meet you.
Oh! Hello. You'll have to forgive me, I'm not used to new faces.
Hello! If you're looking for the bell, it's in the middle. Everything here is in the middle.
A visitor! Mind the chickens, they don't trust anyone either.
Hello, stranger. You look like you've walked a long way.
Welcome to {village}. We're small, but we're friendly. Mostly.
Hello! I'm {name}. If anyone asks, I was very welcoming.
Ah, hello. I don't bite. The goat by the fence does, though.
Hello, {player}. I've heard about you. Good things, I think.
Oh, hello! Are you here to trade? Or just passing by?
Welcome, welcome! I'm {name}. Feel free to look around, just don't trample the carrots.
Good to meet you. Folks here call me {name}. You can too.
Hello! New faces always make the day more interesting.
Greetings! You've got a kind face. Kind of a square one, but kind.
Hello! Welcome to {village}. Tell me, what brings you all the way out here?
Ah, a visitor. The dogs didn't bark, so you must be all right.
Hello, I'm {name}. And before you ask, no, I don't know where the treasure is.
greet.band.acquaintance: Oh, it's you again! Hello, {player}.
Back again? You must like it here.
Hello! I remember you. You were the one with the very full pockets.
{player}! Good to see a familiar face.
Hello again. I was wondering when you'd pass through.
Ah, you're back. The village has been quiet without you.
Hello! Last time we talked, you said you'd come back. And here you are.
Oh, hello! I'm starting to recognize your footsteps.
Back in {village}, are you? Good, good.
Hello! You keep turning up. I'm starting to like it.
Ah, {player}! I was just thinking about our last chat.
Hello again! You're becoming part of the scenery. In a good way.
Oh, hi! You've got that "back again" look.
Welcome back! The chickens remember you too. They're pretending not to.
Hello! I told my neighbor about you. Only nice things.
Ah, good. I was hoping you'd stop by.
Hello again, {player}! What adventures have you had since?
There you are! I had a feeling it was a visiting sort of day.
Oh, hello! You look a bit more sunburned than last time.
Back already? Did you forget something, or did you miss us?
Hello! I saved a smile for you. Here it is.
Look who it is! Come in, come in. Well, there's no door, but you know what I mean.
greet.band.friend: {player}! My friend! Come here, sit a while.
There you are! I've got so much to tell you.
Hello, friend! The day just got better.
Oh good, it's you. I was hoping it would be you.
My favorite visitor! Don't tell the others.
Hello! I've been saving up stories for you.
{player}! You're a sight for sore eyes.
Ah, my friend's back in {village}. Everything's right with the world.
Hello, you! I was telling {neighbor} about you just this morning.
Friend! Did you eat? Have you slept? Tell me everything.
There's my favorite adventurer.
Hello, hello! The kettle's metaphorically on.
Oh, wonderful. I needed a friendly face today.
{player}! I knew it was you from all the way down the path.
Hello, friend. You've got dirt on your nose. No, other side. There.
Look at you! Back in one piece. That's my favorite kind of back.
Hello! I was just about to go looking for you. Not really. But I thought about it.
Ah, my friend the wanderer. Welcome home, or near enough.
There you are! The village didn't feel right without you.
Hello! I made a list of things to tell you and then I lost the list.
Friend! Come, come. The sun's nicer when you're here.
Oh, I'm so glad you're here. You always know what to say.
greet.band.close: {player}! My dear friend. Come here, let me look at you.
There you are. I always feel better when you visit.
Oh, I'm so happy to see you. Truly.
My dear friend! You've been gone ages. Or a day. It felt like ages.
Hello, you. I saved you the good seat. Well, the good patch of grass.
You're back! I worried about you, you know. Just a little.
{player}! I was hoping you'd come. I've missed our talks.
Ah, my good friend. Everything's a bit brighter now.
There's the face I was waiting for.
Oh, hello. You always turn up exactly when I need you.
My friend! Tell me everything. Leave out nothing. Especially the dangerous bits.
Hello, dear. You look tired. Sit a while with me.
You came! I knew you would.
There you are, my friend. {village} has been asking after you.
Ah! You. Come here. I've got something important to say. I'm glad you're here. That was it.
{player}, my friend. The days you visit are my favorite days.
Hello, you wonderful wanderer. Welcome back.
Oh good. I had a feeling today would be a good day, and here you are.
Dear friend! The well, the bell and I have all missed you.
Hello! Don't you dare leave without saying goodbye this time.
greet.band.best: My best friend! The whole village feels like home when you're here.
{player}! There you are. My favorite person in the whole Overworld.
Oh, my dearest friend. Come here. Sit. Stay as long as you like.
You! I'd know your footsteps anywhere.
Best friend! I've been counting the days. All right, I lost count. But I was counting.
There's my kindred spirit. Everything's better now.
Hello, my dear friend. I keep a little corner of every day for you.
{player}! I told everyone you'd be back. I was right, as usual.
My best friend in all the world! Hug? No? A very firm nod, then.
You're home! Well, you know what I mean. You're home to me.
Ah, there you are. Now the day can start properly.
My friend for life. Hello, hello, hello!
Oh, I've missed you so much. Tell me everything, and then tell me again.
{player}! I saved the best gossip just for you.
Hello, dearest. Whatever you need, I'm here.
There's my favorite face. Don't be gone so long next time.
Best friend! I baked a story for you. I mean, I have a story. I'm excited.
You came back! You always come back. That means a lot to me.
Oh, it's you! The day just turned golden.
My best friend's here! Somebody ring the bell. No, don't, it scares the cows.
greet.weather.rain: Come in out of the wet! Well, as in, out from under the clouds.
You're soaked! Did you walk all the way here in this?
Hello! Rainy days are for staying in and talking, I always say.
Oh, look at you, dripping. Stand under the eaves a moment.
Hello! The farmers are thrilled. Everyone else is damp.
Rain again! At least the crops are happy.
Hello, {player}. Don't mind the puddles, they're decorative.
What weather! The whole village smells of wet straw.
Oh, hello! I was just listening to the rain on the roof.
You brought the rain with you, I see. Or it followed you.
Hello! My hat leaks, but my spirits are dry.
Rain, rain. Lovely for the garden, terrible for my hair.
greet.weather.thunder: Get under cover! That thunder's close!
Hello! Did you hear that crack? It shook the windows.
You shouldn't be out in a storm like this! Stay near me.
Oh! I nearly jumped out of my boots. Hello.
Thunder! Everyone's hiding indoors. Smart people, every one of them.
Hello! Keep away from tall trees and the bell tower, please.
What a storm! The sky's having a terrible day.
Hello. If lightning strikes the pig pen again, we'll have a very confused pigman.
Oh, it's you! I thought it was the thunder knocking.
Hello! Stay close. I'm not scared, I'm just... cautious.
That storm's really rolling in, {player}. Let's keep this quick and dry.
Hello! Every flash makes the whole village go white for a moment. Eerie.
greet.weather.snow: Hello! Look at all this snow!
You must be frozen! Come stand by the fire.
Snowing again! The children are delighted. The rest of us are cold.
Hello, {player}! Your shoulders have snow on them.
Hello! Every roof in {village} is wearing a white hat today.
Brr! Hello! My nose has stopped working.
Hello! Mind the ice on the path, I've fallen twice already.
Snow! It makes everything so quiet.
Hello! I'd shake your hand but I can't feel mine.
Oh, a snowy visitor! Do you want something warm?
Hello! The snow's as deep as my boots and rising.
greet.weather.clearing: Hello! The rain's stopped. Smell that air!
Look, the clouds are breaking up! Hello!
Hello! Everything's sparkling after the rain.
Oh, hello. I came out the moment the rain stopped. Couldn't stay inside another minute.
The sun's back! And so are you. Hello!
Hello! Did you see the rainbow? It was right over the fields.
Mind the puddles, {player}. The children have been jumping in them all over.
Hello! The whole village is drying out like laundry on a line.
Everything smells green after rain. Hello!
greet.weather.hot: Hello! Phew, it's hot. Stand in the shade with me.
Hello! The sand's too hot to walk on barefoot. Don't ask how I know.
Hot one today. Hello! Do you have any water?
Hello! Even the lizards are hiding from this sun.
Scorching! Hello. Stay in the shade or you'll cook.
Hello! On days like this I envy the fish.
Hot enough to fry an egg on the wall. Somebody tried. It didn't work.
greet.market: Happy Market Day! The whole village is out.
Hello! It's Market Day, so mind your purse and your manners.
Market Day greetings! Have you been to the stalls yet?
Hello! It's Market Day, my favorite day of the week.
Market Day! No work, just talk and treats. Hello!
Hello! Everyone's at the bell today, trading and gossiping.
Ah, Market Day. The one day nobody asks me to work. Hello!
Hello, {player}! Come for the market, stay for the gossip.
Market Day! I've already bought three things I don't need.
Hello! The whole village smells of pies and wool today.
Market Day hello! Try the honey, if there's any left.
Hello! It's Market Day, so everyone's wearing their good hats.
Happy Market Day, {player}! The stalls are full and the jokes are terrible.
Hello! I love Market Day. Everyone's out, nobody's in a hurry.
Hello! The children have been running between the stalls all morning.
greet.personality.warmhearted: Oh, hello, dear! Come here, you look like you need a smile.
There you are! Have you eaten? You look peaky.
Hello, sweetheart. What can I do for you today?
Oh, it warms my heart to see you!
Hello, love! Sit down, sit down. Tell me how you are.
Welcome, welcome! Any friend of the village is a friend of mine.
Oh, my! Look at you. Come, I'll find you a snack.
Hello, dear one! I was just thinking of you.
greet.personality.thoughtful: Hello. I was just thinking about something. Several somethings, actually.
Ah, {player}. Hello. Have you ever wondered why bells are bell-shaped?
Hello. Forgive me if I'm distracted; my mind's halfway into a book.
Good to see you. I've been meaning to ask your opinion on something.
Hello. You arrived just as I was having a very interesting thought.
Ah, hello. Quiet days are good for thinking, but company's better.
Hello. I wrote down something clever earlier and now I can't read my own writing.
Hello, {player}. Do you think the stars know we're watching them?
greet.personality.playful: Hey hey! Look who it is!
Hello! Guess what I'm thinking. Wrong! It was pie.
Ta-da! Oh, it's just you. Hello! I was practicing my entrance.
Hello! I was just humming a tune. Want to hear it? Too late, here it comes.
Boo! Ha! Did I scare you? No? Rats.
greet.personality.adventurous: Hello, traveler! Where've you been? Anywhere exciting?
Ah, {player}! You've got the look of someone who's seen a jungle lately.
Hello! I was just planning a trip. In my head. Very detailed.
Hello! Tell me there's a dungeon in your story today.
Hey! Your boots are muddier than last time. Good sign.
Hello! I heard there's a shipwreck past the river. Want to go see?
greet.personality.meticulous: Hello. You're precisely on time. For what, I'm not sure, but on time.
Good day. Wipe your boots, please. Thank you.
Hello, {player}. I've just finished organizing my buttons by color.
Ah, hello. Mind the step; I swept it twice.
Hello. Everything's in order today, which makes me very happy.
Good day. Your collar's crooked. There. Better.
Hello. I've counted the chickens. All present. Hello to you, too.
greet.personality.steadfast: Hello there. Good to see you, same as always.
Morning or evening, I'm here. Hello, {player}.
Hello. Steady day today. I like steady days.
Ah, hello. Nice to see a reliable face.
Hello, friend. The garden's coming along. So's the day.
Hello. Same old me, same old village. Good to see you.
Hello there. Things are as they should be.
Hello, {player}. Sit if you like. I'm not going anywhere.
greet.personality.reserved: Oh, hello. I didn't hear you coming.
Hello. Quiet day. I like it that way.
Hi. ...Sorry, I'm not much of a talker. But I'm glad you're here.
Hello. You can stay a while, if you like.
greet.personality.imaginative: Hello! Did you know the clouds today look exactly like a flying sheep?
Oh, hello! I was just imagining a castle made of cake.
Greetings, wanderer from a faraway land! Or wherever you're from.
Hello! What color is your mood today? Mine's sort of teal.
Ah, {player}! You've arrived just as my daydream got good.
Hello! If you were a painting, you'd be a sunrise.
Hello! I've decided the moon is made of very shy cheese.
Oh, it's you! Hello! I was painting you in my head just now.
greet.personality.pragmatic: Afternoon. Or morning. Whatever it is, hello.
Hello, {player}. Make it quick, I've got wood to cut.
Hello. If you're here to talk, I'll listen while I work.
Right. Hello. What can I do for you?
Hello. Weather's fine, crops are fine, I'm fine.
Hello. Good timing; I just finished a job.
Hello. You've got a loose strap on your boot. Fix that before it trips you.
greet.personality.curious: Oh! Hello! Where did you come from? What's that? Where are you going?
Hello! Can I ask you something? Several somethings?
Hello, {player}! What did you find today?
Oh, hello! Have you ever seen the end of the world? The very edge?
Hello! I've been wondering about something and you look like someone who'd know.
Hi! What's in your pockets? Sorry. Hello first.
Hello! Is it true that some caves glow? I need to know.
Oh, it's you! Tell me something I don't know.
greet.personality.protective: Hello. Everything all right? You look a bit worn.
Hello. Anyone bothering you, you let me know.
Hello there. Watch yourself on the road out, it's been rough lately.
Hello. I keep an eye on things around here. You're welcome among them.
Good to see you in one piece, {player}.
Hello. Stay close to the village after dark, understand?
Ah, there you are. I was wondering if you'd made it back.
greet.personality.gentle: Oh, hello. It's lovely to see you.
Hello, {player}. The flowers are blooming beautifully today.
Hello, dear. Would you like to sit in the sun a while?
Oh, hello. You have a kind sort of quiet about you.
Hello. I hope your day has been gentle with you.
Hello there. I just watered the poppies. They say hello too.
Oh, how nice. A visitor. Hello.
Hello, {player}. Mind the little sprouts by the path.
gift.dish.favorite: The {gift}! My favorite in the whole world, and you made it for me. Thank you, {player}.
Oh, you didn't. You did! The {gift}! Nobody's made it for me since I was small.
My mother made {gift} every year on the first cold night. You've just given me that night back.
How did you know? I've never told anyone how much I love {gift}. I must sigh about it more than I thought.
I'm going to eat this slowly. Very slowly. You don't rush {gift}, not when it's this good.
The {gift}, for me? I'd have walked across three valleys for this. You only had to walk across the square.
If I could only ever eat one dish again, I'd choose this one. And here it is, in my hands.
Oh, {player}. The {gift}. One sniff and I'm nine years old again, sitting on my grandmother's kitchen step.
I can't stop smiling. My cheeks will be sore by supper, and it's all the fault of this {gift}.
My brother and I used to fight over the last of the {gift}. I'm not sharing this one with anybody.
You remembered! I mentioned {gift} once, ages ago, and you actually remembered.
I'm putting this on my best plate. The one with the chip in it. It's still my best plate.
Whenever somebody cooks {gift} for me, it feels like being welcomed home. Thank you.
The {gift}! Don't look, I'm getting a bit misty. Something in my eye. Probably joy.
I was having such an ordinary day, and now there's {gift} in it. Thank you, {player}.
I'm going to tell the whole village that {player} made me {gift}. Everyone. Twice.
The {gift}. My favorite. I'm not going to say anything clever. I'm just going to be very, very happy.
When I was young I swore I'd marry whoever cooked me {gift}. Don't worry. I'll settle for being your friend forever.
A dish made just for me, and it's {gift}. I'll remember this day for a long time.
I've had a lot of {gift} in my life, but never one I was this glad to see. Thank you, {player}.
gift.dish.favorite.warmhearted: The {gift}! Oh, come here, I'm hugging you. Mind the dish. I'm hugging you anyway.
You cooked {gift} for me? I'm always the one doing the feeding. I'd forgotten how lovely it is the other way round.
I'll save a spoonful of this for my neighbor. One spoonful. I'm kind, but I'm not a saint.
gift.dish.favorite.thoughtful: The {gift}. Funny how a single dish can hold a whole year of your life inside it. Thank you, {player}.
I've often wondered why we love the foods we love. I think it's the people who first made them for us. Now you're one of them.
I'm going to eat this slowly and think about nothing but how good it is. That's a rare sort of afternoon.
gift.dish.favorite.playful: The {gift}! Quick, hide it before anyone else sees. Too late, I've started. Mmph.
You made me {gift}? That's it, you're my favorite person. I'm rewriting the list right now.
I'm doing a little dance. Inside. Fine, outside too. Look at my feet go!
gift.dish.favorite.adventurous: The {gift}! I'd trek over a mountain for this, and you've saved me the climb.
This is what I dream about on cold nights out in the wilds. And here it is, without a single blister.
Now this is treasure. Forget gold. Gold never smelled this good.
gift.dish.favorite.meticulous: The {gift}. I'm noting it in my ledger: today, one perfect gift, from {player}. Underlined twice.
My favorite, and set out so tidily. I couldn't have arranged it better myself. Almost.
I have very particular standards for {gift}. You've met every one of them. I checked.
gift.dish.favorite.steadfast: The {gift}. Same as my mother made, same as her mother made. Good things don't change.
I've eaten {gift} every winter of my life, and it never once got old. Thank you, {player}.
My favorite. I won't make a fuss. But I'll remember this, and I'll remember who brought it.
gift.dish.favorite.reserved: ...Oh. The {gift}. ...Thank you. I mean it more than it sounds.
...My favorite. You noticed. ...I don't know what to say. Thank you.
...I'll eat it by the window, where it's quiet. That's the best way. Thank you, {player}.
gift.dish.favorite.imaginative: The {gift}! If this dish were a song, it would be the one everybody hums on the way home.
Somewhere a little kitchen spirit is cheering. I'm cheering too. Quietly. With my mouth full.
I once dreamed I lived in a house made entirely of {gift}. This is the next best thing.
gift.dish.favorite.pragmatic: The {gift}. Filling, honest and exactly what I like. You've got good sense, {player}.
My favorite, and nothing wasted on frills. That's how a dish should be. Thank you.
I was going to have bread and dripping for supper again. This is a vast improvement.
gift.dish.favorite.curious: The {gift}! How did you get it just right? Did you add something? Tell me everything.
My favorite! Whose way did you make it? Everybody's grandmother does it a little differently.
I've always wondered why {gift} tastes better when someone else makes it. Now I have a fresh one to study.
gift.dish.favorite.protective: The {gift}. You went to all this trouble for me? I'll guard it with my life. From the children, mostly.
My favorite. Somebody looking out for me, for once. ...It's a nice feeling. Thank you, {player}.
I'll eat this before I walk the fences tonight. Nothing makes a long night shorter than {gift} in your belly.
gift.dish.favorite.gentle: The {gift}. Oh, that's so kind. I feel looked after. Thank you, {player}.
My favorite. I'll sit in the garden with it, where the bees are. Everything tastes better there.
You made this for me? I'm a little overwhelmed. In the softest possible way.
gift.dish: Oh, the {gift}! That's very kind of you. I'll have it with supper tonight.
Thank you, {player}. Home cooking from a friend is the best kind there is.
The {gift}! I can tell this came out of a proper kitchen. Thank you.
That's lovely. I'll be honest, though: if you ever make {dish}, I'll be yours forever.
Thank you! I haven't had {gift} in ages. I'd forgotten how much I like it.
Oh, for me? That's my supper sorted. You've saved me an hour at the pot.
Lovely. Though if you're ever taking requests, I'm terribly partial to {dish}. Just mentioning it.
Thank you! The way to my heart is {dish}, but this {gift} gets you very close.
Ooh, the {gift}. I'll share it with the neighbors. Well, I'll offer. They might say no.
That smells like somebody knows their way round a kitchen. Thank you.
How thoughtful. Between you and me, I'd trade my boots for {dish}, but this will do very nicely.
Thank you, {player}! I was just wondering what to eat, and now I don't have to wonder.
The {gift}, made by hand. That's worth more than emeralds to me.
Mm, thank you! I'm more of a {dish} sort of person myself, but I'd never turn this away.
That's kind. I'll tell you a secret, though: {dish}. If you ever see me looking glum, that's the cure.
Lovely! I'll save it for after work. Something to look forward to all afternoon.
Thank you! My mother would be pleased to see someone feeding me properly.
Oh! I don't often get given food. People give me advice, mostly. This is much better.
The {gift}. Very fine. My favorite is {dish}, should you ever be near a pot with nothing better to do.
I'll put this on the table and pretend I made it. No, I won't. I'll tell everyone it was you.
Thank you. I've had a long day, and this makes it a good deal shorter.
That's lovely of you. If you ever have a spare evening, {dish} is my weakness. Not that this isn't lovely too.
You cook! Of course you cook. Is there anything you can't do? Thank you, {player}.
I don't usually have {gift}, but I've a feeling that's about to change. Thank you!
gift.dish.fine: Look at this {gift}. That isn't everyday cooking, that's feast-day cooking. You've got the knack.
This is beautifully made. Whoever taught you to cook, I'd like to shake their hand.
The {gift}, and done properly too. Not a thing out of place. The cook will be jealous.
I've eaten at the tavern for years and never had {gift} this good. Don't tell the keeper.
Oh, this is something special. You can taste the patience in it.
I'm almost afraid to eat this {gift}. It looks like it belongs on a lord's table.
Did you really cook this yourself? It's far too fine for an ordinary day. I'm eating it anyway.
Every bit of this {gift} is just right. My grandmother would have asked for your secret, and she never asked anyone.
baby.gift.dish.favorite: The {gift}! It's my favorite! How did you know? Did my mum tell you?
Yay, {gift}! I'm going to eat it all and not share. Maybe one bite. A tiny one.
This is the best thing anybody ever gave me. Even better than the frog.
My favorite! I'm doing a happy dance. Watch! Watch me!
The {gift}! I'm going to eat it so fast. No, so slow, so it lasts forever.
You're the best grown-up in the whole village. That's a fact now. Because of the {gift}.
My tummy's been asking for {gift} all day and now here it is! My tummy says thank you.
Is that really for me? The whole thing? The {gift}? Wow.
I love {gift} more than anything. More than puddles. More than staying up late.
I'm going to tell everyone at lessons you gave me {gift}. They'll be so jealous.
baby.gift.dish: For me? Thank you! What is it? Oh, {gift}. Is there cabbage in it?
Thank you! I'll eat it all up, even the green bits. Probably.
The {gift}! I've never had that before. Is it nice? It looks nice. Okay, I'll try it.
Thank you! Mum says I have to say thank you, but I'd say it anyway.
Ooh, food! I was hungry. I'm always hungry. Thank you!
Thank you! Can I give a bit to the cat? Just a bit. She's hungry too.
It smells good! Is there honey in it? There should always be honey in it.
Thank you! I'm going to eat it in my hay fort. Nobody else is allowed. Except you.
I'll eat it. Even if it has onions. I'm very brave about onions.
Thank you, grown-up! Next time can you make something with honey? This is good too, though!
held.dish: Is that {item}? It smells wonderful from all the way over here.
That {item} looks good. You're not going to eat it right in front of me, are you?
Mm, {item}. Did you make that yourself? Of course you did. Look at you.
I can smell that {item} from here. My stomach just said hello.
Careful with that {item}. If the little ones see it, you'll have a crowd.
You're carrying {item} about like it's nothing. That's a bold thing to do in a hungry village.
Is that {item}? You've been cooking, I can tell. You've got that pleased look.
Ooh. Is that {item} for anyone in particular, or is it the sharing sort?
Eat that while it's good. Food doesn't wait, and neither does a hungry neighbor.
If you ever need someone to taste-test {item}, I'm free. Very free. Right now, even.
Cooking's a fine thing to learn on the road. Nobody turns away a traveler with {item}.
That {item} reminds me I skipped lunch. Thank you for the reminder. I think.
Is that {item}? Turn it round, let me see. Oh, that's a good one.
You're spoiling us all, carrying {item} about. The whole lane's sniffing.
I'm not staring at your {item}. I'm staring near it. That's different.
Whoever's getting that {item} is having a lucky day.
held.favorite_dish: Is that... {dish}? Is that really {dish}? Who's it for? Just asking. No reason.
I can't help looking. That's {dish}. My favorite. Don't mind me. Carry on. Slowly.
Oh my. You're holding {dish}. I'm being very polite about it, but I'd like you to know I'm suffering.
If that {dish} happened to be for me, I'd be the happiest person in the village. I'm only saying.
That's my favorite you've got there. My very favorite. I'll just stand here and admire it.
You know {dish} is my favorite, don't you? You must. Why else would you carry it past me like that?
I've stopped listening to a word you're saying. Sorry. It's the {dish}.
My nose found that {dish} before my eyes did. Is it spoken for?
I'd trade you almost anything for that {dish}. My second-best hat. A song. A very good song.
Don't mind me, I'm just following that {dish} with my eyes. And my feet, a bit.
That's {dish}! I'd know it anywhere. Please tell me you're not just passing through with it.
I'm trying very hard not to ask. Very hard. Is that {dish} for me?
chat.food: If I could eat one thing every day for the rest of my life, it would be {dish}. I've given it a lot of thought.
Everyone's growing onions this year. The whole village smells like supper from noon onward.
I put my pot over the fire at noon and let it bubble till dark. Pottage doesn't like to be hurried.
Nobody in {village} makes {dish} quite like my family does. I'm sure of it. Fairly sure.
Have you watched a clay oven at work? You feed it wood, you wait, and then bread comes out. It's nearly magic.
Cabbages are honest. Leaves all the way down. Still, give me {dish} over plain cabbage any day.
I traded half a basket of leeks with {neighbor} for a bunch of herbs. We both think we won.
My kitchen garden's only six rows, but there's a harvest stew hiding in every one of them.
There's {dish} on my mind again. It's usually on my mind, to be honest.
Garlic keeps the chill away, the apothecary says. It keeps the neighbors away too.
I've started chopping on the prep table instead of on my knee. My knees are very grateful.
Barley's back in the fields. Porridge in the morning, bread at noon, broth at night. It's a busy grain.
Every {season} I promise myself I'll learn a new dish. Every {season} I make {dish} again instead.
{friend} came to supper and ate three helpings of my {dish}. I've never been so flattered.
I hung herbs to dry over the hearth. Now the whole house smells green.
My grandmother made {dish} every Market Day. I still can't walk past the market without wanting some.
The tavern does {dish} sometimes, but it's never as good as at home. Don't tell the cook.
Leeks are lovely, but they hide grit between every layer. Wash them three times, then once more.
I keep a jar of sauerkraut by the door. It lasts all winter. Visitors, less so.
Food tastes better when someone else cooks it. Except {dish}. I like mine best.
Cooking for one is lonely. I always make enough {dish} for two, in case someone knocks.
The onions made me cry this morning. I told {neighbor} it was the onions. It was the onions.
Have you tried {dish}? You should. Well, you should try mine. Then you'll understand.
I planted kitchen herbs right by my door. Now I can season supper without putting my boots on.
I'd walk to the next village and back for {dish} done properly.
Everybody in {village} keeps a kitchen garden now. You can tell whose house is whose by the smell at suppertime.
A proper trencher is bread you eat your dinner off, and then eat. No washing up. I call that genius.
My {dish} has one secret ingredient, and I'm taking it to my grave. Unless you ask nicely.
The clay oven takes all morning to heat and then bakes a loaf in no time. Patience, then hurry. Like most things.
I've eaten {dish} three times a week this {season}. My belt has noticed. My belt can mind its own business.
baby.chat.food: I had honey cake at the party and I'm still thinking about it. I'll think about it until the next party.
Mum makes me eat cabbage. I hide it under my bread. The bread knows.
My favorite food is {dish}. And honey. And {dish} with honey on it.
I'm allowed one honey wafer after supper. I always pick the biggest one. That's called strategy.
When I grow up I'm going to eat {dish} for breakfast, lunch and supper, and nobody can stop me.
The berry pie made my whole face purple. Mum says it'll wash off. I hope it doesn't.
Why are raw onions so loud in your mouth? Crunchy and loud. I don't like loud food.
I helped stir the pot today! I only dropped the spoon in once. Twice.
Grown-ups like leeks. I don't know why. They're just grass that's trying too hard.
If you ever have {dish}, you can give it to me. I'll look after it. In my tummy.
recipe.card: Here. This is my family's recipe for {gift}. My grandmother wrote it down. Her spelling was terrible. Her cooking wasn't.
I don't give this to just anyone, {player}. The {gift}, written out the way my mother made it. Keep it close.
This card has fed my family for three generations. Now it can feed you. The {gift}, every step.
My grandmother taught me {gift} while I stood on a stool by the pot. I'm passing it on to you, minus the stool.
An old cook at a roadside inn gave me this recipe for {gift}, years ago. I've kept it in my apron ever since. Your turn.
My aunt traveled all over before she settled here. This is the {gift} she brought back with her. Don't let anyone copy it.
Here's my recipe for {gift}. There's one step I've underlined. Don't skip it. Everyone skips it.
I've been meaning to give you this. It's the {gift} my family makes for every special day. You're family enough now.
Promise me you won't show this to the cook. The {gift}. They've been trying to wheedle it out of me for years.
My father copied this out for me when I moved into my own house. Now I've copied it out for you. The {gift}.
It's only a card with a few lines on it. But the {gift} on it has seen my family through every hard winter.
Here, {player}. The secret to my {gift}. I've never written it down for anyone outside the family. Until now.
My great-grandmother's {gift}. The card's gone soft at the corners from being held so often. Be gentle with it.
You've been such a good friend that I'd feel mean keeping this from you. My recipe for {gift}. Guard it well.
The card says "a little more than you think." That was my grandmother's answer to everything. Good luck with the {gift}.
I learned {gift} from a traveling cook who stayed one winter and never came back. I've kept her secret all these years. Now it's ours.
recipe.card.warmhearted: Here, love. My {gift}, written out nice and clear. Make it for someone who needs feeding.
This recipe has fed every poorly neighbor and new family on my lane. Now it's yours, {player}. Feed people with it.
recipe.card.thoughtful: A recipe is a kind of letter from someone long gone, I think. This one's from my grandmother. The {gift}. Read it slowly.
Every time someone cooks from this card, the person who wrote it is cooking too, in a way. Now that includes you, {player}.
recipe.card.playful: Here's my secret recipe for {gift}. It's secret, so you have to whisper while you cook it. Those are the rules.
I made you a treasure map! Well, it's a recipe card. For {gift}. The treasure is supper.
recipe.card.adventurous: My uncle got this recipe for {gift} from a cook on the far side of the mountains. Now it's crossed one more border.
Take this on your travels, {player}. The {gift}. A good recipe's better company than most maps.
recipe.card.meticulous: My {gift}. I've written every measure exactly. Please don't improvise. I'll know.
Here. The recipe for {gift}, with my notes in the margin. And notes on the notes. You'll thank me.
recipe.card.steadfast: This recipe for {gift} hasn't changed in sixty years, and it doesn't need to. Make it just like this.
My mother gave me this card when I set up my own hearth. I'm giving it to you because you've stuck by us. The {gift}.
recipe.card.reserved: ...Here. My recipe. For {gift}. ...Don't tell anyone where you got it.
...I don't share this. With anyone. ...But you're not anyone, {player}.
recipe.card.imaginative: This recipe for {gift} came to my great-aunt in a dream, she said. Honestly, it might have.
When you cook this {gift}, hum while you stir. The card doesn't say so, but it helps. I'm sure it helps.
recipe.card.pragmatic: My {gift}. No fuss, no fancy bits, and it's never once gone wrong. Here, take the card.
No point a good recipe sitting in my drawer. The {gift}. Use it, {player}.
recipe.card.curious: My recipe for {gift}. I've tried changing every step to see what happens. This is what happens when you don't.
Here's the {gift}! If you find a way to make it even better, come and tell me. I have to know.
recipe.card.protective: My family's {gift}. Keep this safe. Somebody tried to buy it off me once. They did not get it.
You'll want something good in your belly out on the road, {player}. This is the {gift}. It'll keep you going.
recipe.card.gentle: My grandmother's {gift}. She was the kindest person I've ever known. I think you'd have liked each other.
Here, {player}. It's only a little card, but I hope the {gift} on it makes your kitchen feel like home.
picnic.dish: That was a lovely afternoon. And the {gift} you brought! Nobody left a crumb.
Thank you for bringing the {gift}. Everything tastes better outdoors with friends.
I'm full, I'm sleepy and I'm happy. That's a good gathering. The {gift} helped.
We'll be talking about your {gift} for weeks. Well, I will.
What a day. Good company, good food. I had seconds of the {gift}, and I'd have had thirds.
You brought {gift}! You're invited to every gathering from now on. That's the rule.
I always forget how nice it is to eat together. Thank you for the {gift}, and for coming.
Look at us, all stuffed and smiling. The {gift} was a fine thing to bring.
That's my favorite sort of afternoon: friends, a full basket and the {gift} going round twice.
Did you see how fast the {gift} vanished? I've never seen a dish disappear so quickly.
I'll be humming all the way home. A full belly does that. Thank you for the {gift}.
The {gift} was the best thing at the whole gathering. Don't tell anyone I said so. Especially whoever brought the bread.
picnic.dish.favorite: You brought {gift}! To a gathering! My favorite! I think I ate most of it. I'm not sorry.
The {gift}! I knew the moment you opened the basket. My favorite, and you shared it with everyone. Mostly me.
I didn't say anything at the time, but that {gift} was my favorite in the whole world. Thank you for bringing it.
Of all the dishes you could have brought, you brought my favorite. That was the best gathering I've ever been to.
I hope nobody noticed me taking the last of the {gift}. Everybody noticed, didn't they.
My favorite dish, with friends all round me. I don't think a day gets much better than that.
meal.eating: Mmph! Sorry, mouth full. It's {meal}. Want a bite?
Oh! You caught me mid-mouthful. Hello. This {meal} turned out well, if I say so myself.
Excuse the mess. Meals are a contact sport in this house.
Hello! Pull up a stool. There's more {meal} if you want it. Somewhere.
Hmm? Oh, hello. I'll talk in a moment. This {meal} won't eat itself. Well, not without me.
Sorry, I've got crumbs everywhere. And on you, now. Sorry again.
You're just in time. I was about to say this {meal} needed company.
Mm. Mm-hm. Mmhm! ...That was "hello." I'm eating.
I'd offer you some {meal}, but I've already eaten most of it. You can have the rest. It's a small rest.
Hello! Don't mind my sleeve, it got into the {meal}. It does that.
Ah, {meal}. Nothing fancy, but it's mine, and I made it myself.
Wait. Let me swallow. ...There. Hello! I'd recommend the {meal}. I'm biased.
I always eat too fast when it's {meal}. My mother used to tell me off. Now nobody does, so I eat faster.
Come in, come in. Do you want a spoon? I've got a spare spoon. It's mostly clean.
Oh, you've caught me with my mouth full of {meal}. This is not my most dignified moment.
Sit down a moment. Eating alone is fine. Eating with a friend nearby is better.
tavern.special: The cook's put {special} on today. If you want some, don't dawdle. It goes fast.
Have you heard? It's {special} at the tavern today. Half of {village} has found a reason to walk past.
I came in for a quiet cider and stayed for the {special}. Then I stayed for seconds.
Today's dish is {special}. The keeper chalked it on the board in big letters, as if we needed telling.
I always ask what the dish of the day is, and then I always order it. Today it's {special}.
It's {special} today. I wasn't hungry an hour ago. Funny how that changes.
When the cook gets the {special} just right, the whole tavern goes quiet. Just spoons. It's lovely.
Get to the tavern early. The {special} never lasts past suppertime.
The cook makes a different dish every day, and I've eaten all of them. Today's {special} is near the top of my list.
I asked the cook how they make the {special}. They said "with my hands" and went back to the kitchen.
There's no point cooking at home tonight. Not when the tavern's doing {special}.
People come in from all over {village} for the dish of the day. Today it's {special}, so there'll be a crowd.
work.farmer: Onions want sun on their shoulders and dry feet. Too much water and they sulk.
Cabbages take their time, but when one's ready it's as heavy as a baby. Heavier, sometimes.
Barley's a tough little grain. It grows where wheat won't bother. I admire that.
Plant garlic in the cold and forget about it. It does its best work while you're not looking.
Leeks need earthing up so they grow long and white. It's slow work, but the soup's worth it.
I keep the kitchen herbs by the fence. The bees love them, and the slugs leave them alone. Mostly.
The cook wants onions, the tavern wants barley and everyone wants cabbage, apparently. Busy year.
A row of onions, a row of leeks, a row of cabbages. My field looks like a pottage before it's cooked.
The wheat's coming in tall this year. You can hear it whisper when the wind blows.
Carrots, potatoes, beetroots. Same rows every season, and every season it still feels like a small miracle.
The composter's my best friend. Rotten food in, bone meal out. Magic, really.
I talk to my crops. Don't laugh. The pumpkins grow bigger when I do.
Crows are the bane of my life. And rabbits. And the occasional cow.
I water the fields first thing, before the sun gets fierce.
A good farmer watches the sky more than the soil.
Farmland dries out if you're not careful. Keep water within four blocks. That's the trick.
Harvest week is the busiest week of the year. Everyone pitches in, even the nitwit. Sort of.
I've got calluses on my calluses.
Melons are tricky. They need space to spread. Like teenagers.
I swap my extra wheat for emeralds with anyone who'll have it.
Don't trample the crops! Jumping on farmland turns it right back to dirt.
I plant by the moon. My grandmother did. Can't hurt.
The beetroot this year is so red it looks embarrassed.
Bees love the flowers along my fields. More bees, more crops.
I rotate my fields every year. Keeps the soil happy.
Nothing tastes better than a carrot you grew yourself.
I bake my own bread from my own wheat. Field to table.
Pumpkins! I grew one so big last year the children carved a house in it.
A rainy week does more for my fields than a month of watering.
The golem watches over the fields at night. It's a fine scarecrow, honestly.
My hoe's been in the family for three generations. New handle, new blade, same hoe.
I grew sweet berries along the fence to keep the foxes out. Now the foxes come for the berries.
Every seed's a promise. Not every promise is kept, but most are.
I leave the edge of each field wild for the bees.
Sugar cane by the river's doing well. The baker wants it all for cakes.
Farming's honest work. The soil gives back what you put in.
Some mornings the mist sits on the fields like a blanket. Beautiful.
A good harvest means a good winter. Simple as that.
I once grew a potato shaped exactly like the cleric. We don't talk about it.
Up before the sun, done after it. That's farming.
The children help me pick the carrots. Half of them get eaten on the spot.
I've got dirt under my nails that's older than you.
The farmers in the desert grow cactus and sugar cane. Brave people.
work.cook: The pot over the fire for slow things, the clay oven for bread and pies, the prep table for everything in between. That's my kitchen.
Today's dish is {special}. I started it before the sun was up, so it had better be good.
Never put a pie in the oven till the oven's ready. A cold oven makes a sad crust.
Some days I run between the prep table, the pot and the oven so often I wear a path in the floor.
The secret of a good pottage is patience and one more onion than you think.
Everyone asks what the dish of the day is. Today it's {special}. Tomorrow's is my secret.
If the {special} sells out by suppertime, I've done my job. If it doesn't, I eat it myself.
A trencher's my favorite plate. Bread underneath, supper on top, and nothing to wash afterward.
The stove's been lit since before dawn. Breakfast, lunch, and I'm already thinking about supper.
I make a dish of the day at my stove. Come by and you'll get a helping. One each, mind.
Bread on even days, stew on odd days. That's the kitchen's rhythm.
Hearty stew, fresh bread, steaming coffee. The holy trinity.
My stove cooks twice as fast as a campfire. Put your raw meat on it and watch.
A good cook never measures. A great cook measures and then ignores it.
I've been simmering this stew since sunrise. The longer, the better.
Carrots, potatoes, beef, a pinch of something secret. That's all I'll say.
The whole village eats at my stove eventually.
I burned my thumb on the stove this morning. Kitchens bite back.
Cooking's love you can taste.
I've been experimenting with a pumpkin soup. It's either brilliant or terrible.
The smell of baking bread is the best alarm clock in the world.
I cook for the guards before their night watch. Warm bellies, brave hearts.
Salt, fire and patience. That's cooking.
I trade bread and stew for wheat and emeralds.
My kitchen's small but my portions are large.
Somebody always comes sniffing around the stove at noon. Usually several somebodies.
The chimney smokes all day when I'm cooking. It's how everyone knows I'm open.
I've fed this village for years. Every face here has eaten my bread.
A meal shared is a meal doubled. That's kitchen mathematics.
I've got flour in my hair, sauce on my sleeve and a smile on my face.
Never trust a thin cook.
The kettle sings on my stove all morning.
Cooking for one is boring. Cooking for a village is an adventure.
I've got a new bread recipe with honey. People have been lining up.
The fire's the hardest part. Too hot, it burns. Too cool, it's raw.
My stove's my pride. I scrub it every evening.
Taste everything. Twice. That's the cook's privilege.
I can tell the bread's done by the sound when I knock on it.
On Market Day, I cook from dawn to dusk. Everyone's hungry on Market Day.
Rabbit stew's the hardest to get right. Rabbit stew is also the best.
If you've got raw food, bring it by. The stove's always hot.
A full pot is a happy pot.
I'll teach you a recipe someday. When you've earned it.
work.tavern_keeper: I chalk the dish of the day on the board. Today it's {special}. Then I just point, and people nod.
A mug of cider and a helping of {special}. That's what most folk are ordering today, and I don't blame them.
The cook makes the {special}, I sell it, and we both take the credit. That's a fair partnership.
When it's {special} on the board, I have to put out extra stools. Word gets round fast.
The barrels are full and the mugs are clean. Ready for the evening crowd.
I press cider from apples in the drinks barrel. Bring me apples and I'll pour you a mug.
The tap stand pours coffee. Cocoa beans in, steaming mugs out.
Running a tavern means knowing everyone's business and keeping it to yourself.
I restock the barrel every working day. Apples, berries, and a bit of muscle.
A warm fire, a full mug and a friendly face. That's what a tavern's for.
I've heard every story in {village}. Most of them twice. Some of them true.
Bring an empty mug and I'll fill it. That's the tavern way.
Somebody broke a stool last night dancing. Again.
The bard's been playing here every evening. The crowd loves it.
I sweep the floor three times a day. Taverns get muddy.
Every village needs a tavern. Where else would people complain about the weather together?
I know who likes their cider warm and who likes it cold.
The busiest hour is right after supper. Everyone wants one more drink and one more story.
I wipe down the counter so often it's worn smooth.
Tavern keeping is half pouring, half listening.
I keep a slate of everyone's tabs. Some of them are very long.
I make a special spiced cider for Market Day. People talk about it all week.
The fireplace is the heart of the tavern. I never let it go out.
My feet ache after a long night. But a full tavern's a happy one.
I've broken up three arguments this week. All about pie.
A tavern without music is just a room with chairs.
I open late and close later. My sleep's a mess.
Coffee in the mornings, cider in the evenings. Something for everyone.
Travelers always stop at the tavern first. I'm the welcome committee.
I've got the best seat in the house. Behind the counter, watching everyone.
I keep a spare blanket for anyone who's had a long night.
I can pour a mug blindfolded. I've done it. For a bet.
The cider barrel's the most popular resident in {village}.
I like a busy night. Laughter and clinking mugs. Music to my ears.
Every mug I pour, I hope it makes someone's day a little warmer.
I've been tavern keeper for years. I know every creak in the floor.
The apples this year are sweet. The cider's going to be special.
Tavern's open to everyone. Even grumpy folks. Especially grumpy folks.
I'll pour you a mug if you've got an empty one. That's a promise.
home.plains: The plains go on forever. Grass and sky, grass and sky. I love it.
We get every kind of weather in the plains. Sometimes in one afternoon.
Out here you can see a storm coming from a day away.
Horses run wild across the plains. Beautiful to watch.
I like flat land. You always know what's coming.
Sunflowers grow in fields out here. They all turn to follow the sun.
Plains folk are simple folk. Bread, sheep, and a good fence.
The wind across the grass sounds like the sea, they say. I've never seen the sea.
Every plains village has a bell in the middle. Ours rings the loudest. I'm sure of it.
You can walk for miles here and only see rabbits.
Our soil's the best for wheat. Golden fields as far as you can see.
I was born under a sky this big. I'd feel squashed anywhere else.
The plains are gentle, mostly. Except for the zombies at night.
I like the smell of rain on the grass out here.
There's always a breeze in the plains. Good for drying washing.
We have the friendliest bees in the plains. Lots of flowers.
A plains sunset is the widest sunset there is.
Oak trees here grow round and lazy. Like they've got nowhere to be.
Travelers say plains villages all look the same. They don't look closely.
I've lived on the plains all my life. Every hill's a friend.
home.desert: The desert's hot by day and cold by night. You learn to love both.
Sand gets everywhere. In your boots, your bed, your bread.
We build with sandstone. Cool inside, even at noon.
Water's precious here. We never waste a drop.
The stars in the desert are the brightest in the world.
Cactus is good for green dye. And for not sitting on.
Husks wander the dunes at night. Like zombies, but sunburnt.
Desert folk wear their scarves high against the sand.
We grow sugar cane by the oasis and trade it for everything else.
The dunes shift every year. The village never moves.
I've heard the desert temples hide treasure. And traps.
The camels are my favorite. Tall, patient, a little smug.
In the desert, shade is a gift and a friend is a well.
Sandstorms are rare, but you never forget one.
We don't get rain here. When we do, everyone dances.
The heat makes everyone slow and kind.
Our houses have flat roofs. We sleep up there on hot nights.
The desert looks empty, but it's full of life if you look.
A good well's the heart of a desert village. Ours is deep and sweet.
Sunrise over the dunes turns everything gold.
home.savanna: The savanna's golden and wide. Acacia trees like umbrellas.
Our houses are acacia wood. Orange inside. Warm and bright.
Horses and llamas roam the savanna. Nobody owns them. Everyone loves them.
It never rains much here, but when it does, the grass turns green overnight.
The plateaus rise up like tables for giants.
The sunsets on the savanna are orange and pink and purple all at once.
We grow wheat on the flats and graze sheep on the hills.
Armadillos wander through sometimes. Little armored fellows.
The acacia trees lean every which way. I think they're dancing.
Savanna folk are tough. Hot sun, dry ground, big hearts.
At night you can hear the wind through the long grass.
Our village sits on a high plateau. Best view in the world.
The ground cracks in the dry season. We wait for the rains.
Every savanna house has a good shady porch.
I love the smell of dry grass in the heat.
Llamas come down from the hills to drink at our well.
The sky here is enormous. It makes you feel very small and very free.
We trade acacia wood for things we can't grow.
The cartographer says our plateau's on three different maps.
Living on the savanna teaches you patience. The rain comes when it comes.
home.snow: Winter lasts most of the year here. We're used to it.
