joke.job.fisherman: What do you call a fish that wears a bowtie? So-fish-ticated.
Why did the fisherman put peanut butter in the sea? To go with the jellyfish.
Which fish can perform surgery? A sturgeon.
What did the fisherman say to the magic trick? "Pick a cod, any cod."
joke.job.fletcher: Why did the arrow fall in love? It was struck by cupid.
What's a fletcher's favorite saying? "Feather together, flock together."
Why are arrows good at relationships? They always get to the point.
I'd tell an arrow joke, but you'd see it coming a mile away.
joke.job.cleric: Why did the potion go to church? It needed a little brew-tiful blessing.
What do you call a nervous brewing stand? Bubbly.
Why did I light so many candles? I wanted a holy-day.
What's a cleric's favorite dance? The redstone shuffle.
joke.job.cartographer: Why did the map go to school? It wanted to be well-read.
What did the cartographer say to the mountain? "You're looking great from this angle."
Why are maps great listeners? They know where you're coming from.
What do you call a lost cartographer? Ironic.
joke.job.armorer: Why was the chestplate so confident? It had nothing to hide behind except itself.
What did the helmet say to the head? "I've got you covered."
Why did the knight go to the armorer? He needed to get suited up.
What's an armorer's favorite game? Chain tag.
joke.job.toolsmith: Why did the pickaxe get promoted? It always hit rock bottom first.
What did the shovel say to the dirt? "I dig you."
Why are hammers great friends? They always nail it.
What's a toolsmith's favorite music? Heavy metal.
joke.job.weaponsmith: Why did the sword break up with the shield? It needed space to swing.
What did the grindstone say to the blade? "Stay sharp."
Why are axes great at parties? They break the ice.
What's a weaponsmith's least favorite word? Rust.
joke.job.leatherworker: Why did the cow go to the leatherworker? To get its hide back.
What did one boot say to the other? "Let's step out together."
Why are belts so reliable? They hold everything together.
What's a leatherworker's favorite song? "Hide and Seek."
joke.job.mason: Why are masons so good at relationships? They know how to build a solid foundation.
What did one brick say to the other? "Let's stick together."
Why did the stone go to school? To get a little more polished.
What's a mason's favorite dessert? Rocky road.
joke.job.shepherd: What do you call a sheep that's good at karate? A lamb-chop.
Why did the sheep get a ticket? It made a ewe-turn.
What's a shepherd's favorite bedtime story? Counting sheep, obviously.
Why are sheep so good at parties? They know how to get woolly wild.
joke.job.butcher: Why did the sausage go to school? To be a little more well-done.
What did the steak say to the smoker? "You're making me blush."
Why are butchers great at tennis? They have a great chop shot.
What did the ham say to the smoker? "Cure me of my troubles."
joke.job.nitwit: Why do I never work? Because work's a four-letter word. So is "nap," which I prefer.
What's my favorite exercise? Lying down and then standing up. Occasionally.
Why did I go to the library? I heard they had a lot of shelves to lean on.
What do you call a nap after a nap? A good day.
joke.job.none: Why am I always looking for a job? I'm a professional job-hunter. Ha. Sort of.
What did the unemployed villager say to the workstation? "Is this seat taken?"
Why don't I have a job? The job didn't have me first.
What's my job? Telling jokes about not having a job.
joke.job.knight: Why did the knight take so long to get dressed? He had a lot of armor to put on.
What's a knight's favorite fish? A swordfish. I've said that before. It's still good.
Why did the training dummy get promoted? It always took a hit for the team.
What did the dummy say to the knight? "Is that all you've got?" Then I hit it harder.
joke.job.archer: Why did the archer break up with the bow? It was too high-strung.
What's an archer's favorite month? Arch. Arch-uary.
Why are targets so patient? They're used to people missing them.
How do archers say hello? "Arrow there!"
joke.job.cook: Why did the tomato turn red? It saw the salad dressing. A classic in the kitchen.
What do you call a cook who's always calm? Unflappable. Like a pancake that's done right.
Why did the stew win the contest? It was a hearty competitor.
What's a cook's favorite exercise? Whisking.
joke.job.tavern_keeper: Why did the cider barrel go to therapy? It was feeling a little empty.
What do you call a tavern with no customers? A bar-gain.
Why are mugs so friendly? They're always up for a cup.
What did the coffee say to the tavern keeper? "You mean a latte to me."
joke.job.apothecary: Why did the herb go to the apothecary? It was feeling a bit thyme-worn.
What do you call a nervous tonic? A bit shaken.
Why did the mint win the argument? It was very cool about it.
What's an apothecary's favorite flower? Mari-gold. Expensive and soothing.
joke.job.painter: Why was the paint so tired? It had too many coats.
What did the canvas say to the brush? "Stroke of luck you came along."
Why do painters make great friends? They always help you see the bigger picture.
What's a painter's favorite cake? Marble, obviously.
joke.job.bard: Why did the bard sit on the ladder? To reach the high notes.
What do you call a musician with problems? A trebled artist.
Why are lutes so friendly? They're always in a good tune.
What's a bard's favorite vegetable? Beets. Get it? Beats.
joke.job.tailor: Why did the tailor get an award? She was sew good at her job.
What did the needle say to the thread? "Let's get to the point."
Why are buttons so dependable? They always hold things together.
What's a tailor's favorite movie? Pants-ing Through Time.
joke.job.carpenter: Why did the carpenter refuse to work? It was too boring.
What did the saw say to the log? "I've got a bone to pick with you." Wait, wrong job.
Why are carpenters great at parties? They know how to raise the roof.
What's a carpenter's favorite game? Plank-ball.
joke.job.scholar: Why did the scholar bring a ladder to class? To reach higher education.
What do you call an old history book? A blast from the past.
Why are historians great at parties? They know how to make an old story new.
I'd tell you a history joke, but it's in the past.
joke.weather: What did the cloud say to the rain? "You're dripping with talent."
Why did the snowman call his dog Frost? Because frost bites.
What's a tornado's favorite game? Twister.
Why did the sun go to school? To get brighter. I tell that one every sunny day.
What did one raindrop say to the other? "Two's company, three's a cloud."
Why don't storms ever win arguments? They always end up blowing over.
What does a cloud wear under its raincoat? Thunderwear.
How do snowmen get around? They ride an icicle.
What's the weather like for a skeleton? Bone dry.
Why did the lightning bolt get grounded? It was acting out.
notice.hunt.zombies: Zombies keep groaning outside my window at night and I haven't slept properly in a week. Could someone deal with {mobs}? I'll pay in emeralds. - {name}
Help wanted: {mobs} to be cleared from the fields before the carrots get trampled. Reward offered.
Something keeps rattling my door after dark, and it isn't the wind. Please see off {mobs} and come and tell me it's safe. - {name}
Would a brave soul please send {mobs} packing? All that shuffling by the well has the children frightened half to death.
Wanted: one adventurer with a good sword. Job: {mobs}, gone for good. Pay: emeralds and my undying gratitude. - {name}
I counted the shapes by the fence last night and stopped when I got scared. If you can deal with {mobs}, I'll make it worth your while.
To whoever reads this: {mobs} wandered into the pumpkin patch last night. I would very much like the pumpkin patch back. - {name}
Zombies at the edge of {village} again. Please take care of {mobs}, and please take care of yourself while you do it.
notice.hunt.skeletons: Arrows keep landing in my washing line. Somebody please deal with {mobs} before I run out of shirts. - {name}
Wanted: someone to see off {mobs} rattling about past the fields at night. Reward in emeralds and gratitude.
I heard bones clattering by the old path again. If you could put an end to {mobs}, I'd sleep much better. - {name}
Skeletons have been taking shots at anyone who goes out after dark. Please clear away {mobs}. Mind your head.
A skeleton shot my good hat clean off. I'd like {mobs} dealt with, and I'd like a new hat, but I'll settle for the first. - {name}
Notice to adventurers: bring a shield and see off {mobs} in the shadows past the farms. Emeralds waiting.
Every morning I find arrows stuck in the fence posts. Please, someone deal with {mobs}. The fence is beginning to look like a hedgehog.
Skeletons by the river again. Could a steady hand clear out {mobs}? I'll have a reward ready when you get back. - {name}
notice.hunt.spiders: There are spiders the size of sheep by the barn, and I am not going in there. Please deal with {mobs}. - {name}
Wanted: someone unafraid of eight legs. Job: {mobs}, cleared from the woods past the fields. Reward: emeralds.
I walked into a web this morning and I'm still not over it. Please see to {mobs} near the old path.
Spiders climbing the walls at night again. I'd be grateful if someone dealt with {mobs}. Very grateful. Hurry. - {name}
Would somebody please take care of {mobs}? The red eyes in the dark have stopped being interesting.
To anyone brave: {mobs} by the edge of {village}. I'll pay well, and I'll bring you something warm to drink afterwards.
The chickens won't leave the coop, and I don't blame them. Please clear away {mobs} lurking past the fence. - {name}
I'm told spiders are useful for string. I don't care. Please deal with {mobs} and I'll buy my string honestly.
notice.hunt.creepers: Something hissed behind my house last night, and now there's a hole where the vegetable bed used to be. Please deal with {mobs}. - {name}
Wanted: careful adventurer to handle {mobs}. Quietly, please. From a distance, ideally.
I've rebuilt my garden wall twice this season. Somebody please see to {mobs} before it's three times. - {name}
Please, please deal with {mobs} lurking around the village. My nerves can't take any more hissing.
Notice: {mobs} spotted creeping near the houses. Reward for whoever gets there before anything goes bang.
Green, quiet and very rude. Please see off {mobs} near the fields. I'll pay in emeralds. - {name}
I keep a bucket of gravel by the door for creeper holes. I'd rather not need it. Please take care of {mobs}.
Creepers about! Bring a bow, keep your distance, and rid us of {mobs}. Reward waiting with me.
notice.hunt.witches: Someone in a pointed hat has been cackling in the swamp and throwing bottles at travelers. Please deal with {mobs}. - {name}
Wanted: someone with a good bow and a steady stomach. Job: {mobs}. Mind the potions.
A potion splashed my goat last week and the goat hasn't been right since. Please put a stop to {mobs}. - {name}
Please see to {mobs} near the edge of {village}. I've had enough of strange purple smoke drifting over my washing.
Notice to adventurers: {mobs} brewing trouble past the woods. Bring milk, just in case. Reward in emeralds.
I've heard cackling at night three times this week. That's three times too many. Please deal with {mobs}. - {name}
If a brave sort could handle {mobs}, I'd be ever so thankful. Leave the bottles alone; I don't trust them.
Witch hut, witch trouble. Please clear away {mobs} and I'll make it worth your while.
notice.hunt.slimes: Something green and bouncy has been squashing my flowerbeds. Please deal with {mobs}. - {name}
Wanted: someone to clear out {mobs} from the swampy bit past the fields. It's very sticky work. Emeralds offered.
I stepped in a slime and lost a boot. Please see to {mobs} before I lose the other one. - {name}
Boing, boing, boing, all night long. Please, someone deal with {mobs}. I need my sleep.
Notice: {mobs} hopping about the lowlands. Reward for a tidy job. Bring a rag for your sword.
My cat keeps trying to fight the slimes and losing. Please handle {mobs}, for the cat's sake. - {name}
If you can clear away {mobs}, I'll pay well. If you bring back a slimeball or two, I'll pay better.
They split when you hit them, I'm told. Please deal with {mobs} anyway. All the bits. - {name}
notice.hunt.phantoms: Something swoops over the rooftops every night I stay up late. Please deal with {mobs}. - {name}
Wanted: someone to clear the night sky of {mobs}. Bring a bow and try not to yawn.
Too many of us have been sleeping badly, and now the sky's full of screeching. Please see to {mobs}.
I was nearly carried off on my way home last night. Nearly. Please handle {mobs} before next time. - {name}
Notice: {mobs} circling over {village} after dark. Reward for a steady aim and a late night.
Please, someone deal with {mobs}. And then everyone get a good night's sleep, so no more come back. - {name}
The screeching keeps the baby awake. Please take care of {mobs}. I'll pay in emeralds and in thanks.
If you're a night owl, here's a job: {mobs}, out of our sky. Reward with me in the morning.
notice.hunt.pillagers: Crossbows spotted on the hill again. Please deal with {mobs} before anything worse comes of it. - {name}
Wanted: someone brave and well armed to see off {mobs} near the old road. Reward offered, and the village's thanks.
I saw a banner with a grey face on it past the woods. Please take care of {mobs} before anyone comes to harm. - {name}
Notice to adventurers: {mobs} prowling around our fields. The guards could use a hand. Emeralds paid.
Pillagers stole two of my sheep last season. Not this season. Please deal with {mobs}.
Please handle {mobs} near {village}. Be careful. Crossbows hurt, and so does a raid. - {name}
If anyone's handy with a sword, please clear away {mobs} before the next Market Day. We don't want the traders scared off.
The children have stopped playing past the fence because of the crossbows. Please see to {mobs} so they can play again.
notice.fetch.farmer: Looking for {wanted} to help with the planting. The fields won't sow themselves, and my back's not what it was. - {name}
The composter's hungry and so are the chickens. If you've got {wanted} to spare, bring it by the farm.
Wanted: {wanted}, for the farm. Harvest's coming and I'm short. Emeralds paid fairly.
A storm flattened half my rows. I could use {wanted} to set things right again. - {name}
If anyone has {wanted}, I'll trade emeralds and a basket of whatever's ripe. Ask at the farm by the fields.
notice.fetch.librarian: The library needs {wanted}. Please bring it quietly. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the shelves. A library is never finished, only temporarily tidy.
I'm rebinding the old books by the lectern and I've run short. Could someone bring {wanted}? Payment in emeralds and a good recommendation.
To the kind reader of this notice: I need {wanted}. Please return it to the library, the way you'd return a book. On time. - {name}
A new volume of village history is underway, and I need {wanted} to finish it. Reward at the lectern.
notice.fetch.fisherman: The barrel's half empty and the nets need mending. Bring me {wanted} and there's a fish supper in it for you. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the boat and the barrel. Leave it by the dock. Reward paid.
Lost my good tackle in the river. Could use {wanted} to get back on the water. - {name}
The fish aren't biting and my luck's no better. Bring {wanted} and I'll share the first good catch with you.
If anyone's got {wanted}, I'll trade emeralds and tell you where the big ones hide. Honest. - {name}
notice.fetch.fletcher: The fletching table's bare. I need {wanted} to keep the guards in arrows. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for bows and arrows. Straight shafts and good feathers make a safe village.
Practice season's here and every archer in {village} wants new arrows. Bring {wanted}, please. Reward offered.
Could someone bring {wanted}? My chickens refuse to donate any more feathers. - {name}
I've a big order of arrows due and not enough to make them with. Looking for {wanted}. Emeralds paid.
notice.fetch.cleric: The brewing stand's run dry. If you can bring {wanted}, I'll have healing for whoever needs it. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the temple stores. Blessings and emeralds in return.
A cleric's shelves should never be empty, and mine nearly are. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Someone in {village} is unwell, and I need {wanted} for the remedy. Please hurry, if you can.
Looking for {wanted} for a potion I've been meaning to brew. Payment in emeralds and a quiet prayer for your travels.
notice.fetch.cartographer: My maps have an empty corner and it's bothering me. I need {wanted} to fill it in. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the cartography table. Every map needs paper, patience and a little help.
I'm charting the road to the next village and I've run out of supplies. Bring {wanted}, please. Reward offered. - {name}
If you have {wanted}, bring it by. I'll pay in emeralds and I'll put your name on the map. Small, in a corner.
Seeking {wanted} for a new map of {village} and everything around it. Accurate mapmakers pay accurately.
notice.fetch.armorer: The blast furnace is roaring and I've nothing to feed it. Bring me {wanted}, please. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the forge. The guards need fitting for new armor before the cold sets in.
A good helmet starts with good metal. I'm short on {wanted}. Reward in emeralds. - {name}
Could someone bring {wanted}? I've three breastplates half made and an apprentice full of questions.
If you can find {wanted}, I'll pay you well and polish your armor for free. - {name}
notice.fetch.toolsmith: Every hoe and pickaxe in {village} comes through my door sooner or later. I need {wanted} to keep up. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the smithing table. Broken tools don't mend themselves.
Harvest's close, and everyone wants a sharp hoe at once. Please bring {wanted}. Emeralds paid.
I'm making a set of little tools for the children's garden. Small ones. I need {wanted}. - {name}
Looking for {wanted}. A toolsmith with no metal is just someone with a hammer.
notice.fetch.weaponsmith: The grindstone's been busy, but I'm out of what I need. Please bring {wanted} to the forge. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for blades for the guards. A village is only as safe as its swords are sharp.
Raids have everyone asking for new weapons. Could someone bring {wanted}? Reward offered.
I've an order for a sword I'm very proud of, and I'm short on {wanted}. Help me finish it. - {name}
Seeking {wanted}. Emeralds paid, and I'll sharpen your sword while you wait.
notice.fetch.leatherworker: The cauldron's full of dye and I've nothing to soak. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for saddles, boots and good strong belts. Reward in emeralds.
Every pair of boots in {village} seems to have worn through at once. I need {wanted}, quickly. - {name}
Could somebody spare {wanted}? I'm making a satchel for a traveler and I've come up short.
Looking for {wanted}. I'll pay fairly and patch your gloves into the bargain. - {name}
notice.fetch.mason: The stonecutter's idle and the steps by the bell are crumbling. I need {wanted} to fix them. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the new wall by the fields. Steady work, honest pay.
A house is only as good as its foundations. Please bring {wanted} to my yard. Emeralds offered.
I'm building a little bridge over the stream and I've run out halfway across. Bring {wanted}, please. - {name}
Seeking {wanted}. The chimney on the corner house is leaning, and I'd like it not to.
notice.fetch.shepherd: The loom's waiting, and so are the new banners for the bell. I need {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the flock and the loom. Payment in emeralds, and a fleece if you like.
The sheep wandered off again and I'm behind on everything. Could someone bring {wanted}? - {name}
I'm weaving blankets for winter and I'm short. Please bring {wanted} to the pasture.
Looking for {wanted}. My sheep will thank you, in their way. Mostly by staring. - {name}
notice.fetch.butcher: The smoker's warm and the larder's bare. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the village larder. A feast is coming and I mean to be ready.
Supper for half of {village} depends on me this week, and I'm short on {wanted}. Reward in emeralds.
Could anyone bring {wanted}? I'll trade emeralds and the best cut of the week. - {name}
Seeking {wanted} for the smoker. Good food keeps a village happy. I'd like a happy village.
notice.fetch.knight: My training dummy's seen better days, and so have my supplies. I need {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the guard post. We keep {village} safe; help us keep ourselves ready.
A knight must be prepared. This knight is not. Please bring {wanted}. Reward offered. - {name}
The watch is long and cold this time of year. Bring {wanted}, if you can, for the knights on duty.
Seeking {wanted} for the garrison stores. Emeralds paid, and you'll have a friend in the guard.
notice.fetch.archer: I've loosed every arrow I own at the target, and I need {wanted} to keep practicing. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the archers on the wall. Steady supplies make for steady aim.
My bowstring snapped mid-shot this morning. Very undignified. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Seeking {wanted}. The archery target looks lonely without arrows in it.
Could someone bring {wanted} by the target range? Reward in emeralds, and I'll teach you to aim. - {name}
notice.fetch.cook: The kitchen stove is hot and my pantry is not. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for tonight's supper. Bring it to the kitchen and you'll eat first.
I'm making a stew big enough for the whole village, and I'm short on {wanted}. Help me, and the first bowl is yours.
Could somebody bring {wanted}? A recipe's only a wish without the ingredients. - {name}
Seeking {wanted} for the kitchen. Emeralds paid, and a hot meal whenever you're passing.
notice.fetch.tavern_keeper: The cider barrel's running low and the regulars are noticing. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the tavern. Every mug in {village} thanks you in advance.
Big night at the tavern coming up, and I'm short on {wanted}. Reward in emeralds and a free mug.
Could someone bring {wanted} to the tavern? The tap stand's empty and the bard's getting thirsty. - {name}
Looking for {wanted}. A tavern with nothing to pour is just a room full of stools. - {name}
notice.fetch.apothecary: The alchemical press is empty and I've tonics to make. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for remedies. Scraped knees and coughs don't wait for the seasons.
I'm making a new herbal tonic and I'm short on {wanted}. Bring it by and you'll get the first bottle.
Seeking {wanted}. Half the village has the sniffles and I've only so much in the jars. - {name}
Could somebody spare {wanted}? I'll pay in emeralds and patch you up for free next time. - {name}
notice.fetch.painter: My easel's been staring at me, empty, for days. I need {wanted} to begin. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for a new painting of {village} at sunset. Your name goes in the corner.
I've run out halfway through a masterpiece. Or a nearly-masterpiece. Please bring {wanted}.
Seeking {wanted}. Inspiration I have plenty of. Supplies, not so much. - {name}
Could someone bring {wanted}? I'll paint you a little picture in return. A small one. A very nice small one.
notice.fetch.bard: My music stand's lonely and I've a new song half written. I need {wanted} to finish it. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for the bard. Bring it by and I'll write you a verse. A flattering one.
A song needs inspiration, and inspiration needs {wanted}. Please help. - {name}
The lute's out of tune and so am I. Could someone bring {wanted}? Reward in emeralds and a ballad.
Seeking {wanted} for a performance at the tavern. Come and hear it after. - {name}
notice.fetch.tailor: The sewing table's piled with mending and I'm short on {wanted}. Please help. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for new clothes for the children. They grow faster than I can sew.
I'm making a fine coat for Market Day and I need {wanted} to finish it. Reward offered.
Could someone bring {wanted}? Every hem in {village} is coming loose at once. The hems must have planned it together.
Seeking {wanted}. I'll mend whatever you've torn in return. Adventurers tear a lot of things. - {name}
notice.fetch.carpenter: The sawmill's ready and the woodpile's gone. Please bring {wanted}. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for a new roof on the old barn. Leaks wait for no one.
I'm building benches for the square, so everyone has somewhere to sit by the bell. I need {wanted}. - {name}
Could someone bring {wanted}? The children want a treehouse and I've made the mistake of saying yes.
Seeking {wanted}. Fair pay in emeralds, and I'll fix that wobbly chair of yours. - {name}
notice.fetch.scholar: The archives have a gap in them, and gaps bother me. I need {wanted} to fill it. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}, for research. The village chronicle won't write itself. It has tried.
I'm studying something fascinating and I need {wanted} to go on. Please help. Reward offered.
Seeking {wanted} for the archives. I'll pay in emeralds and tell you something you didn't know. - {name}
Could someone bring {wanted}? I'm halfway through a theory and I'd like to be all the way through it. - {name}
notice.fetch.nitwit: I need {wanted}. I don't remember why. I'm sure it's important. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}. For a project. A very good project. I'll explain when I've thought of it.
If someone brings me {wanted}, I'll give them emeralds. I found the emeralds. They're mine now.
Please bring {wanted}. I promised somebody something and I've forgotten who. This should cover it. - {name}
Looking for {wanted}. Don't ask what for. I've been asked that all week and I still don't know.
notice.fetch.none: I've no trade of my own yet, but I've got a little project going. Could someone bring {wanted}? - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}. I'm fixing up my house, one corner at a time.
I'm trying my hand at something new, and I need {wanted} to get started. Reward offered. - {name}
Could someone spare {wanted}? I've been helping wherever I'm needed, and now it's my turn to ask.
Seeking {wanted}. I haven't found my calling yet, but I've found a use for this. - {name}
notice.fetch.general: Wanted: {wanted}. Bring it to my door and I'll pay you properly. - {name}
Could someone kind bring me {wanted}? I'd go myself, but my knees disagree.
Looking for {wanted}. Emeralds paid, and a cup of something warm.
If you have {wanted} to spare, I'd be ever so grateful. Please ask for {name}.
In need of {wanted}. Not urgent, but not exactly not urgent either. - {name}
Seeking {wanted}, for reasons too boring to write down. Reward offered.
Please bring {wanted} by my house. I'll make it worth the walk. - {name}
A small request: {wanted}. A fair reward. A big thank you.
I've been meaning to get {wanted} for weeks. If you get it for me instead, I'll pay you for the trouble. - {name}
Help wanted: {wanted}, delivered to my door. Mine's the house with the blue shutters. Well, they used to be blue.
Short on {wanted} and long on gratitude. Bring some by, please. - {name}
notice.fetch.child: I need {wanted} for my secret fort. Its a secret. Dont tell anybody. From {name}
Pleese bring me {wanted}. I will give you my best pebble. - {name}
Dear adventurer. I want {wanted} to make a present for my mum. You can have a emerald. I saved it. - {name}
Wanted: {wanted}. For a very importent game. Only brave peeple. From {name}
Can you get me {wanted}? I would get it myself but Im not aloud past the fence.
Hello. I am {name}. I need {wanted} for a castle. A big one. Thank you very much.
If you bring {wanted} I will draw you a picture. I am good at drawing cats and also cows.
Lost: my good marble. Wanted: {wanted}. Reward: a emerald and a hug. - {name}
Pleaz help. I need {wanted} for a surprise. It is a big surprise. Dont look at it.
To the hero. Bring {wanted} to me by the well and I will give you a reward. A real one! From {name}
I want {wanted} because my friend has some and I dont. Thats fair isnt it. - {name}
notice.letter.friend: I've written a letter to {recipient} and I'd like it carried by a friendly hand. Ask me for it. - {name}
Wanted: someone to deliver a sealed letter to {recipient}. Nothing urgent, just old friends catching up.
{recipient} and I haven't had a proper talk in ages. I've put it all in a letter. Could you take it over?
Could a kind traveler carry a letter to {recipient} for me? There's a reward, and probably a smile at the other end. - {name}
I've a letter here for {recipient}, full of news and a joke I've been saving. Please deliver it. Reward offered.
notice.letter.family: I've written to {recipient}, and I'd like it delivered by someone I trust. Come and see me for the letter. - {name}
Family news to share with {recipient}. Could someone carry a sealed letter over? Reward offered.
{recipient} worries if I don't write. Please take my letter across, so the worrying can stop. - {name}
Wanted: a messenger for a family letter to {recipient}. It's only news, but it's our news.
Could someone bring a letter to {recipient} for me? We're family, and family ought to keep in touch. - {name}
notice.letter.crush: I have a letter for {recipient}. Please don't read it. Please don't ask about it. Please just deliver it.
Wanted: a discreet messenger for a sealed letter to {recipient}. No questions. Reward offered.
Could someone carry a letter to {recipient} for me? I've rewritten it eleven times. Don't let me rewrite it a twelfth.
A letter for {recipient}, if anyone's passing. It's nothing. It's very much not nothing. Please be gentle with it.
I'd take this letter to {recipient} myself, but my knees go strange whenever I try. Could you? - a friend
notice.letter.partner: I've written a little letter for {recipient}. We see each other every day, but some things are nicer on paper. - {name}
Could someone deliver a sealed letter to {recipient}? Just a reminder of how lucky I am. Reward offered.
Wanted: a messenger for a letter to my dear {recipient}. Handle with care. It's mostly heart.
I want to surprise {recipient} with a letter in the middle of an ordinary day. Will you carry it? - {name}
A letter for {recipient}, sealed with wax and a lot of love. Please take it over when you can.
notice.letter.apology: {recipient} and I had words, and I said the wrong ones. I've written better ones. Could you deliver them? - {name}
Wanted: someone to carry a letter to {recipient}. It says sorry. I've been too proud to say it out loud.
Please take this letter to {recipient}. I was wrong, and I'd like us to be friends again. - {name}
Could someone deliver a sealed letter to {recipient}? We quarreled over something silly, and I miss how things were.
I owe {recipient} an apology, and I've written it down so I won't make a mess of it. Please carry it over. - {name}
notice.birthday: {celebrant}'s birthday is {when}, and I'm planning a surprise. I need {wanted}. Not a word to {celebrant}! - {name}
Secret notice! It's {celebrant}'s birthday on {birthday}. Please help me gather {wanted} for a surprise. Shh.
I'd like to make {celebrant}'s birthday one to remember. It's {when}. Could someone bring me {wanted}? Keep it quiet.
Wanted: {wanted}, for a birthday surprise. I mustn't say whose. Oh, fine: it's {celebrant}'s, on {birthday}. Please don't let it slip.
{celebrant} has done so much for everyone this year. For the birthday {when}, I want to give something back. I need {wanted}. - {name}
Help me surprise {celebrant}! Birthday on {birthday}. Bring {wanted} to me, not to {celebrant}, whatever you do.
Birthday plans for {celebrant}, {when}. I'm gathering {wanted}. If you see {celebrant}, act natural. - {name}
Please, someone help with a surprise for {celebrant}'s birthday. It's {when}, and I'm still short of {wanted}.
It's {celebrant}'s birthday on {birthday} and I want everything to be perfect. That means {wanted}. Please help. - {name}
A surprise is brewing for {celebrant}'s birthday on {birthday}. My part of it needs {wanted}. Reward in emeralds and cake.
To whoever reads this: {celebrant}'s birthday is {when}. I'm planning something lovely and I need {wanted}. Don't spoil it!
notice.thanks.hunt: You dealt with them? Every one? Thank you. I'll sleep like a log tonight.
Thank you for answering my notice. That was brave work, and you made it look easy.
They're gone? Truly? Oh, thank you. Here, you've more than earned this.
The whole village is safer for what you did. Thank you, {player}.
You came back in one piece! That was what I was most worried about. Thank you.
I knew someone would answer that notice. I hoped it would be you. Thank you.
Thank you! Tonight I'm going to walk to the well after dark, just because I can.
Not a scratch on you? Well, a few scratches. Thank you for taking them on for us.
Thank you. I'll take the notice down and pin up a thank-you in its place.
You did it! I'll tell everyone at supper who to thank.
That's a weight off my mind. Thank you, truly. Here's what I promised.
Thank you, brave adventurer. I'll be telling this story for weeks. With some exaggeration.
Gone, all of them? Then I owe you. Thank you, from me and my poor nerves.
notice.thanks.fetch: You brought it! Exactly what I needed. Thank you!
Thank you for answering my notice. You've saved me a long, grumbling walk.
Oh, wonderful. This is just right. Thank you, {player}.
You found it all? Thank you! I'll put it to good use straight away.
Thank you! I'd started to think nobody read that board.
Just what I asked for, and quicker than I hoped. Thank you.
Thank you kindly. Here's your reward, as promised. I always keep my promises.
Look at that. All of it. Thank you, I'm very grateful.
You've got a good eye and quick feet. Thank you for fetching this.
Thank you! This means I can finally get on with things.
I could hug you. I'm going to hug you. Thank you!
Thank you! I'll take the notice down now. It's done its job, and so have you.
Every bit of it! You're a marvel. Thank you.
notice.thanks.letter: You delivered it? Thank you. I've been nervous all day wondering.
Thank you for carrying my letter. Did it arrive safely? Of course it did. You carried it.
It's delivered? Oh, good. Thank you, {player}. Some things are easier to write than to say.
Thank you! A letter's only words until somebody carries it. Then it's a promise kept.
You took it straight there? Thank you. You're a reliable sort. I like that.
Thank you for being my messenger. Here, for your trouble. And for not peeking.
It's arrived? Then my part's done, and the rest is up to the reader. Thank you.
Thank you so much. I'll write again soon, and I know exactly who I'll ask to carry it.
notice.thanks.birthday: You brought it! Now the surprise is ready. Thank you, and not a word to anyone!
Thank you! This birthday is going to be perfect, and it's partly thanks to you.
Oh, wonderful. I'll hide this somewhere safe until the big day. Thank you!
Thank you for helping with the surprise. Come to the party and see it land.
Shh! Thank you! I'll tuck this away before anyone sees.
You've saved the birthday! Well, my part of it. Thank you, {player}.
Thank you. Birthdays are better when the whole village helps, and you're part of the village now.
Exactly what the surprise needed. Thank you! I can hardly wait.
baby.notice.thanks: You did it! You really did it! Thank you!
Thank you! You're the best adventurer in the whole world!
Wow! You read my notice! Nobody ever reads my notices!
Thank you! Here's your reward. I counted it twice!
You're a real hero! I'm going to tell everybody!
Thank you! I'm going to draw a picture of you doing it!
Yay! Thank you! Can I give you a hug? I'm giving you a hug.
Thank you thank you thank you! That's three thank yous!
letter.read.friend: A letter from {sender}? How lovely. I'll read it by the window with a cup of something.
Oh! From {sender}! We've been meaning to catch up for ages. Thank you for bringing it.
A letter from {sender}. I'll write back tonight. Do you carry replies? Never mind, I'll find you.
{sender} wrote to me? That's made my day. Thank you, {player}.
Ha! I can tell from the handwriting that {sender} was in a hurry. Thank you for carrying it.
A letter from an old friend. There's nothing better. Thank you for bringing it all the way from {sender}.
letter.read.family: A letter from {sender}! Family news, I expect. Thank you for bringing it over.
Oh, {sender} wrote. That's family for you, writing when a short walk would do. I love it. Thank you.
From {sender}? I'll read it at supper. Thank you, dear.
A letter from {sender}. I was only just thinking about family. Thank you for this.
Thank you! {sender} always writes such long letters. I'll need a chair.
From {sender}! I'll keep this with the others. There's a whole drawer of them.
letter.read.crush: A letter? From {sender}? For me? Oh. Oh my. Thank you. I think I need to sit down.
{sender} wrote to me? I'll, um, read it later. Somewhere private. Thank you.
A sealed letter from {sender}. My hands are shaking a little. Isn't that silly? Thank you.
For me? From {sender}? I always wondered. I mean, thank you. Thank you for bringing it.
Oh! Is it really from {sender}? Don't look at me, I'm going red. Thank you.
A letter from {sender}. I'll read it tonight by candlelight, which seems right somehow. Thank you.
letter.read.partner: A letter from {sender}? We saw each other at breakfast! Oh, that's so sweet. Thank you.
From {sender}. Even after all this time, my heart still jumps. Thank you for bringing it.
A love letter in the middle of the day. {sender} knows exactly how to make me smile. Thank you.
Oh, {sender}. Always full of surprises. Thank you for carrying this, {player}.
A letter from {sender}! I'll keep it in my pocket all day. Thank you.
{sender} wrote me a letter. I'm going to pretend to be calm about it. I'm not calm. Thank you!
letter.read.apology: A letter from {sender}? After our quarrel? I'll read it. I'll read it twice. Thank you.
{sender} wrote to me? I hope it's an apology. I've been wanting to say sorry too. Thank you for bringing this.
From {sender}. I'd been too stubborn to make the first move. Thank you for carrying it.
A letter from {sender}. I was cross, but I've missed us being friends. Thank you.
From {sender}? Then I'll read it, and then I'll go and knock on that door. Thank you.
Thank you for bringing this. {sender} and I said silly things. Maybe now we can stop.
notice.thanks.later: I saw my notice had come down from the board. That was you, wasn't it? Thank you.
Someone took my notice down, and everything was sorted by the time I got there. I had a feeling it was you. Thank you!
There you are! My notice was gone from the board when I went to check. I've been wanting to thank you ever since.
I went to the board and my notice was gone. I asked around, and everyone said the same name. Yours. Thank you.
You answered my notice while I was out. I'm sorry I missed you. Thank you, {player}, truly.
My notice came down and I never got to say thank you properly. So: thank you. Properly.
I hear it was you who took care of my notice. I wish I'd been there to see it. Thank you!
Ah, the mystery helper! My notice vanished from the board, and I'd bet my boots it was you. Thank you.
I kept meaning to find you. Thank you for seeing to my notice. It made my whole week easier.
Was it you who finished my notice on the board? I thought so. You've a habit of helping. Thank you.
I missed you at the board, but word gets around in {village}. Thank you for answering my notice.
baby.notice.thanks.later: My notice is gone from the board! Was it you? It was you! Thank you!
I looked at the board and my notice wasn't there! You did it, didn't you? Thank you!
Somebody did my notice and I think it was you! You're the best!
I wanted to say thank you but you were gone! So thank you now! Thank you!
My notice got done while I was having my nap! Thank you, secret hero!
You did my notice! I told everybody it was you. I hope it was you.
held.sword: Careful with that sword! Point it somewhere that isn't me.
That's a fine blade. Use it to protect, not to bully.
You can put the sword away, {player}. Nobody here's going to bite you.
Is that {item}? Looks like it's seen a few fights.
Swords make me nervous. Even friendly ones.
A sword like that could keep a whole village safe. Keep it sharp.
Mind your swing near the chickens, please.
Our knights would admire a blade like that.
held.axe: Chopping trees? Leave a few for the birds.
An axe! The carpenter would love to borrow that.
That's a sharp-looking axe. Careful near my fence.
Plant a sapling for every tree you cut. That's the rule round here.
You look like you've been cutting wood all day. Smell of sap and everything.
Axes make good shields-breakers, I hear. Not that I'd know.
Going lumberjacking? The birch grove's to the north.
held.pickaxe: Off to the mines? Watch out for lava.
A pickaxe! Find any diamonds lately?
Is that {item}? Looks like it's been chewing through stone.
Never dig straight down. My grandfather's rule.
You've got stone dust all over you. Been mining?
Bring a torch for every pickaxe swing. Caves are dark.
If you find iron, the smiths will buy it.
Miners always come back with the best stories. And the worst dust.
held.shovel: Digging something up? Or burying something? I won't ask.
A shovel! Want to help with my garden?
Gravel, sand, dirt. The shovel's for the honest work.
Careful you don't dig up the path again.
Is that for making paths? The village could use a few more.
I once dug a hole so deep I had to call for help.
Shovels are underrated. Everyone loves a pickaxe, nobody thanks the shovel.
held.hoe: A hoe! Are you a farmer now too?
Come help with the harvest, if you're handy with that.
Till the dirt near water and it'll stay farmland.
Nice hoe. The farmer would approve.
Planting something? Carrots grow fast here.
Don't swing that near my flowers, please.
Farming's honest work. Glad to see you trying it.
held.bow: A bow! Our archers would like a look at that.
Careful with that string. It bites.
Is that {item}? Looks well cared for.
Shoot the archery target sometime. It'll tell you your score.
Bows are quiet. That's why the archers love them.
Mind you don't shoot the chickens. Or me.
held.trident: A trident! Did you take that from a drowned? Brave.
That's a strange weapon. It looks like it wants to swim.
Throw that in the rain and they say lightning follows. Don't, please.
Ooh, is that from the ocean? It smells of salt.
I've never seen one up close. Can I... no. I won't touch it.
A trident's a sailor's weapon. Are you a sailor now?
held.shield: A shield! Smart. Shields save lives.
That's a sturdy shield. Did the armorer make it?
Crouch behind that when the skeletons start shooting.
I like a person who carries a shield. Shows sense.
Is that your banner on the front? Very fancy.
Our knights swear by shields. So should you.
held.fishing_rod: Going fishing? The river's best in the morning.
A fishing rod! The fisherman would want to compare notes.
Catch me a salmon while you're at it?
Patience, a good rod and a quiet spot. That's all you need.
If you catch a boot, keep it. You never know.
The fish bite better in the rain, they say.
Fishing's my favorite way to waste an afternoon.
held.map: Is that a map? Can I see? Where have you been?
Maps are wonderful. Every corner a promise.
The cartographer would love to see your map.
Show me where {village} is on that. Is it there? We're famous!
That map's well worn. You've been places.
If you get lost, follow the river downhill. Rivers always find people.
Are you marking us on your map? Put a little bell where the village is.
held.compass: A compass! Which way's north? I always forget.
Does your compass point home, or somewhere else?
Clever little thing, a compass. Never lies.
I'd get lost in my own garden without one of those.
Is that a clock? Or a compass? I can never tell them apart from here.
Keep that close on your travels. It'll bring you back.
held.book: A book! What are you reading?
Ooh, is that enchanted? It's glowing a little.
The librarian would want to borrow that.
Books are the best company. Except you, of course.
What's the story about? Tell me without spoiling the ending.
Is that a journal? Do you write about us?
Reading's my favorite way to travel without moving.
Bring that to the archives if you want a copy of the village chronicle.
held.flower: Oh, a flower! Is that for me? No? Still lovely.
That's a pretty flower. Did you pick it in the meadow?
Flowers make everything better. Even swords. Maybe not swords.
A flower in hand is worth two in the garden. Or something like that.
The golem likes flowers. Did you know? It gives them to the children.
That color's beautiful. You could make a lovely dye from it.
held.emerald: That's a nice shiny emerald. Spend it wisely.
Emeralds make the village go round.
Careful flashing emeralds around. Not everyone's as honest as us.
Oh, I could do a lot with one of those. A new hat, for a start.
Are you rich, {player}? You look rich today.
The wandering trader's prices would make your emeralds weep.
held.diamond: Is that a diamond? A real one? Goodness!
Diamonds! Where did you find that?
Put that away before someone faints.
A diamond like that could buy half the village. Well, not the bell.
I've only seen a diamond once before. It was in a sword.
Make something strong with that. A pickaxe, maybe.
held.gold: Gold! The piglins would love you.
Gold's pretty, but it's soft. Don't make tools with it.
Is that real gold? It's so bright.
A golden apple needs a lot of gold. Just saying.
Gold armor looks lovely and breaks in a breeze.
Careful, the wandering trader's eyes just lit up.
held.torch: Good thinking, carrying a torch. Monsters hate the light.
A torch! The path's dark after sunset. Put one by the well?
Mind you don't set the hay on fire.
Light the way, {player}. Somebody has to.
Torches keep the zombies away. Mostly.
The more torches, the safer the village. That's my motto.
held.bucket: A bucket? Fetching water? The well's that way.
Is that lava? Please tell me that's not lava.
Milk! Is that milk? Fresh milk cures all sorts of nasty potions.
Water bucket! Very useful if you fall from somewhere high.
Careful not to spill that on my doorstep.
Buckets are the unsung heroes of the village.
held.crops: Seeds! Planting something? The farmer would be thrilled.
Carrots, potatoes, wheat. The good stuff.
Are you helping with the harvest? Bless you.
That's a lot of crops. Making bread? Stew? Both?
Plant them near water and they'll grow fast.
A sapling! Plant it somewhere it can grow tall.
You smell like a field. A nice field.
held.egg: An egg! Are you going to throw it? Please don't throw it.
Throw an egg and sometimes a chicken pops out. Strange, but true.
Eggs for cake! Do you bake?
Is that a turtle egg? Put it back on the beach!
Chickens lay eggs everywhere here. You're welcome to them.
held.totem: Is that a totem of undying? Hold onto that. Literally.
That totem looks ancient. Where did you get it?
They say a totem can cheat death once. Don't test it.
Evokers carry those. You fought an evoker? Goodness.
A totem! You must have been somewhere dangerous.
held.elytra: Wings! You can fly with those? Truly?
Is that an elytra? From the End cities? I've only read about them!
Fireworks and wings. What a way to travel.
Don't crash into the bell tower, please.
I'd be terrified to fly. And also thrilled.
held.tnt: Is that TNT? Put it down. Gently. Very gently.
Please don't light that near my house.
Explosives in the village? The golem won't like that.
I hope that's for mining. Far away from here.
That makes me more nervous than a creeper.
TNT and flint? You're a walking disaster, {player}.
held.potion: A potion! What does it do? Does it glow?
The cleric would want to know what's in that bottle.
Be careful what you drink, {player}. Not everything bubbling is friendly.
Is that a healing potion? Smart to carry one.
That color's interesting. Smells like nether wart.
Potions make me nervous. Last one I drank turned me invisible for a day.
held.treat: Is that cake? Are you sharing? You should be sharing.
A treat for me? No? A treat for you, then. Fair.
Sweet berries are lovely. Prickly to pick, though.
held.food: Hungry? You should eat that before it gets cold.
That smells delicious. Did you cook it?
Food's for sharing, they say. I'm just saying they say it.
Eat up! Adventurers need their strength.
Is that bread? Good bread? Let me see.
You've got a good meal there. The cook would approve.
Bring some of that to the tavern and you'll make friends fast.
held.raw_food: That's raw! You'll want to cook that first.
The cook's stove would have that sizzling in no time.
Raw meat? Smoker, furnace or campfire. Not your mouth.
That'll cook twice as fast on our kitchen stove.
Fresh catch? Or fresh from the field? Either way, cook it.
Don't eat that raw. I'm begging you.
held.music: The bard would love to hear you play.
Is that a lute? Play the music stand with it and listen to the sound.
A bell! Don't ring it, it'll start a panic.
Music makes the village feel alive.
held.pet: A name tag! Are you naming someone?
A lead? Do you have a pet? Is it a llama?
I'd name a pet something grand. Lord Fluffington.
Saddles are for horses, pigs and the very brave.
Tame a wolf and you'll never walk alone.
Every pet deserves a good name.
held.wool: Wool! The tailor could make something lovely from that.
Shears? Shearing sheep? Be gentle with them.
That wool's soft. Is it from our flock?
You could make a bed from that. Or a banner.
Bring wool to the sewing table and it'll unravel into string.
Colored wool brightens up any house.
held.wood: Logs! Bring them to the sawmill for extra planks.
Building something? I love building things.
The carpenter would get you six planks a log.
Is that oak? Or birch? I can never tell when it's not on a tree.
held.ore: Iron! The smiths will be glad to see that.
Raw ore? Smelt it before you trade it.
Copper's pretty when it's new. Goes green when it's old. Like me.
Bring that to the blast furnace. Twice as fast.
held.paint: A paintbrush! Are you an artist?
Dyes! You could finish the painting on the easel with those.
Colors in your hands. I like that.
Blue dye makes the sea, red makes flowers. On our easel, anyway.
Are you planning to paint the village? Paint my door blue.
player.hurt: You're hurt! Sit down a moment. Let me look at you.
Goodness, you're bleeding! Have you got any bandages?
You look like you lost a fight with a skeleton. Did you?
Rest before you go anywhere. Please.
The apothecary can patch you up. Or eat something. Food helps.
I don't like seeing you hurt, {player}.
Bandages, potions, a warm bed. You need all three.
player.hungry: You look hungry. When did you last eat?
Your stomach's growling louder than the bell.
Get something to eat, {player}. You can't adventure on an empty belly.
The cook's stove has a dish of the day, if they've been working.
Have some bread. You look peaky.
Hungry adventurers make mistakes. Eat something.
I can hear your stomach from here.
You need a good meal. The tavern does a lovely stew.
player.wet: You're soaked to the bone! Come out of the rain.
Look at you, dripping on my doorstep.
Did you swim here? You look like you swam here.
Stand by a fire and dry off before you catch a cold.
Your boots are squelching. I can hear them.
Rain got you, did it? It gets everyone eventually.
A hooded poncho would keep that off. The tailor makes lovely ones.
You smell like wet wool. No offense.
player.fire: You're on fire! Water! Somebody get water!
Stop, drop and roll! Or jump in the well!
Why are you smoking? Literally smoking!
Fire! You're on fire! Why are you so calm?!
Please don't stand near the hay.
Did you fall in lava? Get to water, quick!
player.riding: Look at you up there! What a fine steed.
Mind your animal doesn't eat my flowers.
Riding into the village like a hero. Very dramatic.
Is that comfortable? It looks comfortable.
Don't let it trample the crops, please.
player.pumpkin: Why are you wearing a pumpkin on your head?
Is that a pumpkin? Are you hiding from the endermen?
You look like a scarecrow with ambitions.
I can't tell if you're smiling under there.
The endermen won't stare at you, at least. Very sensible. Very silly.
Nice hat. Very orange. Very round.
Can you even see out of that thing?
You smell like pie, {player}. Is it the pumpkin?
player.elytra: You've got wings! Where did you get wings?
Is that an elytra on your back? Can you really fly?
Fly over the bell tower! Please! I want to see!
Wings and all. You really are an adventurer.
I've only read about elytras. Is it as wonderful as it sounds?
You must have been to the End. Nobody comes back with wings otherwise.
player.diamond: Look at that armor! You sparkle like a geode.
Diamond armor! You must be very brave. Or very rich.
I can see my reflection in your chestplate.
You look like a hero from a story.
That armor must have cost a fortune.
Nobody's going to mess with you in that.
Shiny! You'll scare the zombies just by glinting at them.
Is that netherite? It's so dark. Very serious-looking.
player.golden: Golden armor! Very fancy. Very soft.
You look like a king. Or a very confident piglin.
That gold's going to dent if you sneeze.
The piglins would love you right now.
Golden armor? Going to a party?
player.leather: Leather armor? Simple and sturdy. Good choice for a start.
You look like a proper traveler in that leather.
Leather's light. Easy to run in. Smart.
Did you dye that? It's a lovely color.
You've got the look of a hunter.
player.unarmored: No armor? Out in the wilds? You're braver than I am.
Where's your armor, {player}? The skeletons won't be gentle.
You should get some armor. The armorer can help.
Out and about with no armor. Bold.
Even a leather cap would help, you know.
I worry when I see you without armor.
player.dark: It's dark out. You should be inside, or at least near a torch.
Walking around at night? Stay near the lamps.
The night's full of things you don't want to meet.
Don't stay out too long, {player}. The zombies are about.
It's black as pitch out there. Mind your step.
Have you got a torch? You should have a torch.
Night walks are lovely until something groans at you.
The golem's on patrol, but you should still be careful.
remember.likes_rain: You told me you love the rain. I thought of you all through the last storm.
Rain-lover! I saved a puddle for you. It's by the well.
I walked in the rain yesterday because you said you liked it. You're right. It's lovely.
remember.fond_village: You said {village} was your favorite. I've been telling everyone. You're famous now.
I keep remembering what you said about {village}. It made us all a bit prouder.
You love it here. I can tell. And we love having you.
remember.trait_generous: You said you'd share your last loaf. I believe it. You've got a generous heart.
I told {neighbor} how generous you are. They didn't seem surprised.
Generous people like you make the world softer. Thank you.
remember.likes_fishing: You like fishing, don't you? The salmon are running this week.
I found a good spot by the river and thought of you. Bring your rod.
Fancy a fishing trip soon? You said you liked it. I haven't forgotten.
remember.likes_cats: You're a cat person! There's a new kitten by the bakery. You'd love her.
The village cats have been asking about you. Well, one meowed at me. Same thing.
I saw a cat sleeping on a pumpkin and thought of you.
remember.fond_bell: You said the bell was the best. I gave it a little polish in your honor.
Every time the bell rings now, I think of what you said.
The bell rang at noon and I said "that one's for {player}." The cleric gave me a look.
remember.drink_coffee: Strong coffee, you said! The tap's full this morning, if you've got a mug.
I tried my coffee strong like you. My hands haven't stopped shaking.
You're the coffee one! I remember. The tavern keeper does a lovely mug.
remember.drink_cider: Warm cider, wasn't it? The barrel's been freshly pressed.
You like cider. I'll save you a mug at the tavern.
The apples this year are perfect for your cider.
remember.drink_milk: Cold milk in the morning! You were right. I tried it. Very refreshing.
Milk-drinker! The cows have been very productive this week.
remember.dream_cottage: You dreamed of a cozy cottage. I saw a perfect spot by the stream. Just saying.
Still dreaming of that little cottage? Build it near us, would you?
I keep thinking about your cottage dream. It sounds like the nicest dream.
remember.dream_castle: How's your castle in the clouds coming along? I want a tower room.
You wanted to build a castle! Have you started? Do you need a bell for it?
remember.dream_farm: A giant farm, you said! The farmer's got opinions on how you should start.
You and your giant farm. You'd feed the whole Overworld.
remember.dream_redstone: Have you built your redstone machine yet? What does it do? Never mind, I'll just be impressed.
You and redstone! I still don't understand it. I still think it's wonderful.
remember.writes_journal: Did you write about today in your journal? Write something nice about me.
I've started a journal too, because of you. Mostly I draw cats in it.
Your journal must be enormous by now.
remember.why_see: You want to see everything. Have you seen something new since we last talked?
Still seeing the world? Tell me the best new thing.
remember.why_people: You said you travel for the people you meet. I hope I'm one of the good ones.
You travel for people. I keep thinking about that. It's the nicest reason.
I told {neighbor} why you travel. They said "for people? That's lovely." It is.
remember.why_build: You said you want to build something great. I hope you'll show us when it's done.
How's the great building project? Bigger than the church yet?
remember.wants_swim: You'd rather breathe underwater. I saw a turtle today and thought of you.
Still wishing you could swim like a fish? There's a potion for that, I've heard.
remember.wants_fly: You wanted to fly! Have you found wings yet? Elytra, they call them.
I watched the birds today and thought of you. You'd love it up there.
remember.wants_animals: You'd talk to animals if you could. The goat has been very chatty lately. Try him.
I'm sure the cats would tell you everything. You'd hear so much gossip.
remember.travels_wolf: How's your wolf? You said you travel with one. Give it a scratch from me.
Bring your wolf by sometime! The village dogs would love a new friend.
remember.travels_friends: Still traveling with friends? Bring them here sometime.
Adventures with friends are the best kind. You told me that.
remember.travels_alone: You said you travel alone. Take care of yourself out there. Someone here worries.
Lonely roads are long. Come back to us often.
remember.trait_trusty: You said you'd never tell a secret. So here's one: I'm glad we're friends.
I trust you. You keep secrets. That's rare.
remember.trait_tidy: You sort your chests by type! I still think about that. Wonderful.
Your chests must be the tidiest in the Overworld.
remember.trait_miner: You're a miner at heart. The old mineshaft east of here might interest you.
remember.trait_honest: You'd ask around about a lost emerald. That's why I trust you.
Honest folk are rare. You're one of them.
remember.trait_healer: You said you'd cure a zombie neighbor. That stays with me. Thank you.
I feel safer knowing you'd try to cure one of us. You know how. Weakness and gold.
remember.trait_farmer: How are your crops coming along, farmer?
A farmer at heart! The wheat's high this year. You'd be proud.
remember.trait_explorer: Where's the explorer been this time? Tell me everything.
You're always off somewhere new. Explorer through and through.
remember.trait_careful: You said you're careful. Good. Stay that way out there.
remember.trait_builder: How's the building going, builder? Need any planks? The sawmill's busy.
You're a builder. The carpenter's been asking about you.
remember.trait_brave: Brave as ever, I see. Just don't be too brave.
You told me you're brave. I believe it now. I've seen your armor dents.
remember.talent_cooking: You can cook! When are you cooking for me? I'm waiting.
I still want to taste your cooking. Bring something next time.
remember.song_jig: The bard's been working on your jig. It's very bouncy. You'll love it.
Your jig is nearly ready! The bard's been humming it all week.
remember.song_ballad: Your ballad's up to forty verses. The bard can't stop.
The bard sang a bit of your ballad at the tavern. Everyone cried. In a good way.
remember.sleeps_stars: Still sleeping under the stars? Watch for spiders.
I slept outside last night because you made it sound nice. A spider walked on my face.
remember.sleeps_bed: Still carrying your bed around? Very wise. Very heavy, I'd imagine.
A bed in your pack. I still think that's clever.
remember.season_winter: Winter's your season! I'll save you a spot by the fire when the snow comes.
You love winter. The first frost made me think of you.
remember.season_summer: Summer's your favorite! The river's warm enough to swim in now.
You love summer. Long days, warm nights. Enjoy them.
remember.season_spring: Spring's your time. The blossoms are coming out by the church.
You love spring. Everything new. Like you, every time you visit.
remember.season_autumn: Autumn, you said! The pumpkins are coming in nicely.
You love the harvest. You'd love our harvest festival. If we had one. We should.
remember.promise_garden: You said you'd plant something with me. I've saved the seeds. Whenever you're ready.
Our garden plan! I've marked out a little spot. It's waiting for us.
remember.promise_defend: You said you'd help if trouble came. I've told the guards. They're glad.
I sleep better knowing you'd come if the bell rang.
remember.promise_adventure: You said you'd take me on an adventure someday. I've packed. Twice.
Is today the day? For our adventure? No? Tomorrow, then.
I've been training for our adventure. I walked to the river and back. Twice.
remember.plays_tag: You played tag with me! You're it! Still! Forever!
Will you play again? You promised! Sort of!
remember.plays_snowball: I've been saving snowballs for our fight. Well, they melted. I'll make more.
Snowball rematch when the snow comes back! You're not getting away.
remember.plays_nap: The haystack's ready for our nap. Same time as usual?
Napping together was the best idea you've ever agreed to.
remember.pet_sir: How's Sir Barks-a-Lot? Have you found him yet? I keep imagining him.
If you ever get a wolf, I'm holding you to the name Sir Barks-a-Lot.
remember.pet_biscuit: Did you name a wolf Biscuit yet? I need to know.
Biscuit! I still think that's the cutest name ever.
remember.number_64: Sixty-four! A full stack. I see your lucky number everywhere now.
I counted sixty-four seeds today and thought of you.
remember.loves_ocean: You love the ocean. I hope you get to see it again soon.
I painted the sea after you told me about it. It's very blue. Mostly blue.
remember.loves_mountains: The snowy mountains, you said. I looked at the hills and imagined them taller.
Have you been back to the mountains? Tell me about the snow up there.
remember.loves_cherry: The cherry groves! I dreamt about them after you told me. Everything pink.
You love the cherry groves. I'd love to see one with you someday.
remember.likes_sweet: Something sweet for the sweet-tooth! The baker's got honey cakes today.
You're the cake person. I'll let you know when there's cake. There's always cake somewhere.
remember.likes_sunset: The sunset last night made me think of you. All orange and gold.
You're a sunset person. There's a good one coming tonight, I can feel it.
remember.likes_sunrise: I watched the sunrise this morning because you said you love them. You're right.
Sunrise person! You'd have loved this morning's. Pink everywhere.
remember.likes_sun: A fine sunny day, just how you like it.
Sunshine for the sunshine person! Enjoy it.
remember.likes_snow: You love snow! I'll make a snow golem for you when it comes.
I thought of you when the first flakes fell. You'd have been out in it.
remember.likes_savory: The stew-lover! The cook's made a big pot today.
You'd rather have stew than cake. I'll never understand it. I respect it.
remember.likes_parrots: Seen any parrots lately? I still want one that says my name.
You and your parrots! The jungle traders have one, I think.
remember.likes_music: You love a good jig. The bard's playing tonight. Come by.
The bard asked if the jig-lover was in town. That's you!
remember.likes_dogs: A dog person! The village dogs have been extra waggy since you visited.
I saw a puppy today and thought of you.
remember.likes_bread: The bread-lover! The bakery smells amazing this morning.
Bread, just bread. You were right. I had some plain bread today. Perfect.
remember.idea_wall: I told the guards your idea about the wall. They're considering it. Slowly.
Your wall idea came up at the meeting. Very heated debate.
remember.idea_tavern: Your bigger tavern idea is very popular. The bard's started a petition.
Everyone agrees with you about the tavern. The tavern keeper agrees the loudest.
remember.idea_snow: A first snow festival! I keep thinking about your idea. Lanterns in the snow.
Your snow festival idea! We'll do it this winter. I've decided.
remember.idea_lanterns: I mentioned your lantern idea. A few more lanterns went up by the well. Your doing.
More lanterns, you said. The path by the church has two new ones now.
remember.idea_harvest: A harvest festival! I've started planning. Pies. So many pies.
Your harvest festival idea has everyone excited. The farmer most of all.
remember.idea_golem: A festival for the golem! I gave it a poppy and told it your idea. It seemed pleased.
The golem doesn't know about its festival yet. Let's keep it a surprise.
remember.hours_late: Night owl! Make sure you sleep sometimes. The phantoms are watching.
Up late again? I could tell. You've got that night-owl glow.
remember.hours_early: An early riser like you would love the morning mist we had today.
Up with the sun, as always? Good for you.
remember.home_wanderer: Still wandering? You've always got a bed in {village}, you know.
Every wanderer needs somewhere to come back to. Let it be here.
remember.home_village: You said {village} was your home. I haven't stopped smiling about it.
Welcome home, {player}. You said it was home, so I'm saying it.
remember.home_built: How's the house you built? Any new rooms?
You built your own home. I'd love to see it someday. Or a painting of it.
remember.food_steak: The butcher's got good steak today. I thought of you.
A steak person! Well cooked, you said. I remember.
remember.food_pie: The baker made pumpkin pie this morning. I asked her to save a slice for you.
Pumpkin pie for the pie lover. It's in season.
remember.food_carrots: Golden carrots! Fancy as ever, I'm sure.
I saw a golden carrot at the market and thought, that's {player}'s favorite.
remember.fears_warden: You faced the warden. I still can't believe it. Brave, brave {player}.
I told the children you met the warden. They hid under the table for an hour.
remember.fears_endermen: Don't look any endermen in the eye this week, all right?
I wear a pumpkin in the garden now, because of what you said about endermen.
remember.fears_creepers: Seen any creepers lately? Watch your back, they're sneaky.
I got a cat because of your creeper stories. She's fierce.
remember.enchant_unbreaking: Hard to break, you said. That's you, I think.
Unbreaking. I keep thinking about your answer. It suits you.
remember.enchant_mending: Mending, you said. Healing as you grow. I think about that a lot.
Learning and mending. That's the best kind of life.
remember.color_red: Red, your favorite color! The poppies are blooming.
I painted my door red because of you. Well, partly because of you.
remember.color_purple: Purple! I found an amethyst shard and kept it for you.
Your favorite color's all over the sky at dusk tonight.
remember.color_green: Green, your color. The hills are so green this week.
Green, like the hills. And like creepers, unfortunately.
remember.color_blue: The sky's your color today. Lovely and blue.
I used so much blue in my last painting. For you.
remember.collects_gems: How's your gem collection? Anything new and sparkly?
I found a shiny pebble for your collection. It's not a gem. It's very shiny though.
remember.collects_friends: You collect friends, you said. I'm proud to be one.
How many friends in your collection now? I hope I'm near the top.
remember.collects_flowers: I pressed a flower for your collection. A cornflower. Very blue.
How's your flower collection? I saw a rare one by the river.
remember.collects_discs: Found any new music discs? I've never heard one play.
Your music disc collection must be wonderful.
remember.chronicle_yes: You're in the chronicle now! Right after the bit about the goat on the roof.
I've written about your last visit. It's a very flattering entry.
remember.cared_fed: Have you been eating properly since we talked? Truly?
I've got food for you again. I haven't forgotten my promise.
remember.birthday_today: Happy belated birthday! I've been thinking about it since you told me.
Birthday person! Did you do anything special? You should have.
remember.birthday_market: It's nearly your birthday! Market Day, remember? We agreed!
Every Market Day's your birthday now. That's the rule.
greet.routine.sleep: Mm? Oh, hello. I was just about to turn in.
Hello. It's my bedtime, but I can spare a minute.
Yawn... sorry. Hello! I should really be asleep.
Oh, you caught me in my nightcap. Hello.
Hello. Keep it short, my pillow's calling my name.
Hello! I'm officially off duty. Unofficially, I'm still nosy.
greet.routine.nap: Wha? Oh! I wasn't napping. Hello.
Hello... I was resting my eyes. Both of them. Very thoroughly.
Mm. Five more minutes. Oh, it's you. Hello!
Hello! You woke me from a very important nap.
Shh. I'm napping. Officially. But hello.
Hello. My afternoon nap is sacred, but you're allowed.
greet.routine.wake: Mmh. Morning. I'm still finding my feet.
Hello! I just got up. My hair's still deciding which way to go.
Oh, hello. Give me a moment, my eyes are only half open.
Good morning! I'm awake. Mostly. In theory.
Hello! I just washed my face in the cold water bucket. I'm VERY awake now.
Morning. Don't mind the yawning; it's not you, it's the hour.
greet.routine.breakfast: Hello! You caught me mid-breakfast. Want a crust?
Morning! I'm just finishing my porridge.
Hello! Breakfast first, then the world. Sit down.
Ah, hello. Mind the crumbs, I'm a messy eater before noon.
Hello! The eggs were good today. The chickens outdid themselves.
Hello! I always say nothing good happens before breakfast. Then you showed up.
greet.routine.prayer: Peace be with you. I was just finishing my morning prayers.
Hello, friend. The quiet hours are the best for reflection.
Ah, hello. I asked for a good day. Maybe you're the answer.
Hello. Forgive the incense smell; it gets in everything.
Good morning. I lit a candle for everyone in {village} today.
Hello. My prayers are said, my mind is clear. How can I help?
greet.routine.work: Hello! I'm at work, but I can talk while I do this.
Oh, hello! Don't mind me, my hands are busy but my ears are free.
Hello! Busy, busy. What can I do for you?
Ah, a visitor at the workstation. Hello!
Hello! You've caught me in the middle of something. That's always the way.
Hello, {player}. Mind your elbows, there are sharp things about.
Hello! It's a working day, but a chat never hurt anyone.
Hello! My workstation and I were just having a disagreement.
greet.routine.lunch: Hello! Lunchtime! Sit down, I'll share.
Ah, hello! I'm on my lunch break. Best part of the day.
Hello! The bell rang for lunch and I ran.
Hello, {player}! Want a bite? It's only a little squashed.
Hello! Everybody comes out to the bell at lunch. It's like a small festival every day.
Hello! I'm eating, so if I talk with my mouth full, forgive me.
greet.routine.lunch_home: Hello! I popped home for lunch. Nobody steals my soup here.
Oh, hello. I'm having lunch at home today. Quiet's nice sometimes.
Hello! Back home for a bite. Come in, come in.
Hello! My own kitchen, my own chair, my own sandwich. Bliss.
Hello! I always eat better at home. Fewer people asking for some.
Hello! I came home to eat and accidentally started cleaning.
greet.routine.lunch_tavern: Hello! I'm lunching at the tavern. The stew's good today.
Oh, hello! Pull up a chair. The tavern's busy but there's room.
Hello! I treat myself to a tavern lunch now and then.
Hello! You can smell the tavern kitchen from here, can't you?
Hello! Tavern lunch, best lunch. Don't tell my mother.
Ah, hello. Mind the bench, it wobbles.
greet.routine.hobby: Hello! It's my free time, so I'm doing what I love: {hobby}.
Oh, hello! You caught me enjoying a little {hobby}.
Hello! Work's done and now it's time for {hobby}.
Hello, {player}! This is my favorite part of the day.
Hello! I lose track of time completely when I'm {hobby}.
Hello! Don't mind the mess; hobbies are supposed to be messy.
greet.routine.social: Hello! Come join us, we're catching up by the bell.
Hello! This is when the whole village comes out to chat.
Oh, hello! You've arrived at the best hour for gossip.
Hello! The bell's the heart of {village}, and this is its busiest beat.
Hello! I just heard the most interesting thing. I'll tell you if you're nice.
greet.routine.market: Hello! The market's in full swing. Have you seen the stalls?
Happy Market Day! I'm out browsing.
Hello! I'm only here for the honey cakes. And the people. Mostly the cakes.
Hello! Market Day! The busiest, happiest day of the week.
Hello! Everyone's selling something, and I'm buying everything.
Hello! I've been haggling all morning. I lost.
greet.routine.supper: Hello! Supper's on the table. Join us?
Ah, hello. It's suppertime. Smell that?
Hello! I'm just sitting down to eat. You're welcome to the bread.
Hello! Supper's the best meal. It means the day's work is done.
Hello! Come in, there's enough stew for one more.
Oh, hello! I was just washing up the bowls.
greet.routine.evening: Hello! Just relaxing at home. Come in a moment.
Ah, hello. My feet are up and my day is done.
Hello! A quiet evening at home is the finest thing.
Hello, {player}. I was just reading by the lamp.
Hello! Evenings are for slippers and slow talks.
Oh, hello! I wasn't expecting company, but I'm glad of it.
greet.routine.tavern: Hello! Come in, come in, the tavern's warm and loud tonight.
Hello! Pull up a stool, {player}! The cider's good.
Ah, hello! Evening at the tavern. Best part of the week.
Hello! Shh, the bard's about to start. Or he's tuning. Hard to tell.
Hello! You'll want to try the cider here, it's pressed fresh.
Hello! Everyone in {village} ends up at the tavern eventually.
greet.routine.perform: Hello! I'm about to go on. Wish me luck!
Ah, an audience member! Hello! Any requests?
Hello! I'm warming up my fingers. And my nerves.
Hello! Tonight's the night. Every night's the night, really.
Hello! Sit close to the front. I sing better when I can see faces.
Hello! Don't clap yet, I haven't played anything.
greet.routine.night_watch: Hello. I'm on watch, so I'll keep my eyes on the dark while we talk.
Evening, {player}. All quiet so far. Let's keep it that way.
Hello. You're out late. Stay close to the torches.
Hello. Night watch. Long hours, cold hands, good stars.
Hello. Heard any groaning out by the fields? No? Good.
greet.routine.defend: Not now! They're coming. Stay close to the bell.
Hello, quickly! Have you got a weapon? We could use it.
Eyes on the treeline, {player}. They'll come from there.
Stand with us or get indoors. Either way, be quick!
Hold steady. We've got this village covered.
greet.routine.play: Hi! We're playing! Want to play?
Hello! I'm hiding! Don't tell anyone where I am.
Hi hi hi! I'm being a dragon! Rawr!
Hello! I've been playing since forever!
Hi! We're having a race! Are you fast?
Hello! I found a really good stick!
greet.routine.lessons: Hello! We're at lessons. Shh, the teacher's watching.
Hi! I'm learning my letters. Want to hear the alphabet?
Hello! Lessons are boring but don't tell anyone I said that.
Hi! We're learning about the stars today!
Hello! I already know all the answers. Mostly.
Hi! I'm supposed to be paying attention. Hello!
greet.routine.shelter: Hello! Come in out of the rain!
Oh, you're drenched! Come stand under the roof.
Hello! I ran home the moment it started pouring.
Hello! Rainy afternoon. Perfect for staying in.
Hello! I got caught halfway across the square. My shoes are full of water.
Hello! Inside's where all the sensible people are today.
greet.routine.storm: Hello! Quick, inside! That lightning's close!
You're out in this? Come in, come in!
Hello! I'm staying put until the sky calms down.
Hello! Every clap of thunder makes me jump. Don't laugh.
Hello! Shut the door, quick! The wind's fierce.
Hello. I'm counting between the flashes and the booms. It's getting closer.
greet.routine.snowed_in: Hello! Come warm your hands by the fire.
Oh, you're covered in snow! Stamp your feet before you come in.
Hello! I'm not going out in that. Not for all the emeralds in the world.
Hello! Cozy day by the hearth for me.
Hello! The snow's piling up against the door.
Hello! I've got a blanket and a warm drink and I'm not moving.
greet.routine.rain_walk: Hello! I love walking in the rain. Everyone thinks I'm odd.
Hello! Don't hide from it, the rain's lovely!
Hello! I'm soaked and happy about it!
Hello! Listen to it pattering on the leaves.
Hello! Puddle-jumping is very serious business.
greet.routine.snow_play: Hello! Snowball fight! Want to join?
Hi! I'm building a snow golem! It doesn't move yet.
Hello! Look how deep the snow is! It's up to my knees!
Hi! Catch a snowflake on your tongue! Like this!
Hello! My nose is frozen and I don't care!
Hi! I made a snow angel! It's a bit square.
routine.sleep: I really should be in bed by now. I'll say goodnight soon.
My eyelids are getting heavy. It's been a long day.
Bedtime, I'm afraid. Even the chickens have turned in.
I'm just about to blow out my lamp. The dark's coming down quick.
My bed's calling me. It's very persuasive.
I'll be dreaming soon. Hopefully about pie again.
I keep my bed by the window so the morning light wakes me. Bit of a trick, that.
Sleep's the best medicine. That, and soup.
I always sleep better after a good day. And today was a good one.
If you hear snoring, it's my neighbor. Definitely not me.
I count sheep to fall asleep. Real ones. There are eleven.
Goodnight soon, {player}. Don't wander too far in the dark.
routine.nap: A nap after lunch is the secret to a long life. Or at least a good mood.
I was in the middle of a lovely nap. I dreamed I was a cloud.
Napping is an art, and I'm a master.
Everyone works so hard. I nap so they don't have to. Balance.
A little rest and I'll be good as new. Or as good as I ever am.
Don't tell anyone I nap every day. It's my secret talent.
The hay in the barn makes the best nap spot. Itchy, but cozy.
I'll be up and about in a bit. Probably. Possibly.
Naps are like little holidays you take every afternoon.
I could nap anywhere. I once napped standing up.
My cat taught me how to nap properly. Find the sunbeam, curl up, ignore everyone.
Shh. The afternoon's for resting. That's the rule.
routine.wake: I just woke up. The world's a bit fuzzy around the edges.
I always wake up hungry. Is that normal? Don't answer.
I had the strangest dream about a flying pig wearing a saddle.
The roosters did their job. Unfortunately.
I like to lie still for a minute when I wake up and listen to the village.
