I'll keep you in one piece, {player}. That's my job.
work.painter: My easel's set up by the window. The light's perfect this time of day.
I paint a new picture every day. Some days it's good. Some days it's a learning experience.
When a painting's finished, take it off my easel and hang it at home. I'll start another.
A dye or two on a blank canvas makes a sketch, then a picture. Try it yourself!
I've been painting the sunset all week. It keeps changing on me.
Blue for the sky, green for the hills, a dab of gold for the sun. That's most landscapes.
I paint portraits too. Sit still and I'll make you famous.
My fingers are every color today.
I wanted to paint the sea, so I mixed blue dye. Blue dye makes ships, apparently.
Mixing colors is like cooking. Too much of anything ruins it.
I've painted every building in {village}. Twice.
A painter sees the world differently. Everything's a shape and a shade.
I've got a painting of a creeper in a meadow. It's my most popular work. I don't understand people.
I sketch in charcoal first. Then the colors come.
My paintbrush has seen things. Mostly the sky.
Art takes patience. And a lot of dye.
I painted the village at night with all the windows lit. It made the cleric cry.
Every finished painting goes to whoever takes it home. Art should be lived with.
The paint pots on my easel tray are always running low.
Painting outdoors is best. Painting in the rain is not.
I'm trying to capture the light on the river. It won't hold still.
Some people collect emeralds. I collect sunsets.
A blank canvas is terrifying and exciting at the same time.
I painted the flowers in a vase this morning. The vase was empty. I imagined the flowers.
My work hangs in half the houses in {village}.
Colors have feelings. Red's angry, blue's calm, yellow's showing off.
I paint what I love. That's why there are so many paintings of bread.
Bring a paintbrush to a finished canvas and I'll show you how to start over.
The best painting I ever did was of my mother. She hung it upside down.
I get paint everywhere. My cat's slightly purple.
I paint best in the afternoons. Morning light's too sharp.
I'm working on a mural for the tavern wall. It's going to be enormous.
Painting is just looking very carefully and then telling the truth with color.
You can have any painting you find finished on my easel. That's a promise.
I see beauty everywhere. Even in mud. Especially in mud. Lovely browns.
work.bard: I play the music stand every evening at the tavern. Come and listen!
Music lifts the spirits. Literally. When I play, everyone works a little faster.
Play the stand yourself if you like. Everyone nearby gets a little spring in their step.
I know songs from every corner of the world. Well, three corners.
My lute's been with me for years. We've been through a lot.
A bard's job is to remember the stories and sing them back.
I'm working on a ballad about {village}. It has thirty verses. So far.
The tavern goes quiet when I start a sad song. That's the best feeling.
I can play "Greensleeves," "Frère Jacques" and a jig I wrote myself.
The children dance when I play. The adults pretend they're not tapping their feet.
I practice at my music stand in the mornings. The roosters harmonize, sort of.
Every song's a little bit of magic. I believe that.
I wrote a lullaby for the golem. It didn't fall asleep. It doesn't sleep.
A tavern without a bard is just a room full of people drinking quietly.
My fingers are calloused from the strings. Worth it.
I play for coins on Market Day. Mostly I get apples.
Music makes the long nights shorter.
Hold a lute and play the stand for a guitar sound. A bell for chimes. An amethyst for something magical.
I've been learning to play the flute. The neighbors have been learning to sleep with pillows over their heads.
Songs are how villages remember who they are.
I once played so long my fingers fell asleep.
Everyone hums my tunes. They don't know they're mine. I don't mind.
A good song can stop an argument mid-shout.
I play a quiet tune at dusk to call everyone home.
My sheet music's mostly scribbles only I can read.
Music is the only thing that sounds better shared.
I'm composing a song for each resident. Yours will have a lot of drums. Adventurous drums.
When the bell rings for a wedding, I play the procession.
Sometimes I just play to the empty square. The pigeons appreciate it.
A bard is a walking library of songs.
I'd play for the Ender Dragon if it'd listen.
I tune my lute every morning. It goes out of tune every afternoon. It's a moody lute.
I've got a new song about a brave chicken. It's a crowd favorite.
Music, stories and a warm mug. That's a bard's whole life.
Play a tune for the village. They'll love you for it.
work.tailor: Needle, thread, and a steady hand. That's tailoring.
Bring me torn leather or a frayed bowstring and I'll mend it at my sewing table. A bit of string, that's all.
Wool unravels into string at my table. Handy if you're out of thread.
I mend the guards' padding while they're on duty. They come back to it good as new.
I've been sewing a rain cloak. Waterproofed with beeswax. Very fashionable.
A good seam is invisible. That's how you know it's good.
I've got pins in my mouth half the day. Don't make me laugh.
Every coat in {village} has a stitch of mine in it somewhere.
Bolts of wine and mustard cloth. My two favorite colors.
I patched the farmer's trousers again. He kneels on everything.
A hooded poncho for every traveler. Rain or shine.
My spool of red thread is my most precious thing.
I measure everyone by eye. You're a size "adventurer," by the way.
I'm making a cloak for the knight. Blue with silver trim.
The trick to sewing is never rushing the last stitch.
Leather boots, wool cloaks, linen shirts. I make it all.
I can mend almost anything. Except a broken heart. Though I try with a nice scarf.
I've been embroidering flowers on the cleric's robes. Don't tell her yet.
Thimbles save fingers. I've learned that the painful way.
My sewing table's covered in scraps. Every scrap's a future patch.
Elytra need delicate mending. Very delicate. Very expensive.
I make uniforms for every trade in the village. Each one's different.
The bard wants a cape with stars on it. I'm on it.
I sew by candlelight in the evenings. Bad for the eyes. Good for the soul.
A well-made garment can last a lifetime.
I found a moth in my wool. We had words.
I'm teaching my niece to sew. She's better at it than I was.
Clothes make people feel like themselves. That's important work.
Fishing rods, bows, crossbows. All mendable with good string.
I've got a pincushion shaped like a tomato. It's very old. It's very loved.
I can tell a lot about a person from the state of their sleeves.
Bring me your worn things. I'll make them good as new.
I darn socks for the whole village. Socks wear out faster than anything.
Fashion comes and goes. Good stitching stays.
Every garment I make, I make it like it's for a friend.
work.carpenter: The sawmill cuts logs into half again as many planks as hand-crafting does. Bring me your logs.
I've been building benches for the village square. Sturdy ones. No more wobbling.
Measure twice, cut once. My father said it. I say it. My apprentice is sick of hearing it.
The saw sings when the wood's good. Squeaks when it's not.
I leave offcuts by the sawmill. Sticks are always handy. Help yourself.
I built half the houses in {village}. The other half I've repaired.
Oak's my favorite. Strong, honest, smells lovely.
Spruce for roofs, oak for floors, birch for furniture. Every wood has its place.
My hands are covered in splinters. Occupational hazard.
I made a rocking chair for my grandmother. She says it's the best chair in the world.
A good joint needs no nails. Just a snug fit.
I'm building a new bridge over the stream. Arched, of course.
Sawdust in my hair, sawdust in my boots, sawdust in my soup.
Planks into sticks, three to a plank at my sawmill. Much better than the crafting table.
I fixed the church door. It stopped creaking. The cleric's thrilled.
A carpenter's work is everywhere. Doors, floors, beds, barrels.
I can tell the age of a tree by its rings. That oak was older than the village.
I carved a little bird for the windowsill. It's mostly for me.
Sanding's the boring part. Also the most important part.
I built a treehouse for the children. They haven't come down since.
The sawmill's the best tool in my workshop. It saves me hours.
Every house in {village} needs fixing eventually. I'm never out of work.
I made a cradle for the newest baby. Smoothed every edge.
Wood breathes, wood moves, wood remembers. You have to respect it.
I've got a hammer for every job and a job for every hammer.
I'd like to build a ship someday. A real one. With a mast.
I mended the well's roof last week. Now it doesn't leak on people's heads.
A crooked shelf is a carpenter's nightmare.
I build things to last. My great-grandchildren will sit on my benches.
I keep a stack of planks by the door. You never know.
My workshop smells of sap and pine. Best smell in the world.
I made the notice board by the bell. Proudest work I've done.
Bamboo's strange wood. Grows fast, splits easy. Saws nicely, though.
Bring me a log and I'll show you what it wants to be.
Woodwork's slow, but it's honest.
work.scholar: I keep the village archives. Every birth, wedding and great event in {village}.
Bring a book to the archives and I'll copy out the village chronicle for you.
Study with me while I work at the archives. You'll learn a thing or two. Literally.
Every neighbor has a story worth keeping. Our archives help us remember where we came from.
I've been cataloguing the village's history. Did you know we once had a mayor who was a llama? Briefly.
Scrolls, ledgers, boxes of letters. The archives are a treasure.
I write down the news every day. Someday, someone will want to know.
History isn't dusty. It's people. People are never dusty.
I'm working on a history of the founding of {village}. Lots of goats in it.
The archives smell of old paper and candle wax. My favorite smell.
Right-click the archives with an empty hand and you'll read the village news. Hold a book to copy it all.
I've read every letter in the archive. Some of them made me cry.
A scholar's work is never done. History keeps happening.
I teach lessons by the bell some mornings. The children are better students than they think.
Knowledge kept is knowledge shared. Eventually.
I found a map in the archives showing a village that isn't there anymore.
I study everything. Plants, stars, people. Especially people.
My candle burns down every night. I go through a lot of candles.
I've been writing an encyclopedia of {village}. Volume one: the bell.
The past teaches us. If we listen.
I keep records of every wedding. The happiest pages in the archive.
Ink, quill and a good chair. All a scholar needs.
I've got questions no book can answer. That's what keeps me going.
The library's for books. The archives are for us. Our own story.
I record the weather every day. Patterns emerge. Slowly.
Every resident in the village has a page in my ledger.
I've been reading about the old kingdoms. They had bells too.
Scholars and librarians are cousins. We argue about filing systems.
I wrote down the bard's songs so they'll never be forgotten.
Curiosity is the scholar's only qualification.
I've been translating an old stone tablet. It's either a poem or a shopping list.
History is just yesterday's gossip with better handwriting.
The archives are open to everyone. Knowledge shouldn't be locked away.
I'd like to know what the first villagers dreamed about.
Every day is a page. I'm writing as fast as I can.
station.farmer: My composter turns scraps into bone meal. Feed it anything that rots.
Put a composter near any unemployed neighbor and you might make a farmer.
Fill the composter to the top and it'll give you bone meal. Spread that on your crops.
Bring me your rotten apples and old seeds. The composter's hungry.
A farmer's workstation is a barrel of muck. A very useful barrel of muck.
Composting is just patience in a bucket.
station.librarian: The lectern holds a book open so anyone can read it. Put a book and quill on it to share your writing.
A lectern near a free resident makes a librarian. Then bring them books.
The lectern gives off a little redstone signal when you turn the page. Clever, isn't it?
I keep my favorite book on the lectern. You may read it, but don't fold the corners.
Lecterns and bookshelves go together like bread and butter.
If you want enchanted books, a librarian with a lectern is your friend.
station.fisherman: The barrel by my door holds my catch. Sixty-four of anything per slot. Very roomy.
Give a free resident a barrel and they'll take up fishing.
My barrel keeps the fish fresh. Well, fresh enough.
A barrel's a good chest for small spaces. It opens even with something on top.
Barrels smell of fish after a while. All of them. Forever.
I trade fish for emeralds. My barrel's always stocked.
station.fletcher: The fletching table's for arrows and bows. Mostly arrows.
Put a fletching table near an unemployed resident and they'll learn to make arrows.
My fletching table's covered in feathers and flint. Organized chaos.
A fletching table is a sort of promise. Arrows when you need them.
The table's where I sort my feathers. White on the left, grey on the right.
Every good archer needs a fletcher, and every fletcher needs a table.
station.cleric: The brewing stand bubbles all day. Blaze powder fuels it; nether wart starts every potion.
A brewing stand near a free resident makes a cleric.
Put water bottles in the stand, add nether wart, then your ingredient. Magic.
My brewing stand's been in the church for generations.
The stand's three arms hold three bottles. Efficient.
Blaze powder burns slow in the stand. One rod lasts a long time.
station.cartographer: The cartography table copies and zooms maps. Paper makes them bigger.
A cartography table near a free resident makes a mapmaker.
Lock a map with glass at the table and it'll never change.
My cartography table's got compass marks scratched all over it.
Two maps in, one copy out. Perfect for travelers.
The table's the most useful thing in my house. And the most cluttered.
station.armorer: The blast furnace smelts ore and armor twice as fast. Only metal, mind.
A blast furnace near a free resident makes an armorer.
Melt old iron armor in the blast furnace and you'll get nuggets back.
My blast furnace roars all day. You get used to it.
Fuel it well and it'll smelt a stack before lunch.
The blast furnace is faster than a regular furnace, but it won't cook your supper.
station.toolsmith: The smithing table upgrades diamond gear to netherite and puts trims on armor.
A smithing table near a free resident makes a toolsmith.
The smithing table's for the clever work. Upgrades and decorations.
I use the smithing table for finishing touches.
Templates go in the smithing table. Rare things, templates.
A smithing table never wears out. Unlike my patience.
station.weaponsmith: The grindstone repairs and removes enchantments. Good for a fresh start.
A grindstone near a free resident makes a weaponsmith.
Put two worn swords in the grindstone and you'll get one better one.
The grindstone strips curses off. Most curses.
I spin the grindstone all day. My arms are like iron.
The grindstone gives you a bit of experience back when you strip enchantments.
station.leatherworker: The cauldron holds water, lava or powder snow. I use it for dyeing and washing leather.
A cauldron near a free resident makes a leatherworker.
Wash the dye off leather armor in a cauldron of water.
My cauldron's always full. Rain fills it up for free.
Cauldrons catch drips from pointed dripstone. Clever trick, that.
The cauldron's the oldest tool in my trade.
station.mason: The stonecutter makes stairs, slabs and walls from a single block. No waste.
A stonecutter near a free resident makes a mason.
One stone block in, one stone stair out. The stonecutter's a marvel.
My stonecutter's blade spins so fast you can't see it.
Mind your fingers near the stonecutter.
The stonecutter saves me so much stone.
station.shepherd: The loom turns banners into art. Dye plus a pattern, and you've got a crest.
A loom near a free resident makes a shepherd.
Put a banner and a dye in the loom and pick a pattern. Endless designs.
My loom clacks all day. It's like a heartbeat.
Banner patterns go in the loom too. Creeper faces, flowers, globes.
station.butcher: The smoker cooks food twice as fast as a furnace. Food only.
A smoker near a free resident makes a butcher.
Smoked meat keeps longer and tastes better. Everyone knows that.
Put raw meat and fuel in the smoker and you'll have supper in no time.
The smoker's smoke tells the whole village when dinner's coming.
station.knight: Strike my training dummy to see how hard you hit. It shows your combo too.
The dummy won't break if you hit it. Sneak and swing if you want to move it.
I train on the dummy every working day. A little more skill each time.
Put a training dummy near a free resident and you might make a knight.
The dummy's got a pot for a helmet. Aim for the bullseye on its chest.
A full swing does more damage than a quick tap. The dummy will show you.
station.archer: Shoot the archery target and it'll tell you your score. Ten for the bullseye.
Put an archery target near a free resident and you might make an archer.
I loose practice arrows at the target every working day. Blunt ones; they hurt nobody.
The target's rings go gold, red, blue, black, white. Gold is ten points.
Arrows that clip the edge still earn a point. Everyone deserves a point.
Practice makes the archer. The target never complains.
station.cook: My kitchen stove cooks raw food twice as fast as a campfire. Four pieces at a time.
Put raw meat, fish or potatoes on the stove and they'll pop out cooked.
When I've worked at my stove, there's a dish of the day for every visitor. Just ask.
A kitchen stove near a free resident might make a cook.
The stove's fire glows while something's cooking. Smell that?
One helping of the dish of the day per visitor. I'm generous, but not that generous.
station.tavern_keeper: The drinks barrel takes apples and berries and pours cider into an empty mug.
The tap stand brews cocoa beans into coffee. Bring a mug.
I restock the barrel and the tap every working day.
A drinks barrel or a tap stand near a free resident might make a tavern keeper.
Right-click the barrel with an empty hand to see how many mugs are left.
Cider warms you up and helps you heal a little. Coffee gives you a spring in your step.
station.apothecary: Press three herbs, flowers, berries, ferns or kelp, then bring a glass bottle for an Herbal Tonic.
The alchemical press holds up to twelve herbs at once.
When I work at my press, anyone hurt nearby gets patched up.
An alchemical press near a free resident might make an apothecary.
An Herbal Tonic gives you a few seconds of regeneration. Gentle stuff.
Every flower in the meadow has a little medicine in it.
station.painter: Paint my easel's canvas with a dye to sketch, and a second dye to finish the painting.
The color of the second dye decides the picture: blue for the sea, red for flowers, yellow for a sunset.
Take a finished painting off the easel with an empty hand. It's yours to hang.
A paintbrush on a finished canvas paints it over into a different picture.
I paint a new picture on my easel every working day.
An easel near a free resident might make a painter.
station.bard: Play my music stand and everyone nearby gets Haste for a minute. Music makes the work go faster.
Hold a lute when you play the stand for a guitar sound. A bell rings like chimes.
The stand knows ten songs. Some old, some mine.
I perform at my stand every working day. The neighbors gather round.
A music stand near a free resident might make a bard.
Let a song finish before you start another. Even bards need to breathe.
station.tailor: Mend leather, bows, fishing rods and elytra at my sewing table with string.
Unravel wool into string at the sewing table. Three lengths per block.
Each length of string mends a quarter of the damage. Bring enough.
When I'm sewing, I mend the guards' armor too.
A sewing table near a free resident might make a tailor.
Good thread, good needle, good table. That's all tailoring needs.
station.carpenter: My sawmill turns a log into six planks instead of four. And planks into three sticks.
The sawmill cuts up to sixteen at a time. Saves your arm.
I leave offcuts at the sawmill when I work. Take the sticks if you need them.
A sawmill near a free resident might make a carpenter.
Bamboo blocks saw into planks too.
Sawmills are louder than they look. Mind your ears.
station.scholar: Open the archives with an empty hand to read the village news.
Hold a book to the archives and I'll copy you the whole village chronicle.
Study near me while I'm at the archives and you'll pick up a little experience.
Archives near a free resident might make a scholar.
The chronicle has everything: births, weddings, quarrels, the lot.
Everything that happens in {village} ends up in the archives eventually.

ask: Be honest with me. Are you a sunrise person or a sunset person?
Settle an argument for me. Sunrises or sunsets?

answers.label: Sunrise, always
answers.reply: Me too! The whole village goes pink for a minute and nobody else is awake to see it.

answers.label: Sunset, easily
answers.reply: A sunset person. Then you'd love the view from the bell around six. It's like the sky's on fire.

answers.label: Whichever has breakfast
answers.reply: Ha! A practical answer. I respect that.

ask: Cats or dogs? I need to know who I'm dealing with.
Important question: are you a cat person or a dog person?

answers.label: Cats, obviously
answers.reply: A cat person! Creepers are scared of them, you know. Very sensible choice.

answers.label: Dogs, every time
answers.reply: A dog person! Loyal, brave, a bit muddy. Suits you.

answers.label: Parrots
answers.reply: Parrots! Bold. Noisy. I like it. Teach yours to say my name.

answers.label: Llamas
answers.reply: Llamas? They spit! ...I suppose you'd forgive them anything.

ask: If you could only eat one forever: something sweet or something savory?

answers.label: Sweet. Cake forever.
answers.reply: A cake person. I'll remember that next time there's a party.

answers.label: Savory. Give me stew.
answers.reply: A stew person! You'd get on well with our cook.

answers.label: Bread. Just bread.
answers.reply: Just bread. Simple, honest, perfect. I couldn't agree more.

ask: Do you like the rain, or are you a sunshine sort?

answers.label: I love the rain
answers.reply: You love the rain? Most people run from it! You're a kindred spirit, then.

answers.label: Sunshine, please
answers.reply: Sunshine it is. The village is prettiest in the sun anyway.

answers.label: Snow beats both
answers.reply: Snow! Quiet and white and sparkly. I like how you think.

ask: Where are you from, really? You don't talk like anyone from around here.
Do you have a home somewhere, out there past the hills?

answers.label: A house I built myself
answers.reply: You built it yourself? Then you know what it means to make a place your own.

answers.label: Wherever I sleep tonight
answers.reply: A wanderer at heart. I hope you'll count {village} as one of your homes.

answers.label: Somewhere far away
answers.reply: Far away. You must miss it sometimes. You can always tell me about it.

answers.label: Here, I hope
answers.reply: Here? Oh, that's the nicest thing anyone's said all week.

ask: What's the scariest thing you've ever faced out there?

answers.label: Creepers. Every time.
answers.reply: Creepers! Silent, green and explosive. I'd scream too.

answers.label: The warden
answers.reply: The warden? The one in the deep dark that hears your heartbeat? You're braver than anyone I know.

answers.label: Endermen
answers.reply: Endermen give me the shivers. Don't look them in the eye, they say.

answers.label: Nothing scares me
answers.reply: Nothing at all? Hmm. Even heroes are allowed to be scared, you know.

ask: Out of everywhere you've been, where's the most beautiful place?

answers.label: Cherry groves
answers.reply: Cherry groves! Pink petals everywhere. I'd love to see one someday.

answers.label: The ocean
answers.reply: The ocean. All that blue going on forever. I've only dreamed about it.

answers.label: Snowy mountains
answers.reply: Snowy peaks! Cold and quiet and enormous. You've got good taste.

answers.label: Right here
answers.reply: Right here? In {village}? Oh, you're just saying that. ...Are you? Thank you.

ask: Are you a day person or a night owl, {player}?

answers.label: Up with the sun
answers.reply: Early riser! You'd get on with the farmers. They're up before the roosters.

answers.label: Night owl
answers.reply: A night owl. Be careful out there after dark. The phantoms like sleepy people.

answers.label: I nap whenever I can
answers.reply: Ha! You'd love our nitwit. Naps are his whole philosophy.

ask: What's your favorite thing to eat after a long day?

answers.label: Golden carrots
answers.reply: Golden carrots! Very fancy. Very nourishing. You must be rich.

answers.label: Pumpkin pie
answers.reply: Pumpkin pie! The baker would adore you.

answers.label: Steak, well cooked
answers.reply: A steak person. Hearty and simple. The butcher would approve.

answers.label: Whatever's in my pocket
answers.reply: Whatever's in your pocket? Oh, you poor thing. Come back at supper and I'll feed you properly.

ask: Why do you do it? All the traveling, the danger. What keeps you going?

answers.label: To see everything
answers.reply: To see everything. I understand that. The world's too big to leave unseen.

answers.label: To build something great
answers.reply: To build something great. I'd like to see it when it's done.

answers.label: For the people I meet
answers.reply: For the people. That's the best answer anyone's ever given me.

answers.label: Honestly, I'm not sure
answers.reply: Not sure? That's honest. Maybe you'll find out on the way.

ask: If you could only keep one tool forever, which would it be?

answers.label: My pickaxe
answers.reply: The pickaxe. Of course. Can't get anywhere without digging.

answers.label: My sword
answers.reply: Your sword. Practical, but I hope you need it less and less.

answers.label: My fishing rod
answers.reply: A fishing rod! Peace, patience and supper all in one.

answers.label: A bed
answers.reply: A bed? Ha! Is that a tool? I suppose it is. The best one.

ask: Do you have a lucky number? I'm collecting them.

answers.label: Seven
answers.reply: Seven! Like the days of our week. Lucky indeed.

answers.label: Sixty-four
answers.reply: Sixty-four! A full stack. Very satisfying number.

answers.label: Thirteen
answers.reply: Thirteen? Bold. Most people think that's unlucky. You like to be different.

ask: What's your favorite color? I'm painting something and I need inspiration.

answers.label: Blue, like the sky
answers.reply: Blue! Calm and clear. I'll use a lot of it.

answers.label: Green, like the grass
answers.reply: Green! Like the hills around {village}. Lovely.

answers.label: Red, like redstone
answers.reply: Red! Bold. Like a poppy, or a warning sign.

answers.label: Purple, like amethyst
answers.reply: Purple! Royal and mysterious. I knew you had good taste.

ask: Is {village} the first village you've ever visited?

answers.label: The very first
answers.reply: The first? Then we'd better make a good impression! Welcome, properly.

answers.label: One of many
answers.reply: One of many. I hope we're one of your favorites.

answers.label: My favorite one
answers.reply: Your favorite? Oh, I'm going to tell everyone you said that.

ask: If you tamed a wolf tomorrow, what would you call it?

answers.label: Biscuit
answers.reply: Biscuit! Adorable. Every wolf deserves a snack name.

answers.label: Shadow
answers.reply: Shadow. Very mysterious. Very cool.

answers.label: Sir Barks-a-Lot
answers.reply: Sir Barks-a-Lot! That's the best name I've ever heard. I'm laughing.

answers.label: Wolf
answers.reply: Just "Wolf"? Practical. Very practical. A little sad.

ask: If you could build anything at all, what would it be?

answers.label: A castle in the clouds
answers.reply: A castle in the clouds! You'd need a lot of scaffolding. And courage.

answers.label: A cozy cottage
answers.reply: A cozy cottage. Simple, warm and yours. That's the best dream there is.

answers.label: A giant farm
answers.reply: A giant farm! You'd feed the whole world.

answers.label: A redstone machine
answers.reply: A redstone machine! What would it do? Never mind, I wouldn't understand it.

ask: Do you like music? The bard's always looking for requests.

answers.label: I love a good jig
answers.reply: A jig! Tell the bard. The tavern floor could use the exercise.

answers.label: Something slow and sad
answers.reply: Slow and sad. Sometimes those are the songs that help most.

answers.label: I only like note blocks
answers.reply: Note blocks! You and the redstone folk. Beep boop.

ask: How do you start your mornings? Coffee? Cider? Water from the well?

answers.label: Coffee, strong
answers.reply: Strong coffee! The tavern's tap pours a good mug. Bring your own.

answers.label: Cider, warm
answers.reply: Warm cider in the morning? You're a bit wild, aren't you? I like it.

answers.label: Milk, cold
answers.reply: Cold milk! Good for the bones, they say. And for curing bad potions.

answers.label: Whatever's nearest
answers.reply: Whatever's nearest. A true adventurer.

ask: Would you say you're brave or careful?

answers.label: Brave
answers.reply: Brave. I could tell. Just don't be brave and foolish at the same time.

answers.label: Careful
answers.reply: Careful. Good. The careful ones come home.

answers.label: Both, depending
answers.reply: Both! Brave when it counts, careful when it doesn't. That's wisdom.

ask: Do you collect anything? I have a box of interesting buttons.

answers.label: Music discs
answers.reply: Music discs! Creepers drop them, I hear. Only when skeletons shoot them. Strange world.

answers.label: Flowers
answers.reply: Flowers! Press them in a book and they'll last forever.

answers.label: Ores and gems
answers.reply: Ores and gems. A treasure hunter. I'd love to see your collection.

answers.label: Friends
answers.reply: Friends! Well, you've got one more now. Me.

ask: What's the best day you've ever had? I like to collect those too.

answers.label: The day I found diamonds
answers.reply: Diamonds! I'd have screamed. Did you scream? You screamed.

answers.label: The first night I survived
answers.reply: Your first night! I remember mine. Hiding in a hole in a hill, waiting for dawn.

answers.label: A quiet day here
answers.reply: A quiet day here? In {village}? That makes me so happy.

ask: Where do you sleep when you're on the road?

answers.label: In a bed I carry
answers.reply: A bed in your pack? Very sensible. Phantoms hate people who sleep.

answers.label: Under the stars
answers.reply: Under the stars! Romantic. Also full of spiders.

answers.label: I don't sleep much
answers.reply: You don't sleep much? Please do. The phantoms will come for you.

ask: Are you more of a miner or a builder?

answers.label: Miner, deep down
answers.reply: A miner! You'd love the old mineshafts. Rails and cobwebs everywhere.

answers.label: Builder, up high
answers.reply: A builder! The carpenter would love to talk shop with you.

answers.label: Explorer, far away
answers.reply: An explorer! Never staying put long enough to dig or build. I understand.

answers.label: Farmer, honestly
answers.reply: A farmer at heart! The best kind of person. Don't tell the miners I said so.

ask: What's the hardest lesson the world's taught you?

answers.label: Never dig straight down
answers.reply: Never dig straight down. My grandfather said the same thing, and he learned it the hard way.

answers.label: Always carry a bed
answers.reply: Always carry a bed. Wise. The night comes for everyone.

answers.label: Don't trust gravel
answers.reply: Gravel! Falling on your head when you least expect it. Treacherous stuff.

answers.label: Kindness is worth it
answers.reply: Kindness is worth it. That's a lesson I hope everyone learns.

ask: When you travel, do you like company, or do you go alone?

answers.label: Alone, mostly
answers.reply: Alone. Peaceful, but lonely. You can always take a friend from {village}, you know.

answers.label: With a wolf
answers.reply: With a wolf! A loyal friend who never complains. Lovely.

answers.label: With friends
answers.reply: With friends. Adventures are better shared.

ask: If you could put any enchantment on yourself, which would it be?

answers.label: Mending
answers.reply: Mending! Heal as you learn. That's beautiful, actually.

answers.label: Feather Falling
answers.reply: Feather Falling. Very sensible for someone who climbs things.

answers.label: Fortune
answers.reply: Fortune! Double everything. Greedy, but honest.

answers.label: Unbreaking
answers.reply: Unbreaking. I like that. Being hard to break is a good thing to want.

ask: Can I ask something silly? Are you ever afraid of the dark?

answers.label: Sometimes, yes
answers.reply: Me too. Thank you for saying so. It makes me feel less silly.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never? I envy you. I keep a candle lit all night.

answers.label: Only without a torch
answers.reply: Only without a torch. Fair. Torches make everything braver.

ask: Do you keep a journal of your adventures?

answers.label: Every single day
answers.reply: Every day! I'd love to read it someday. Only the parts you'd let me.

answers.label: I keep it in my head
answers.reply: In your head. Then I hope your head has a very good memory.

answers.label: I draw maps instead
answers.reply: Maps instead of words. A cartographer's soul.

ask: When's your birthday? I keep a list so nobody's ever forgotten.

answers.label: I don't know
answers.reply: You don't know? Then let's say it's Market Day. Every Market Day. More cake that way.

answers.label: Today, actually
answers.reply: Today?! Happy birthday! Why didn't you say? I'll tell everyone.

answers.label: I don't celebrate it
answers.reply: You don't celebrate? Everyone deserves one day that's just theirs. Think about it.

ask: If you could change one thing about {village}, what would it be?

answers.label: More lanterns at night
answers.reply: More lanterns. You're right, the paths get very dark. I'll mention it at the next meeting.

answers.label: A bigger tavern
answers.reply: A bigger tavern! Everyone would agree with that. Especially the bard.

answers.label: Nothing. It's perfect.
answers.reply: Nothing? Oh, that's lovely to hear. It's not perfect, but it's ours.

answers.label: A wall, for safety
answers.reply: A wall. Sensible. The guards have been saying the same thing.

ask: Do you have a secret talent? Everyone has one.

answers.label: I can tame anything
answers.reply: Anything? Even a llama? Even a grumpy one? I'm impressed.

answers.label: I can cook
answers.reply: You can cook! Why didn't you say? You must come to supper and show me.

answers.label: I can't think of one
answers.reply: Nonsense. Your talent is turning up when people need you. I've seen it.

ask: Which time of year do you love most?

answers.label: Spring blossoms
answers.reply: Spring! Everything new and green and full of bees.

answers.label: Summer days
answers.reply: Summer! Long days and warm nights and swimming in the river.

answers.label: Autumn harvest
answers.reply: Autumn! Pumpkins and full barns. My favorite too.

answers.label: Winter snow
answers.reply: Winter! Cozy fires and snow on everything. You're a romantic.

ask: Have you ever left somewhere you wish you'd stayed?

answers.label: Once or twice
answers.reply: Once or twice. Me too, in my own small way. Places stay with you.

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never. You always know when it's time to go. That's a gift.

answers.label: I'll stay here a while
answers.reply: Stay a while? Here? Then let me be the first to say I'm glad.

ask: How are you, really? Not the polite answer. The real one.
I've been meaning to ask: how are you doing, truly?

answers.label: Honestly, tired
answers.reply: Tired. Then rest here a while. Nobody's going to rush you in {village}.

answers.label: Really happy today
answers.reply: Really happy? Good. I'm going to borrow some of that.

answers.label: A bit lonely
answers.reply: A bit lonely. I'm glad you told me. You've always got a friend here. Always.

answers.label: Better now
answers.reply: Better now? Then my day's done its job.

ask: If I ever left {village} for a day, where should I go first?

answers.label: The river, to fish
answers.reply: The river! Close, quiet, full of fish. Perfect first adventure.

answers.label: The next village over
answers.reply: The next village? To spy on their bell? Ha! I'd like that.

answers.label: The tallest hill
answers.reply: The tallest hill. You'll see {village} from above. It looks tiny and precious.

answers.label: Nowhere. Stay here.
answers.reply: Nowhere? You think I should stay? ...You might be right.

ask: You're hurt! Sit down, let me see to that. I've got salve and clean bandages right here.
Look at you, all scraped up. Hold still and I'll patch you.

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Hold still... there. Clean, wrapped and on the mend. Try not to do that again.

answers.label: I'm fine, really
answers.reply: Fine? You're bleeding on my floor. All right, but come back if it gets worse.

ask: Oh, you're hurt! Come here, let me look after you. I always keep bandages handy.
You're limping, {player}. Let me wrap that for you. It won't take a moment.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: There we are. Gently, gently. You'll be right as rain soon.

answers.label: It's just a scratch
answers.reply: Just a scratch, they all say. Promise me you'll rest.

ask: You look rough. Let me patch you up before you go anywhere. That's what friends are for.

answers.label: Please
answers.reply: Ow, I know, I know. Done. Now eat something and stay out of trouble for an hour.

answers.label: I'll manage
answers.reply: You'll manage. You always do. But I worry, you know.

ask: I can hear your stomach from here. Let me give you something to eat. No charge.
You look hungry, {player}. I've got food to spare. Want some?

answers.label: Yes, thank you
answers.reply: Here. Eat it all, and properly, not on the run.

answers.label: I've got food
answers.reply: You've got food? Then eat it! Right now! I'm watching you.

ask: When did you last eat? Never mind, don't tell me. Take some bread.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: There. Now I'll sleep tonight knowing you've eaten.

answers.label: I'm not hungry
answers.reply: Not hungry? Your stomach says otherwise. Suit yourself.

ask: I baked cookies this morning. Far too many. Would you like a couple?

answers.label: I'd love some
answers.reply: Here you go. Still a little warm. Don't share them with the cat.

answers.label: Maybe next time
answers.reply: Next time, then. I'll save you the biggest ones.

ask: I picked a few flowers this morning. Would you like one? It might brighten your journey.

answers.label: I'd love one
answers.reply: Here. Keep it somewhere safe, or plant it somewhere new.

answers.label: Keep it for yourself
answers.reply: Keep it? You're sweet. Then I'll put it in my window for you.

ask: The orchard's been generous. Take an apple for the road?

answers.label: Gladly
answers.reply: Here's a good red one. Crunchy. Don't eat the core, there's seeds in there.

answers.label: No, thanks
answers.reply: No? More for the pigs. They won't complain.

ask: You're carrying farming things. Want some seeds to get you started?

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Here's a handful of wheat seeds. Plant them near water and you'll have bread in no time.

answers.label: I've got plenty
answers.reply: Plenty? A farmer after my own heart.

ask: You're soaked! Come stand under here with me until the worst of it passes.
Want to wait out the rain together? I'll tell you a story while we wait.

answers.label: I'd like that
answers.reply: We watched the rain come down in silver sheets and talked about nothing in particular. It was lovely.

answers.label: I like the rain
answers.reply: You like the rain? Off you go, then, you strange duck. Don't catch a cold.

ask: That storm's right overhead! Stay here with me until it calms down, please.

answers.label: I'll stay
answers.reply: Thank you. Every flash is less scary with someone here.

answers.label: I'll be careful
answers.reply: Careful isn't enough in a storm like this! ...Fine. Stay low. Move fast.

ask: It's dark out and you've no torch in hand. Take a few of mine, please.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: Three torches. Light your way home. Or wherever you're going.

answers.label: I can see fine
answers.reply: You can see fine until a creeper's on your shoulder. Suit yourself.

ask: Is that raw? Give it here, I'll cook it for you on my fire. Won't take a moment.

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Sizzle, sizzle... and done. Cooked properly. Eat it while it's hot.

answers.label: I'll cook it myself
answers.reply: Do it properly, then. Not on a campfire in the rain.

ask: That's seen some hard use. Let me put it right for you on my anvil.
You're carrying a battered thing there. Want me to knock the dents out?

answers.label: Please do
answers.reply: A few good strikes and... there. Not new, but much better.

answers.label: It's fine as it is
answers.reply: Fine? It'll break at the worst moment. They always do.

ask: That's fraying. Hand it over a moment. A few stitches and it'll hold for ages.

answers.label: Thank you
answers.reply: In, out, pull... there. Neat as anything.

answers.label: No need
answers.reply: No need? You'll be back when it falls apart. I'll be here.

ask: You're carrying a map. Want me to mark where {village} sits, so you can always find your way back?

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: There. The heart of {village}, right where the bell hangs. Never be lost.

answers.label: I know the way
answers.reply: You know the way? Good. Some people never do.

ask: Need directions home to {village}? I can tell you exactly where the bell is.

answers.label: Please
answers.reply: Here's where we are. Write it down somewhere safe.

answers.label: No, thanks
answers.reply: All right. The bell's loud enough to follow anyway.

ask: ...You've got a rod. Want a tip? And a fish, while I'm at it?

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: ...Cast where the water's dark and still. Wait longer than you think. And here, have this one.

answers.label: I'm good, thanks
answers.reply: ...All right. The fish are biting at dusk. Just so you know.

ask: You've brought a book! Would you like me to read you a passage? It's very educational.

answers.label: I'd love that
answers.reply: "The patient miner finds the deepest veins." There. You're wiser already.

answers.label: Another time
answers.reply: Another time. The words will wait for you. They're good at that.

ask: I'm reading about the old builders. Want to learn something with me?

answers.label: Teach me
answers.reply: Did you know the first villages were built around wells, not bells? The bell came later.

answers.label: Not today
answers.reply: Not today? Then I'll save it for you. It's a good story.

ask: I've just finished a little tune. Would you like to hear it? It's short. Mostly.

answers.label: Play it
answers.reply: The notes fill the air, bright and bouncing, and for a minute everything feels lighter.

answers.label: Maybe later
answers.reply: Later, then. It'll still be here. I'll hum it to myself until then.

ask: I've been keeping something for you. Just a little thing. For luck. Will you take it?

answers.label: You're too kind
answers.reply: An emerald. Buy yourself something nice. Or don't, and keep it for luck.

answers.label: Keep it, please
answers.reply: Keep it? You're impossible. Then it stays here, waiting for you.

ask: It's dark, {player}. I can walk you to the edge of the village if you like.

answers.label: That would be kind
answers.reply: Stay close. Eyes open. ...There. You're past the worst of the dark now. Go safely.

answers.label: I'll be fine
answers.reply: You'll be fine. You always say that. Just stay near the torches.

ask: You look like you could use a warm mug of something. On the house today?

answers.label: Please
answers.reply: Here. Warm cider with a pinch of spice. Don't tell the others it was free.

answers.label: I'm all right
answers.reply: All right. Bring a mug next time and I'll fill it.

ask: Can I give you a hug? You look like you need one. Or I do. One of us does.

answers.label: Yes
answers.reply: There. That's better. For both of us, I think.

answers.label: Maybe a handshake
answers.reply: A handshake! Very formal. Very you. Here.

ask: Riddle time! I have a tongue but cannot taste, I call everyone but cannot speak. What am I?

answers.label: A bell
answers.reply: The bell! Of course. Clever you.

answers.label: A creeper
answers.reply: A creeper? No! Creepers don't call anyone. They just... hiss. It's the bell!

answers.label: A parrot
answers.reply: A parrot can speak! It's the bell. Good guess, though.

ask: Here's a riddle: the more I burn, the more I keep the monsters away. What am I?

answers.label: A torch
answers.reply: A torch! Right! Never leave home without one.

answers.label: A furnace
answers.reply: A furnace keeps you warm, not safe. It's a torch!

answers.label: Lava
answers.reply: Lava? That burns, but it brings more trouble than it stops. It's a torch.

ask: Riddle! I have mountains but no stone, rivers but no water, villages but no people. What am I?

answers.label: A map
answers.reply: A map! Brilliant. The cartographer would hire you.

answers.label: A painting
answers.reply: Close! But it's a map. Paintings have everything, at least in color.

answers.label: A dream
answers.reply: A dream? That's lovely. The answer's a map, but I like yours better.

ask: Riddle: what has to be broken before you can use it?

answers.label: An egg
answers.reply: An egg! Correct. Breakfast was the real winner.

answers.label: A promise
answers.reply: A promise? That's sad and clever. It's an egg, though.

answers.label: A pickaxe
answers.reply: A pickaxe breaks other things. The answer's an egg!

ask: A riddle for you: I follow you all day, but disappear at night. What am I?

answers.label: My shadow
answers.reply: Your shadow! Right. Unless you're near a torch, then it sneaks back.

answers.label: A wolf
answers.reply: A wolf would follow you at night too! It's your shadow.

answers.label: A zombie
answers.reply: A zombie follows you at night, not the day! It's your shadow.

ask: Try this one: I run but never walk, have a mouth but never talk. What am I?

answers.label: A river
answers.reply: A river! Yes! Running all day and never tired.

answers.label: A horse
answers.reply: A horse walks too! It's a river.

answers.label: The bard
answers.reply: Ha! The bard never stops talking. It's a river.

ask: Riddle: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. Shout into the well and you'll meet me.

answers.label: An echo
answers.reply: An echo! You got it. Hello, hello, hello.

answers.label: A ghost
answers.reply: A ghost? Spooky! No, it's an echo.

answers.label: The well itself
answers.reply: Close! It's the echo inside the well.

ask: Riddle! I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old. What am I?

answers.label: A candle
answers.reply: A candle! Right! Sounds a bit like my grandfather, too.

answers.label: A tree
answers.reply: A tree grows taller when it's old! It's a candle.

answers.label: A villager
answers.reply: Ha! Some of us shrink, but it's a candle.

ask: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?

answers.label: Footsteps
answers.reply: Footsteps! Correct. You've left a lot of them in {village}.

answers.label: Emeralds
answers.reply: Emeralds? The more you take, the fewer you leave! It's footsteps.

answers.label: Memories
answers.reply: Memories... that's beautiful. The answer's footsteps, but I like yours.

ask: Riddle: if you have me, you want to share me. If you share me, you don't have me. What am I?

answers.label: A secret
answers.reply: A secret! Clever! Don't share the answer.

answers.label: A cookie
answers.reply: A cookie? You still have half if you share. It's a secret!

answers.label: A cold
answers.reply: Ha! A cold you'd rather not share. It's a secret, though.

ask: What gets wetter the more it dries?

answers.label: A towel
answers.reply: A towel! Right. Very sensible riddle, that one.

answers.label: The rain
answers.reply: The rain? No, the rain's already wet. It's a towel!

answers.label: A fish
answers.reply: A fish? It never dries! It's a towel.

ask: Riddle: what has keys but opens no doors, and makes music when you press it?

answers.label: A note block
answers.reply: A note block! Close enough. Clever.

answers.label: A chest
answers.reply: A chest opens! It's a note block.

answers.label: A lute
answers.reply: A lute has strings, not keys. It's a note block!

ask: Riddle: what goes up and never comes down?

answers.label: Your age
answers.reply: Your age! Right. Don't remind me.

answers.label: A firework
answers.reply: A firework comes back down in pieces! It's your age.

answers.label: A balloon
answers.reply: Balloons come down eventually. It's your age!

ask: What has an eye but cannot see? The tailor told me this one.

answers.label: A needle
answers.reply: A needle! Correct. The tailor will be proud.

answers.label: A potato
answers.reply: A potato! Ha! That's actually right too. Potatoes have eyes. I'll allow it.

answers.label: An enderman
answers.reply: Endermen can see! That's the whole problem with them. It's a needle.

ask: Riddle: you can see me every night, but you can never count me. What am I?

answers.label: The stars
answers.reply: The stars! Right. People have tried. People have failed.

answers.label: The sheep
answers.reply: You can count sheep! That's how you fall asleep. It's the stars.

answers.label: My worries
answers.reply: Your worries? Oh. Come talk to me about them sometime. It's the stars, though.

ask: The more of me you dig out, the bigger I get. What am I?

answers.label: A hole
answers.reply: A hole! Yes! Every miner knows that one.

answers.label: A mine
answers.reply: A mine is a hole, so I'll allow it. Clever.

answers.label: A garden
answers.reply: A garden grows when you plant, not dig. It's a hole!

ask: Last riddle, a tricky one: what breaks if you say its name?

answers.label: Silence
answers.reply: Silence! Clever, clever. Shh.

answers.label: A promise
answers.reply: A promise breaks, but not from saying it! It's silence.

answers.label: A golem
answers.reply: A golem? No, golems don't break that easily. It's silence.

ask: I'm black when you buy me, red when you use me, and grey when you throw me away. What am I?

answers.label: Coal
answers.reply: Coal! Right! Into the furnace with you.

answers.label: A creeper
answers.reply: A creeper's green! It's coal.

answers.label: Redstone
answers.reply: Redstone's red all the time. It's coal!

ask: Listen to that rain. Do you mind getting caught in it?

answers.label: I love it
answers.reply: You love it? Then you're one of us rain-walkers. Puddles are the best part.

answers.label: I hate being wet
answers.reply: Hate it? Then stay under the eaves with me a while. No rush.

answers.label: It helps the crops
answers.reply: It helps the crops. Spoken like a true farmer. The fields thank you.

ask: Are you scared of storms? Be honest. I am.

answers.label: A little, yes
answers.reply: A little? Me too. Sit with me until it passes.

answers.label: Not at all
answers.reply: Not at all? Then I'll hide behind you.

answers.label: I love storms
answers.reply: You love storms? The lightning, the noise? You're a strange and wonderful person.

ask: Snowball fight later, when the snow's deep enough? Yes or no?

answers.label: Absolutely yes
answers.reply: Yes! I've been practicing my aim on the barn. You've been warned.

answers.label: Too cold for me
answers.reply: Too cold! Then hot cider by the fire instead. Equally good.

answers.label: Only if I win
answers.reply: Only if you win? Ha! We'll see about that.

ask: What do you think about when you look at the stars?

answers.label: Home
answers.reply: Home. Even when you're right here? I hope {village} feels like a little bit of it.

answers.label: How small we are
answers.reply: How small we are. Small, but not unimportant. I think about that too.

answers.label: Where to go next
answers.reply: Where to go next. Always looking forward. Don't forget to come back.

ask: Did you have breakfast? Tell me you had breakfast.

answers.label: I did, a big one
answers.reply: Good! A big breakfast makes a brave adventurer.

answers.label: Just an apple
answers.reply: Just an apple? That's not breakfast, that's a snack. Eat more.

answers.label: I forgot
answers.reply: You forgot?! How can you forget breakfast? Go to the tavern this instant.

ask: It's Market Day! What are you hoping to find at the stalls?

answers.label: Something sweet
answers.reply: Something sweet! The honey cakes go fast. Hurry.

answers.label: A good trade
answers.reply: A good trade. The fletcher's been generous today, I hear.

answers.label: Just the company
answers.reply: Just the company. That's what Market Day's really for.

ask: The sun's going down. Do you have somewhere safe to sleep tonight?

answers.label: Yes, I'm fine
answers.reply: Good. I worry otherwise. Sleep well, wherever it is.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: Not really? Find a bed in {village} if you need one. Nobody will mind.

answers.label: I'll keep exploring
answers.reply: Explore at night? Be careful. Torches, armor, a lot of courage.

ask: Are you eating enough out there? Really? Tell me the truth.

answers.label: Yes, I promise
answers.reply: You promise? I'll take your word for it. This time.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: I knew it! Come by at supper. I'm feeding you. No arguments.

answers.label: Mostly mushroom stew
answers.reply: Mushroom stew every day? You poor thing. I'll make you something with bread.

ask: Do you think the world was made, or did it just happen?

answers.label: Someone made it
answers.reply: Someone made it. Then I'd love to know what they were thinking.

answers.label: It just happened
answers.reply: It just happened. Then everything's a happy accident. Even you. Especially you.

answers.label: Does it matter?
answers.reply: Does it matter? Perhaps not. We're here now. That's the interesting part.

ask: Quick! If you were a block, which block would you be?

answers.label: A bouncy slime block
answers.reply: A slime block! Bouncy and fun. I knew it.

answers.label: A cozy wool block
answers.reply: Wool! Soft and warm. Aw.

answers.label: TNT
answers.reply: TNT?! Explosive personality. I respect it. Stand back, everyone.

answers.label: A diamond block
answers.reply: A diamond block! Fancy! A bit full of yourself, maybe. Ha!

ask: Would you take me on an adventure someday? A small one. Maybe a big one.

answers.label: Of course I would
answers.reply: You would? I'm packing tonight! Well, I'm thinking about packing.

answers.label: When you're ready
answers.reply: When I'm ready. I'm ready now! Mostly. Nearly. Soon.

answers.label: It's too dangerous
answers.reply: Too dangerous? That's what makes it an adventure! ...I'll wait.

ask: How do you organize your chests? This matters to me more than it should.

answers.label: Sorted by type
answers.reply: Sorted by type. A person after my own heart.

answers.label: One big chaos chest
answers.reply: One chaos chest?! I need to sit down.

answers.label: By color
answers.reply: By color! Unusual, but beautiful. I approve.

ask: What do you do when things go wrong? Me, I go to the garden.

answers.label: Keep going
answers.reply: Keep going. Yes. One step, then another. That's how we get through.

answers.label: Rest first
answers.reply: Rest first. Sensible. You can't fix a fence with tired hands.

answers.label: Find a friend
answers.reply: Find a friend. Come find me, then. I'll be in the garden.

ask: ...Do you ever like being alone?

answers.label: Yes, sometimes
answers.reply: ...Me too. It's nice to hear someone say it.

answers.label: Not really
answers.reply: ...That's all right. Then I'm glad you come to talk.

answers.label: With you, I don't mind
answers.reply: ...With me? ...That's kind. Thank you.

ask: If the moon was something else, what would it be?

answers.label: A giant pearl
answers.reply: A pearl! That's what I think too! A giant forgot to pick it up.

answers.label: A lamp for the sky
answers.reply: A lamp for the sky. Lovely. Who turns it on, though?

answers.label: Cheese
answers.reply: Cheese! The classics never die.

ask: How many torches do you carry, on a normal trip?

answers.label: A full stack
answers.reply: A full stack. Good. Sixty-four's the right number.

answers.label: A handful
answers.reply: A handful? Not enough. Never enough. Take more.

answers.label: I make them as I go
answers.reply: Make them as you go. Efficient. Assuming you find coal.

ask: Have you ever seen something that couldn't be explained? Anything at all?

answers.label: A glowing cave
answers.reply: A glowing cave? Was it glow lichen? Glow berries? Something else? I need to know.

answers.label: A villager in a boat
answers.reply: A villager in a boat? How did they get there? Where were they going? Fascinating.

answers.label: A golem dancing
answers.reply: A golem dancing?! No! I'd give anything to see that.

ask: If trouble ever came to {village}, would you help us?

answers.label: Without a doubt
answers.reply: Without a doubt. I knew it. You're one of us.

answers.label: If I'm nearby
answers.reply: If you're nearby. Fair. We'll ring the bell loud.

answers.label: I'd bring friends
answers.reply: You'd bring friends! Even better. An army of friends.

ask: Would you like to plant something with me someday? A flower, maybe?

answers.label: I'd love that
answers.reply: You would? I'll save the best seeds for us.

answers.label: I'm bad with plants
answers.reply: Nobody's bad with plants. Plants just need patience. So do we.

answers.label: What's your favorite?
answers.reply: My favorite? Blue orchids. Or poppies. Or cornflowers. All of them.

ask: Which crop should I plant next season? I can't decide.

answers.label: More pumpkins
answers.reply: More pumpkins! For pies and lanterns. Good thinking.

answers.label: Melons for summer
answers.reply: Melons! The children will be thrilled.

answers.label: Sweet berries
answers.reply: Sweet berries! Prickly, but worth it. The foxes will be furious.

ask: If you could only read one book again and again, what would it be about?

answers.label: Faraway places
answers.reply: Faraway places. Of course. You'd never tire of it.

answers.label: A love story
answers.reply: A love story! Oh, I've got just the one. Sort of.

answers.label: How to build things
answers.reply: How to build things. A practical reader. My favorite kind.

ask: ...Do you fish? It's a good way to think.

answers.label: All the time
answers.reply: All the time? Then we'll fish together someday. The spot upstream is the best.

answers.label: I never catch anything
answers.reply: You never catch anything? Patience. And a lure. Mostly patience.

answers.label: I prefer swimming
answers.reply: Swimming scares the fish. ...But it's fine.

ask: Do you have someone you pray for, or think of, when you're far away?

answers.label: My family
answers.reply: Your family. I'll light a candle for them too.

answers.label: Everyone here
answers.reply: Everyone here? In {village}? That's... that's lovely.

answers.label: No one in particular
answers.reply: No one in particular. Then I'll think of you instead.

ask: What's the toughest thing you've ever broken a tool on?

answers.label: Obsidian
answers.reply: Obsidian! Only diamond touches it. I've seen grown smiths cry.

answers.label: A creeper's surprise
answers.reply: A creeper blew up your gear? That's not breaking, that's tragedy.

answers.label: I never break tools
answers.reply: Never? You must have Unbreaking. Or you never work. Ha!

ask: If I made you one dish, right now, what would it be?

answers.label: Hearty stew
answers.reply: Hearty stew. Good choice. It's on the stove already.

answers.label: Fresh bread
answers.reply: Fresh bread! Coming right up. Well, in an hour. Bread takes time.

answers.label: Surprise me
answers.reply: Surprise you? Oh, now you've done it. Pumpkin and mushroom pie. Brace yourself.

ask: What's your drink, traveler? Cider, coffee, or a mug of the well's finest?

answers.label: Cider
answers.reply: Cider! Pressed fresh. Bring a mug and I'll fill it.

answers.label: Coffee
answers.reply: Coffee! The tap's always ready.

answers.label: Just water
answers.reply: Water? Wise. Cheap, too. My worst customer. Ha!

ask: If I painted you, how would you like to be shown?

answers.label: As a hero
answers.reply: As a hero! Sword raised, cape blowing. I'll make you taller.

answers.label: Just as I am
answers.reply: Just as you are. That's the best portrait of all.

answers.label: Fishing by a lake
answers.reply: Fishing by a lake. Peaceful. I'll use a lot of blue.

ask: I'm writing a song about you. Should it be a ballad or a jig?

answers.label: A grand ballad
answers.reply: A grand ballad! Thirty verses at least. You'll be famous.

answers.label: A silly jig
answers.reply: A silly jig! Everyone will dance. Even the golem. Maybe.

answers.label: Please don't
answers.reply: Please don't? Too late. I've already rhymed your name with "pickaxe."

ask: If I made you something to wear, what would it be?

answers.label: A warm cloak
answers.reply: A warm cloak. For the cold nights out there. I'll make it blue.

answers.label: A fancy hat
answers.reply: A fancy hat! With a feather. You'll be the talk of the market.

answers.label: Sturdy boots
answers.reply: Sturdy boots. Practical. Your feet will thank me.

ask: What's the most important thing in a house, if you ask me? No, wait, I'm asking you.

answers.label: A good door
answers.reply: A good door! Keeps the zombies out and the warmth in. Correct.

answers.label: A big window
answers.reply: A big window. Light's everything. I'll allow it.

answers.label: The people inside
answers.reply: The people inside. Hm. You're right. That's the best answer.

ask: Should I write down your visits in the village chronicle?

answers.label: Yes, please
answers.reply: Yes? Then you're in the archives forever. I'll be kind.

answers.label: Only the brave bits
answers.reply: Only the brave bits. I'll leave out the time you fell in the river.

answers.label: Leave me out
answers.reply: Leave you out? A humble one. All right. A footnote, then.

ask: You've seen fighting out there. Any advice for a guard?

answers.label: Never fight alone
answers.reply: Never fight alone. The golem and I will remember that.

answers.label: Light everything
answers.reply: Light everything. Monsters hate torches. We'll put more up.

answers.label: Run when you should
answers.reply: Run when you should. That's the hardest advice to follow. And the wisest.

ask: Want to join me for a nap later? I've found the perfect haystack.

answers.label: Absolutely
answers.reply: Absolutely! A fellow napper. I'll save you the soft side.

answers.label: I'm too busy
answers.reply: Too busy? Busy's overrated. The haystack will wait for you.

answers.label: Only a short one
answers.reply: A short one! Twenty minutes. Or two hours. We'll see.

ask: Will you play with me? Please? Just one game?

answers.label: Of course!
answers.reply: Yay! You're it! Run!

answers.label: Maybe later
answers.reply: Later? Promise? You have to pinky promise.

answers.label: What game?
answers.reply: Hide and seek! I'll hide. Count to a hundred. No peeking!

ask: What did you want to be when you were little like me?

answers.label: An adventurer
answers.reply: An adventurer! And now you are one! That means I can be one too!

answers.label: A farmer
answers.reply: A farmer? But you're an adventurer now. Did you change your mind? Can I change mine?

answers.label: I still don't know
answers.reply: You still don't know? Grown-ups don't know either? That's a relief!

ask: Are there monsters under beds? My sister says there are. Tell me the truth!

answers.label: No, never
answers.reply: Never? Promise? Okay. I believe you. Mostly.

answers.label: Only dust bunnies
answers.reply: Dust bunnies! Are they cute? Can I keep one?

answers.label: The golem protects you
answers.reply: The golem protects me! Even under my bed? It's very big. It won't fit.

ask: Would you rather fly like a phantom or breathe underwater like a fish?

answers.label: Fly
answers.reply: Fly! You'd see {village} from the clouds. Wave to me.

answers.label: Breathe underwater
answers.reply: Underwater! All those ruins and coral and turtles. I'd choose that too.

answers.label: Neither, I like walking
answers.reply: Walking. Steady and sure. The ground's never let you down.

ask: Would you rather have an iron golem as a bodyguard, or a creeper who's sworn never to explode?

answers.label: The golem
answers.reply: The golem! Strong, silent and gives flowers to children. A perfect friend.

answers.label: The polite creeper
answers.reply: A polite creeper! Ha! You'd never relax, though. Every hiss would be terrifying.

answers.label: Both, for balance
answers.reply: Both! The golem would keep an eye on the creeper. Very sensible arrangement.

ask: Would you rather live in the Nether or the End? If you had to choose.

answers.label: The Nether
answers.reply: The Nether! Warm, at least. Bring a lot of fire resistance.

answers.label: The End
answers.reply: The End. Quiet and strange. You'd be the only one there besides the endermen.

answers.label: I'd stay right here
answers.reply: Right here. Good answer. Neither of those places has a bell.

ask: For the rest of your life: bread every day, or cake once a week?

answers.label: Bread every day
answers.reply: Bread every day! Steady and good. You think like a farmer.

answers.label: Cake once a week
answers.reply: Cake once a week! Something to look forward to. Market Day cake!

answers.label: Can I have both?
answers.reply: Both? Greedy! I'd say the same, honestly.

ask: Would you rather live in a huge castle or a tiny cottage by a stream?

answers.label: The castle
answers.reply: A castle! You'd need a lot of servants. And a lot of torches.

answers.label: The cottage
answers.reply: The cottage. Me too. Small enough to keep warm, big enough for friends.

answers.label: A boat
answers.reply: A boat! Always moving, always home. Very romantic.

ask: If you could know one thing about your future, would you want to?

answers.label: Yes, tell me everything
answers.reply: Everything? I'd be too scared. You're braver than me.

answers.label: No, I'll find out
answers.reply: You'd rather find out. Me too. That's half the fun of tomorrow.

answers.label: Only good news
answers.reply: Only good news! Clever. Leave the rest as a surprise.

ask: Would you rather talk to animals or understand every language in the world?

answers.label: Talk to animals
answers.reply: Talk to animals! Imagine what the cats would say. Mostly complaints, I think.

answers.label: Every language
answers.reply: Every language! You could talk to the wandering trader properly. Finally.

answers.label: Neither, I like quiet
answers.reply: Quiet. Sometimes the best conversations have no words at all.

ask: Would you rather have a chest full of diamonds, or never need to sleep?

answers.label: The diamonds
answers.reply: The diamonds! Practical. You could buy the whole market.

answers.label: Never sleep
answers.reply: Never sleep? You'd miss dreaming. And the phantoms would never leave you alone.

answers.label: I'll keep my naps
answers.reply: Keep your naps! A wise person. The nitwit would be so proud.

ask: Endless summer or endless winter? You have to pick one.

answers.label: Endless summer
answers.reply: Summer forever! Swimming, sunshine, picnics. Sounds lovely. And hot.

answers.label: Endless winter
answers.reply: Winter forever! Snow and fires and soup. I'd need more scarves.

answers.label: I couldn't choose
answers.reply: Couldn't choose? Then you'd better not be in charge of the weather.

ask: If you found a dragon egg, would you hatch it or leave it be?

answers.label: Hatch it!
answers.reply: Hatch it! You'd have a dragon! The whole village would come to see it. Or run away.

answers.label: Leave it be
answers.reply: Leave it be. Some things aren't ours to wake. Wise.

answers.label: Bring it here
answers.reply: Bring it here? To {village}? The golem would have a fit.

ask: Would you rather explore a woodland mansion or a jungle temple?

answers.label: The mansion
answers.reply: The mansion! Full of illagers and secret rooms. Bring friends. And a totem.

answers.label: The temple
answers.reply: The temple! Vines, traps and puzzles. Very adventurous.

answers.label: A library
answers.reply: A library! The safest adventure of all. And the quietest.

ask: Would you rather be invisible or be able to see in the dark?

answers.label: Invisible
answers.reply: Invisible! Would you use it to sneak cookies? I would.

answers.label: See in the dark
answers.reply: See in the dark! Never afraid of caves again. Golden carrots would be wasted on you.

answers.label: Neither, thanks
answers.reply: Neither? Happy as you are. That's the best answer of all.

ask: What's the best block in the whole world? I have strong opinions on this.

answers.label: Oak planks
answers.reply: Oak planks! Honest, warm and everywhere. A fine choice.

answers.label: Glass
answers.reply: Glass! You can see the world through it. Very clever.

answers.label: The bell
answers.reply: The bell! The heart of every village. You understand us.

answers.label: Hay bales
answers.reply: Hay bales! Soft to land on and pretty to look at. A playful pick.

ask: Which creature in the world do you like best?

answers.label: Axolotls
answers.reply: Axolotls! Pink and smiling. Everyone loves an axolotl.

answers.label: Foxes
answers.reply: Foxes! Clever little thieves. They steal our chickens, but I can't stay mad.

answers.label: Bees
answers.reply: Bees! Hard workers. Honey makers. Underrated.

answers.label: Villagers, of course
answers.reply: Villagers! Oh, you flatterer. We like you too.

ask: Do you think creepers are evil, or just misunderstood?

answers.label: Definitely evil
answers.reply: Evil! They blow up houses. I can't argue with that.

answers.label: Just misunderstood
answers.reply: Misunderstood. Maybe they just want a hug. A very loud, very final hug.

answers.label: They're lonely
answers.reply: Lonely. Oh, that's sad. Now I'll never look at one the same way.

ask: The wandering trader. Honest merchant or charming swindler?

answers.label: Honest merchant
answers.reply: Honest? You're kind. His prices say otherwise.

answers.label: Charming swindler
answers.reply: Charming swindler! Exactly. But I still buy his saplings every time.

answers.label: Mysterious wizard
answers.reply: A wizard! The invisibility potions make sense now.

ask: Why do you think the iron golem gives flowers to children?

answers.label: Because it's kind
answers.reply: Because it's kind. Simple and true. I believe that too.

answers.label: It wants friends
answers.reply: It wants friends. Oh. That makes my heart ache a little.

answers.label: It's a mystery
answers.reply: A mystery. Some things are better that way.

ask: Honestly now: is our bell too loud?

answers.label: Far too loud
answers.reply: Too loud! I knew it. I'm telling the cleric you agreed with me.

answers.label: Just right
answers.reply: Just right! A diplomatic answer. You'd make a good mayor.

answers.label: Ring it louder
answers.reply: Louder?! You're dangerous. I love it.

ask: Pumpkins or melons? The village is divided.

answers.label: Pumpkins
answers.reply: Pumpkins! Pies, lanterns and scarecrow heads. Versatile.

answers.label: Melons
answers.reply: Melons! Sweet, juicy and perfect on a hot day.

answers.label: Both are just round
answers.reply: Both are just round? Bold. Nobody's said that at a village meeting yet.

ask: If you found an emerald on the path, would you keep it or ask around?

answers.label: Ask around
answers.reply: Ask around. Honest! That's why people trust you here.

answers.label: Keep it
answers.reply: Keep it? Ha! Well, finders keepers, I suppose. Don't tell the baker.

answers.label: Give it to the bell
answers.reply: Give it to the bell? You mean leave it for whoever needs it. That's lovely.

ask: Last loaf of bread, two hungry people. What do you do?

answers.label: Share it
answers.reply: Share it. Of course. Half a loaf for two is better than a whole one for one.

answers.label: Give it away
answers.reply: Give it away entirely? You're too good. Eat something yourself sometimes.

answers.label: Bake more
answers.reply: Bake more! Practical. Problem solved for everyone.

ask: Storm's coming and the sheep are out. Save the sheep or your own house?

answers.label: The sheep
answers.reply: The sheep! They can't help themselves. The shepherd would kiss you.

answers.label: My house
answers.reply: Your house. Sensible. Sheep can swim. Probably.

answers.label: Call the neighbors
answers.reply: Call the neighbors and save both! That's how a village works.

ask: If a neighbor got turned into a zombie, would you try to cure them?

answers.label: Of course I would
answers.reply: Of course. A splash of weakness and a golden apple. I'm so glad you know.

answers.label: If I knew how
answers.reply: Weakness potion, then a golden apple. Now you know. Promise you'd try?

answers.label: Too dangerous
answers.reply: Too dangerous? I understand. But I hope someone would do it for me.

ask: If a friend told you a secret, would you ever tell anyone?

answers.label: Never
answers.reply: Never. Good. Then I know I can trust you.

answers.label: Only if it hurt them
answers.reply: Only to protect them. That's the right exception. You're wise.

answers.label: Depends on the gossip
answers.reply: Depends on the gossip? Ha! At least you're honest about it.

ask: If we renamed {village}, what would you call it?

answers.label: Keep the name
answers.reply: Keep it? Good. We've grown into it, like an old coat.

answers.label: Something with "bell"
answers.reply: Bellsworth? Bellmere? Ooh, I like that. I'll suggest it. Nobody will agree.

answers.label: Name it after me
answers.reply: After you?! Bold. ...{player}ville. It does have a ring to it.

ask: If we threw a festival, what should it celebrate?

answers.label: The harvest
answers.reply: The harvest! Pumpkins and pies and dancing. Perfect.

answers.label: The first snow
answers.reply: The first snow! Lanterns and hot cider. How lovely.

answers.label: The golem
answers.reply: The golem! A festival for our protector. We'd give it all the flowers.

answers.label: Nothing, just a party
answers.reply: Just a party! No reason needed. You understand village life perfectly.

ask: The village wants a mascot animal. What should it be?

answers.label: A cat
answers.reply: A cat! It keeps the creepers away. Practical and adorable.

answers.label: A goat
answers.reply: A goat! Loud, stubborn and climbs everything. Very like us.

answers.label: A chicken
answers.reply: A chicken! Humble, dependable, makes breakfast. Good choice.

answers.label: A llama
answers.reply: A llama! Spits at strangers. Excellent guard animal.

ask: What would your perfect day in {village} look like?

answers.label: Fishing, then a nap
answers.reply: Fishing and a nap! You'd fit right in with our fisherman.

answers.label: Market Day with friends
answers.reply: Market Day with friends. Honey cakes, gossip, music. Yes.

answers.label: Building something
answers.reply: Building something. Bring your tools; we'll find you a project.

answers.label: Talking with you
answers.reply: Talking with me? Oh, stop. ...Don't stop.

ask: Can I ask for some advice? What should I do when I'm feeling stuck?

answers.label: Take a walk
answers.reply: Take a walk. Yes. The answers are usually somewhere between here and the river.

answers.label: Talk to a friend
answers.reply: Talk to a friend. Like we're doing now. It's working already.

answers.label: Have a snack
answers.reply: Have a snack! Ha! Honestly, that fixes half my problems.

answers.label: Sleep on it
answers.reply: Sleep on it. Things look different in the morning. Usually better.

ask: When do you think {village} looks its prettiest?

answers.label: At sunrise
answers.reply: At sunrise! Everything gold and quiet. I agree.

answers.label: Lit up at night
answers.reply: At night, with every window lit. Like a little constellation.

answers.label: After the rain
answers.reply: After the rain, when everything sparkles. You notice the nice things.

answers.label: On Market Day
answers.reply: Market Day! Busy, colorful, alive.

ask: Enchanting or redstone? Which is the real magic?

answers.label: Enchanting
answers.reply: Enchanting! Glowing books and floating letters. The old magic.

answers.label: Redstone
answers.reply: Redstone! Clever little circuits. Magic you can understand, if you're clever.

answers.label: Bread rising
answers.reply: Bread rising! Ha! That's the real magic. The baker would agree.

ask: What's the best sound in the world, do you think?

answers.label: Rain on the roof
answers.reply: Rain on the roof. Yes. Cozy and safe.

answers.label: A cat purring
answers.reply: A cat purring! Nothing more peaceful.

answers.label: The village bell
answers.reply: The village bell. Calling everyone home. You're sentimental. I like that.

answers.label: Friends laughing
answers.reply: Friends laughing. The best sound there is.
